title: Bo Nix: We're not freaking out about being 0-1
summary: The Broncos opened the regular season with a dud against the Chiefs, but they're not making too much of one result as they prepare for Sunday's home opener against the Jaguars.
full_text: The Broncos opened the regular season with a dud against the Chiefs, but they're not making too much of one result as they prepare for Sunday's home opener against the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix threw an interception and lost one of his three fumbles in the 31-10 loss to a divisional rival. He was sacked four times in the game and the Broncos only had 176 total yards of offense, which is the kind of performance that might have some wondering if the offense somehow lost its way on the way into the regular season. On Thursday, Nix said that's not the case in Denver and that the team still believes they're built the right way for success. "Overall, we're not going to press the panic button and we're not freaking out ," Nix said, via the team's website. "We're not starting from scratch or anything. We feel like we're still in a good spot, we just didn't play great by any means, and we've got to play better." The Jaguars are coming off a more impressive start, although a home win over the Browns is certainly a different degree of difficulty than a Monday night trip to Arrowhead Stadium. Jacksonville won in Denver last season as well, so the Broncos will have to be much sharper if they're going to avoid a week of listening to stats about how few teams go from 0-2 to making it to the playoffs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalen Carter to wear a cast on his wrist against the Titans
summary: Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter returned to practice on Thursday with a new look.
full_text: Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter returned to practice on Thursday with a new look. Carter missed Wednesday's practice with a wrist injury and returned to the field wearing a cast on his right wrist. After practice, Carter declined to delve into the details of his injury while telling reporters that he's planning to play against the Titans with the cast on as protection. “I look fine out there wearing it ," Carter said. "Just minor adjustments and I’m still out there practicing and ready to play. . . . I'm still going to have to strike, grab and play the run and pass rush. That's pretty much it. I can't let it affect me." Carter said he suffered the injury while trying to punch the ball out late in last Sunday's win over the Commanders, but he doesn't plan on letting it interfere too much with the Eagles' bid for a 2-0 start to the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Allen: Very fortunate to be the QB to open this stadium
summary: Josh Allen had a lot of big games in the old Highmark Stadium, but it's hard to top the one he came up with for the first game in the new one.
full_text: Josh Allen had a lot of big games in the old Highmark Stadium, but it's hard to top the one he came up with for the first game in the new one. Allen opened the game with a one-yard touchdown run and then went on to throw three scores while running for another one in a 41-31 win that pushed the Bills to 2-0 on the season. He now has four games with at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing scores in his career and he's the first quarterback with five passing touchdowns and four rushing scores through the first two games of a season. Those would be special results under any circumstances, but they hit even harder in the first game on a new field. Allen said after the game that being in the spotlight in the new stadium meant something extra to him. "I think at the national anthem, I caught myself like taking it all in and understanding my job is the coolest thing in the world ," Allen said, via the team's website. "It's everything that I've ever wanted to be the quarterback of an NFL franchise. And I'm just very fortunate that I ended up here in Buffalo and got to be the first quarterback to open this stadium. It's a special spot." No one is calling the new Highmark Stadium "The House that Josh Allen Built" at the moment, but there's little doubt that he'll be the center of attention in every game he plays in the building and they just might come up with a way to name it after him if he can cap off the first season in its history with the first Super Bowl title in franchise history.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Brady: I wanted to take the ball in that environment and set the tone
summary: Many teams choose to defer to the second half after winning the coin toss before games, but Bills head coach Joe Brady did not do that on Thursday night.
full_text: Many teams choose to defer to the second half after winning the coin toss before games, but Bills head coach Joe Brady did not do that on Thursday night. Brady elected to take the ball to start the first game at his team's new stadium and that turned out to be a wise move. Running back James Cook ran three times for 23 yards while quarterback Josh Allen completed two passes for 22 yards and ran four times for 40 yards, including a one-yard touchdown to set off a frenzied celebration in the team's new home. "I've said all along, it was important for us, and I wanted to take the ball in this environment and set the tone ," Brady said, via WGR. "I thought we had some good third downs, we finished in the end zone, and that stadium was electric. That was the start that we needed." Brady was remembering another drive involving third downs because the Bills never faced one on that trip to the end zone, but that's understandable because his team had six touchdown drives over the course of the 41-31 win. All of that success can run together, especially when it plays out to a soundtrack of joyful Bills fans celebrating a memorable night in franchise history.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay: Myles Garrett is like Wolverine, healing fast, but we won't rush him back
summary: "I'm reluctant to put a timeline on it. We know that he's going to miss those four weeks at a minimum," McVay said.
full_text: Rams coach Sean McVay says defensive end Myles Garrett's knee surgery was successful, but it's too soon to tell when Garrett will be back on the field. "It went good, he's feeling good, you already see he had crutches yesterday and then he was walking without crutches today. He's like Wolverine, healing fast," McVay said. That doesn't necessarily mean Garrett will be back on the field on October 18 for the Rams' Week 6 game against the Cardinals, which is the earliest he's eligible to return from injured reserve. "I'm reluctant to put a timeline on it," McVay said. "We know that he's going to miss those four weeks at a minimum. We're not going to rush him back. We want to make sure he's feeling good, he's able to get on the practice field, do all the things that are necessary for him to perform at a level that he's been accustomed to. I'll keep you guys posted as we have updates, as we go." Garrett did next to nothing in the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers and can't play for the next four weeks, so the Rams will be about one-third of the way through the season before they get any meaningful contributions for him. That wasn't the plan when they traded for him, but the Rams' top priority is having him ready late in the season and in the playoffs, and McVay sounds confident that will happen.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Campbell: It's a long season, Lions need to get better
summary: "They got after us, and we didn't play good enough, and we didn't coach good enough. That falls on me," Campbell said.
full_text: Lions head coach Dan Campbell saw a lot that his team needs to improve in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Bills. "We've got a lot of room to grow, and that's encouraging," Campbell said. "We've just got to clean up a lot of things on defense right now, particularly in the back end. . . . It wasn't good enough." Campbell expressed optimism about the way the Lions can use their extra three days after playing on Thursday night to prepare for Week 3 against the Jets. "It's early, we're in Week 2, we've got a long season, and the most important thing is that we get better," Campbell said. "We just need to get better than we were today in all three phases. We need to play better against the Jets, and I think we will. We can, and we certainly will." Campbell credited Bills head coach Joe Brady for having his team ready to play. "They got after us and we didn't play good enough and we didn't coach good enough. That falls on me," Campbell said. "It certainly needed to be a lot cleaner than that."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Thursday Night Football: Josh Allen accounts for five TDs in Bills' 41-31 win over Lions
summary: The Bills quarterback threw three touchdowns and ran for two.
full_text: Josh Allen made the first regular-season game in Highmark Stadium memorable for Bills fans. The quarterback threw three touchdown passes and ran for two in a dominant 41-31 win over the Lions. The Bills improved to 2-0, while the Lions fell to 1-1. Allen now has four career games with three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns. No other player in NFL history has more than two (Kordell Stewart), according to NFL Researcher. Allen completed 20 of 31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns. His scoring tosses went for 43 yards to Josh Palmer, 1 yard to Dawson Knox and 16 yards to Dalton Kincaid. Palmer has two catches for 77 yards and two touchdowns this season, having caught the game-winning touchdown in the win over the Texans on Sunday. Kincaid caught seven passes for a team-leading 95 yards. The Bills lost wide receiver DJ Moore to a shoulder injury and a stinger in the first half. Allen also ran for 69 yards and two touchdowns on 14 carries, topped only by James Cook's 21 carries for 135 yards. Cook scored the team's last touchdown on a 1-yard run with 2:50 left to seal it. The Bills outgained the Lions 446 to 355, were 5-for-5 in the red zone and went 9-of-12 on third down. Buffalo scored touchdowns on its first four possessions and punted only twice all night. The Lions, who blew a 21-0 lead to the Saints last week before winning in overtime, fell behind 21-0 and trailed 27-10 at halftime. They twice pulled to within 10 points when the game was still in reach, but Allen and the Bills answered twice. Detroit's last touchdown, which pulled it to within 10 again, came with 1:42 left as as Amon-Ra St. Brown scored his second touchdown. The Bills, though, recovered the onside kick. Lions quarterback Jared Goff was 26-of-38 for 327 yards and four touchdowns after a slow start. Goff reached 40,000 yards in his 153rd game, the sixth-fastest for any quarterback. St. Brown caught nine passes for 142 yards and two touchdowns, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs had 16 carries for 52 yards and caught six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, who had two sacks and two forced fumbles in the season-opening win over the Texans on Sunday, had two sacks and a forced fumble against the Lions.
author: Charean Williams

title: Roger Goodell: Europe is the most likely destination for a franchise
summary: Last month, Commissioner Roger Goodell said he has "no doubt" that the NFL will have a team headquartered outside the United States.
full_text: Last month, Commissioner Roger Goodell said he has " no doubt " that the NFL will have a team headquartered outside the United States. Appearing on Prime Video's pregame show before Lions-Bills on Thursday night, Goodell was asked how soon it will happen and where the team would be located. "You know, that's tough to say," Goodell said. "I think if we continue to grow and continue to get the kind of reaction, I do think a franchise will be international at some point in time. I think Europe is the most likely, for a lot of reasons. One, the length of time we've been playing there. But also the scheduling is going to be a lot easier. Australia might create a few complications for us. But I also believe we could have more than one team. . . . The support is there." It would make sense to have two teams, especially if the first destination is London, which has two NFL-ready stadiums. The lingering question is whether current teams would move, or whether the league would expand. Goodell has in the past hinted at a four-team European division. The best long-term vision could be four teams in Europe and four teams elsewhere (Brazil, Mexico, Australia, and Japan). Much of that hinges on the return of supersonic flight, a development the NFL is closely monitoring. Yes, the league has been dangling the carrot of an international team for years. Often, it's about driving interest in the variety-pack of games played in other countries. At this point, it does indeed feel as if it's coming, eventually.
author: Mike Florio

title: Emmitt Smith thinks Derrick Henry can break all-time rushing record
summary: Derrick Henry, at age 32, is playing like he did at age 22.
full_text: '' Derrick Henry, at age 32, is playing like he did at age 22. And he's in position to make a climb up the all-time rushing list. With 13,163 career yards, could Henry get all the way to the top? The guy who holds the No. 1 spot — Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith — believes he can. "Oh yeah, I think it’s possible ," Smith said recently, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "Derrick Henry is a bigger back. He takes great care of his body. He's in great shape." Smith has said he hopes someone breaks the record in his lifetime. He wishes Walter Payton had still been alive when Smith broke the prior record of 16,726 yards. Currently, Henry trails Smith by 5,193 yards. To get to 18,355, Henry will need to keep rolling for at least four more seasons beyond 2026. That's 84 more games. At an average of 61.8 yards per game, he'll get there. While Father Time remains undefeated, Henry has been defying it. If he wants to keep going, and if his body holds up, he could get there. For now, he's only 97 yards behind Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson. With another 403, he'll catch Hall of Famer Jerome Bettis. With 22 more, he'll match Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson. And with 417, he'll tie Hall of Famer Curtis Martin. In all, Henry is 940 yards away from leapfrogging Dickerson, Bettis, Tomlinson, and Martin. Each of whom are in Canton. Henry will surely get there, too. Especially if he keeps working his way to the top of the all-time rushing list.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay hopes the Rams never play in Australia again
summary: One week ago, the Rams made their debut in Australia.
full_text: '' One week ago, the Rams made their debut in Australia. It didn't go well; the 49ers drubbed the Rams, 27-7. For that reason, coach Sean McVay hopes the assignment doesn't come their way again. “It's almost like you try to do the Men in Black thing where you say, ‘Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago,’" McVay told reporters on Thursday. "We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context." The atmosphere was great. The burden on the teams was not. The strategy of showing up the day before the game ended up being a miscalculation. Either way, the Rams have 16 games to play. Starting with a visit from the Giants on Monday night. "Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let's go be about it," McVay said. "Let's go prepare the right way. Let's have great focus and concentration. Let's have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let's go be ready to go against a really damn good football team. What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That's what every week is. We're excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today." It remains to be seen whether the two long flights with a football game as the Vegemite in the sandwich will affect the Rams in Week 2, or beyond. Either way, an up-and-coming Giants team is coming to town — and thousands of Giants fans in the L.A. area are surely scrambling to buy tickets for the prime-time game at SoFi Stadium.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jadarian Price will get more reps moving forward
summary: In his Week 1 debut, running back Jadarian Price was on the field for only 24 snaps — less than half of the Seahawks' total offensive workload.
full_text: In his Week 1 debut, running back Jadarian Price was on the field for only 24 snaps — less than half of the Seahawks' total offensive workload. That will be changing. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury told reporters on Thursday that Price will be getting more playing time moving forward. "We were very deliberate about the reps that he was going to get, and how he was going to be used," Fleury said. "He didn't play in the preseason. It was the very first NFL game, huge stage. We wanted to be cautious in terms of his workload. He earned more reps moving forward, and we'll continue to bring him along and develop him the right way.” Fleury explained that the limited use of Price had nothing to do with "anything physical." Said Fleury, "It’s just being a rookie.” With Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III gone in free agency and Zach Charbonnet out for at least the first four games as he continues to recover from an ACL tear suffered in the divisional-round win over the 49ers, Price is the top tailback. With his 24 reps in the season opener, Price had 10 carries for 52 yards and two catches for six yards. The next opportunity comes in Arizona on Sunday, against the 1-0 Cardinals.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Allen registers 10th game with 2+ rushing, 2+ passing touchdowns
summary: Steve Young is second on the all-time list, with four.
full_text: Josh Allen is a touchdown machine. For the 10th time in his career, he has scored two or more rushing touchdowns and two or more passing touchdowns in the same game. His latest score came on the ground from two yards out, extending Buffalo's lead over the Lions to 34-17. Allen holds the record by a wide margin. In second place on the all-time two-and-two list is Hall of Famer Steve Young. He did it four times. For the season, Allen has already accounted for nine touchdowns. Barring a collapse, the Bills will move to 2-0 on the year, with a proper christening of their new stadium.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills rule out WR DJ Moore
summary: Bills wide receiver DJ Moore will not return tonight.
full_text: '' Bills wide receiver DJ Moore will not return tonight. With extra time until their next game, the Bills will have to hope 10 days is long enough for Moore to heal. Moore was injured with 2:56 remaining in the first half when he dove in the end zone for a pass from Josh Allen. The pass was incomplete, and Moore landed on his shoulder before Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin landed on top of him. Moore is out with a shoulder injury and a stinger. The Bills lead the Lions 34-17 after Josh Allen's 2-yard touchdown run with 1:07 remaining in the third quarter. Allen has run for two touchdowns and thrown three others.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions score on first drive of second half to close to within 27-17
summary: The Lions aren't dead yet.
full_text: The Lions aren't dead yet. Detroit opened the second half with an 11-play, 74-yard touchdown drive, and now trail the Bills 27-17. The Lions were down 21-0 before Jared Goff hit Jahmyr Gibbs for an 11-yard touchdown. Jake Bates kicked a 31-yard field goal on the last play of the first half, and Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 2-yard touchdown with 9:29 left in the third quarter. Goff is 18-of-24 for 198 yards and two touchdowns. He has thrown a touchdown in 25 consecutive games. St. Brown has six catches for 70 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Josh Allen, Bills running over Lions, up 27-10 at halftime
summary: The Bills quarterback has thrown three touchdowns and run for another.
full_text: '' The Bills have christened their new stadium with champagne and caviar on the field. Josh Allen threw three touchdowns in the first half and ran for another, and the Bills are in the locker room at halftime with a 27-10 lead. Almost everything went right for the Bills in the first half other than Tyler Bass missing an extra point, punting on their fourth possession and injuries to wide receivers DJ Moore and Keon Coleman. Moore is in the X-ray room being examined for a shoulder injury and a stinger, and Coleman returned after getting his right ankle taped on the sideline. The Bills have outgained the Lions 299 to 155, scoring touchdowns on their first four possessions on drives of 85, 79, 57 and 68 yards. Allen is 12-of-19 for 164 yards with three touchdowns on throws of 43 yards to Josh Palmer, 1 yard to Dawson Knox and 16 yards to Dalton Kincaid, The quarterback also has four carries for 40 yards and a touchdown. James Cook already has 100 yards, rushing for 101 on 11 carries. Kincaid has five catches for 65 yards. Jared Goff kept his streak of consecutive games with a touchdown alive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to running back Jahmyr Gibbs. It was the 25th game in a row Goff has thrown a TD pass. But it came with the Lions down 21-0. Goff is 11-of-16 for 128 yards and a touchdown. He's been sacked three times, including twice by Greg Rousseau, who is off to a great start this season. Gibbs has rushed for 47 yards on eight carries and has caught four passes for 40 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills WR DJ Moore questionable to return after injuring shoulder
summary: Moore was injured while diving in the end zone late in the second quarter.
full_text: Bills wide receiver DJ Moore was injured while diving for a Josh Allen pass in the end zone. Moore is in the X-ray room for further evaluation after coming down hard on his left shoulder and then having Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin land on top of him. The Bills list Moore as questionable to return with a shoulder injury and a possible stinger, according to Prime sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung. The Bills scored on the next play, as Josh Allen connected with tight end Dalton Kincaid for a 16-yard touchdown. Tyler Bass missed the extra point wide left. The Bills lead 27-7 with 2:52 remaining in the second quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions on the board, trail 21-7
summary: It took long enough for Detroit to show up.
full_text: It took long enough for Detroit to show up. The Lions dug a huge hole they might not climb out of tonight, but they kept the dirt from being shoveled over them for now. Detroit, which had seven plays for minus-1 yard on its first two possessions, drove 70 yards in 12 plays for a touchdown. The Lions trail 21-7 after Jahmyr Gibbs' 11-yard touchdown reception from Jared Goff and the extra point by Jake Bates. Goff now has a touchdown pass in 25 consecutive games. He is 6-of-7 for 57 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Korn Ferry tries to keep key document in Brian Flores case under seal
summary: The Brian Flores litigation has uncovered a potentially significant document through a subpoena issued to the Korn Ferry search firm.
full_text: The Brian Flores litigation has uncovered a potentially significant document through a subpoena issued to the Korn Ferry search firm. And Korn Ferry is trying to keep the document out of public view. The document has been designated as confidential under a general protective order that allows the parties to claim that certain materials should not be disclosed. Flores's lawyers have challenged the effort to keep it secret. Via Daniel Kaplan, Korn Ferry filed paperwork on Thursday in support of the effort to keep the document under seal. Korn Ferry argues, among other things, that “whether the limited information from Exhibit A that Korn Ferry requests remain sealed is purportedly `discriminatory’ or `retaliatory,’ such that it supports and is relevant to Plaintiff’s claims in the Supplemental Complaint, has no bearing on whether Korn Ferry is legally entitled to have Exhibit A remain under seal.” This statement suggests, as Kaplan notes, that Flores's lawyers have argued that the document helps prove that he was the victim of discrimination and/or retaliation. The document in question, which one source called "insane," was generated by Korn Ferry in connection with a coaching search conducted by the Raiders. The precise Raiders coaching search isn’t specified; the Raiders have hired new coaches in 2026, 2025, 2024, 2022, and 2018. If the document shows potential retaliation, it means that it came from a coaching search after the filing of Flores's lawsuit, on February 1, 2022 . Because the Raiders hired Josh McDaniels on January 31, 2022 , it would limit the potential application of the document to the search that resulted in the hiring of Antonio Pierce in 2024, Pete Carroll in 2025, or Klint Kubiak in 2026. Two of those searches happened after Tom Brady — who played for the Patriots when Flores served on the coaching staff there — became a minority owner of the team. Regardless of whether the document comes to light in the short term, it'll definitely be disclosed and discussed if/when the case goes to trial. If the document is truly bad for the NFL and the various teams that have been sued, it could result in the case being settled before the document ever comes to light.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rout is on in Buffalo as Bills take 21-0 lead
summary: Josh Allen has run for a touchdown and thrown for two on three possessions for the Bills.
full_text: The Bills are having a grand ol' time in their new stadium. Buffalo has scored three touchdowns on three possessions in the new Highmark Stadium, taking a 21-0 lead over the Lions. The Bills have outgained the Lions 209 to 10, with three possessions to two. Josh Allen threw his second touchdown, finding Dawson Knox for a 1-yard score. The quarterback had his choice whether to run it in or throw it to Knox. He took care of his tight end. Allen scored on a 1-yard run on the Bills' first possession and threw a 43-yard touchdown pass to Josh Palmer on the second. As if things weren't bad enough for the Lions, defensive back Avonte Maddox was carted off the field in the second quarter. The team lists him as questionable to return with a foot injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams officially place Myles Garrett on injured reserve
summary: The Rams have made one of their expected roster moves official on Thursday.
full_text: The Rams have made one of their expected roster moves official on Thursday. Myles Garrett has been placed on injured reserve, Los Angeles announced. It was reported on Sunday that Garrett would have knee surgery and be placed on IR after an ineffective performance to start the season in the loss to the 49ers. Head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that the team had believed that Garrett's knee injury was something he could work through. Now, Garrett is officially out for at least the next four weeks. The Rams did not announce a corresponding move, leaving a roster spot open. The Rams will host the Giants on Monday night.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Josh Palmer scores his second TD of the season on his second catch
summary: Josh Palmer has only two catches this season.
full_text: Josh Palmer has only two catches this season. He also has 77 yards and two touchdowns. Four days after catching the 34-yard game-winner against the Texans, the Bills wide receiver caught a 43-yard touchdown from Josh Allen with 3:42 remaining in the first quarter Thursday. The Bills went 79 yards in eight plays. The Bills, who have had two possessions to the Lions' one, have outgained Detroit 159 to minus-5 and lead 14-0. Josh Allen scored the team's first touchdown on a 1-yard run. He threw the second. Allen is 5-of-7 for 97 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Hall of Fame announces its new group of voters
summary: The recent overhaul of the Hall of Fame selection process includes a dramatic reduction in the number of voters, from 50 down to 28.
full_text: The recent overhaul of the Hall of Fame selection process includes a dramatic reduction in the number of voters, from 50 down to 28. On Thursday, the Hall of Fame announced the new group of voters. They are: Hall of Famer Jared Allen, Howard Balzer of USA Today , Jarrett Bell of USA Today , Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press , Vic Carucci of WGRZ-TV, Mike Chappell of CBS4/Fox59, Pete Dougherty of the Green Bay Press-Gazette , Jeff Duncan of the New Orleans Times-Picayune , Hall of Famer Dan Fouts, Scott Garceau of WMAR-TV, Bob Glauber, Vahe Gregorian of the Kansas City Star , Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic , Lindsay Jones of The Ringer , Ira Kaufman of JoeBucsFan.com, Ross Ketover of NFL Films, Sam Kouvaris, Jeff Legwold of ESPN, Rob Maadi of the Associated Press, Gary Myers, Sal Paolantonio of ESPN, Dan Pompei of The Athletic , Mike Sando of The Athletic , Hall of Famer Will Shields, Jim Trotter, Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News , Eric Williams of Fox Sports, and Charean Williams of PFT. There's no apparent rhyme or reason regarding the decisions made to keep and to cut loose members from the former panel of 50. If anything, fewer voters can create more problems because it takes a smaller group to screw things up. But it wouldn't be the first time that the nameless, faceless folks who control the Hall of Fame screwed something up. It would simply be the latest.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills take 7-0 lead on Josh Allen's 1-yard run
summary: The Bills started Thursday night's game with a holding penalty on the opening kickoff.
full_text: The Bills started Thursday night's game with a holding penalty on the opening kickoff. On the third play from scrimmage, Aidan Hutchinson had a strip-sack of Josh Allen that offensive lineman Spencer Brown recovered. Six plays later, the Bills were in the end zone with a 7-0 lead. Buffalo went 85 yards in 10 plays, with Allen scoring on a 1-yard run. It was the first regular-season touchdown in Highmark Stadium. Allen was 2-for-2 for 22 yards, completing both to Khalil Shakir. He also had four carries for 40 yards. James Cook had three carries for 23 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean McVay "hopeful" Aaron Donald will play this week
summary: The Giants expect Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald to play on Monday night.
full_text: The Giants expect Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald to play on Monday night. Rams coach Sean McVay is "hopeful." McVay said before practice that Donald would fully participate on Thursday, and indeed, Donald is not on the team's injury report. (Donald's roster exemption was lifted Friday.) Donald did not travel to Australia with the team, staying at home to continue working his way back from a two-year absence from football. He participated in individual drills for the first time on Aug. 30 and joined team drills on Sept. 6. McVay said the Rams are not looking for specific benchmarks to determine whether Donald plays for the first time since 2023. "It's more along the line of how does he feel ?" McVay said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN. Donald is "obviously champing at the bit" to play, but the Rams' travel schedule to Australia has prevented limited practice opportunities for Donald. "But what we are hopeful is, is that we'll have some good work today and tomorrow and then hopefully he's feeling good enough and if he says he's ready to go, then we'll be excited to see him," McVay said. Rams defensive end Myles Garrett is "feeling good" after knee surgery on Monday, but the reigning Defensive Player of the Year has no timeline for his return. Garrett was on crutches on Wednesday and walking without them Thursday. Because Garrett is on injured reserve, he will miss at least the next four games. "We're not going to rush him back," McVay said. "We want to make sure that he's feeling good, he's able to get out on the practice field, do all the things that are necessary for him to perform at a level that he's been accustomed to."
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Bills DL Ed Oliver won't play after injuring hip in pregame
summary: Lions cornerback D.J. Reed, who was questionable with a foot injury, is active.
full_text: The Bills will be without a key piece of their defense for Thursday Night Football against the Lions. Buffalo has ruled out defensive lineman Ed Oliver after he injured his hip in pregame wramups. He is inactive for the game. Oliver was not on the injury report this week. The Bills' other inactives are running back Ty Johnson (hamstring), wide receiver Skyler Bell, offensive tackle Jude Bowry, offensive guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams, defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (knee/illness) and safety Jalon Kilgore. Bills safety Cole Bishop is active after being listed as questionable with knee and groin issues. The Lions' inactives are offensive tackle Blake Miller (knee), offensive guard Christian Mahogany (hip), cornerback Keith Abney II, cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr., linebacker Jimmy Rolder, defensive lineman Mekhi Wingo and edge rusher Ahmed Hassanein. Cornerback D.J. Reed, who was questionable with a foot injury, is active.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joe Burrow has another limited practice
summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow's practice status didn't change on Thursday.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow's practice status didn't change on Thursday. Burrow remained a limited participant as the team heads into Sunday's game against the Texans. Burrow is dealing with back tightness, but said on Wednesday that it was " ridiculous " to think that it could cause him to sit out in Houston. Defensive end Shemar Stewart (knee) was listed as a full participant for the second straight day. Stewart did not play in last Sunday's win over the Buccaneers. Defensive tackle B.J. Hill (rest, Achilles) was limited while running back Samaje Perine (knee) and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen (rest) did not practice. Perine was a new addition to the injury report on Thursday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Alvin Kamara says he's going to play on Sunday
summary: Saints running back Alvin Kamara plans to make his 2026 debut on Sunday.
full_text: '' Saints running back Alvin Kamara plans to make his 2026 debut on Sunday. Kamara missed the opener while he continued to recover from a knee sprain he suffered this summer, but has been a full participant in practice both days this week and he said on Thursday that he will be in the lineup against the Ravens. "I'm going," Kamara said, via the team's website. "If it wasn't right, I wouldn't be in. I feel great, moving well, really no limitations . I feel good." The Saints signed Travis Etienne this offseason and he had nine carries for 46 yards against the Lions last weekend. Kendre Miller also got nine carries and Kamara said he's ready for whatever role the team has in mind for his return. "You really never know when your number is going to be called ," Kamara said. "I feel the same as if I'm leading or not, that's more for the coaches to figure out. My job is to be ready, so I'll be ready." Official word from the Saints on Kamara's status will come on Friday. The team will also share any injury designations for wide receiver Chris Olave, defensive end Cam Jordan, and defensive end Chase Young after they were limited in Thursday's practice.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brock Bowers misses practice again on Thursday
summary: The Raiders practiced without tight end Brock Bowers again on Thursday.
full_text: '' The Raiders practiced without tight end Brock Bowers again on Thursday. Bowers has not practiced since having surgery on his meniscus last week. Head coach Klint Kubiak said earlier this week that he hoped Bowers would be able to return to practice, so Friday will be the last chance for that to happen before the Raiders face the Chargers. Michael Mayer would be the team's top tight end if Bowers remains out. He had six catches for 32 yards in last Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Cornerback Darien Porter (foot) was also out of practice for the second straight day and quarterback Aidan O'Connell missed practice for personal reasons. Running back Ashton Jeanty (ankle) was listed as a full participant.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kyler Murray remained limited in Thursday's practice.
summary: Carson Wentz is set to start for the Vikings if Murray does not clear the concussion protocol.
full_text: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was back on the practice field Thursday. Murray was knocked out of last Sunday's win over the Packers in the first quarter with a concussion and he had made enough progress in his recovery to practice on a limited basis Wednesday. Murray got in another limited session on Thursday and the next update on where he stands in the concussion protocol will come on Friday. If Murray is not cleared in time to face the Bears, Carson Wentz is in line to start. Wentz was 12-of-19 for 133 yards and three touchdowns after taking over for Murray in Week 1. Wide receiver Jauan Jennings (personal) and right tackle Brian O'Neill (knee) did not practice. O'Neill was limited on Wednesday while Jennings has not practiced this week. Linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) was limited for the second straight day and linebacker Blake Cashman (wrist) moved up to full participation.

title: Judge declines to sign order sealing Josh Jacobs video, on procedural grounds
summary: A week after the judge presiding over the criminal case involving Packers running back Josh Jacobs signed an order temporarily sealing the evidence (including a video of the altercation that prompted a misdemeanor battery charge), the judge declined to sign an order that would have sealed the evidence permanently.
full_text: A week after the judge presiding over the criminal case involving Packers running back Josh Jacobs signed an order temporarily sealing the evidence (including a video of the altercation that prompted a misdemeanor battery charge), the judge declined to sign an order that would have sealed the evidence permanently. Via Fox 11, the judge rejected a proposed order on procedural grounds, concluding it was in an " improper format ." A hearing on the issue has been set for next Thursday. At that point, the judge could decide to grant the request, made by the victim's lawyer, to permanently seal the evidence. The NFL wants to see the video, as part of the effort to determine the proper discipline to be imposed on Jacobs under the Personal Conduct Policy. The league's inability to get access to the video underscores the flaws in its in-house justice system. The NFL doesn't have the power that a court of law possesses. It can't compel witnesses to cooperate. It can't subpoena records. It possibly will be stymied by a court order blocking access to important evidence. The league should nevertheless attempt to secure the ability to review the video, subject to the requirement of a protective order. It's possible to balance the victim's privacy rights with the NFL's desire to ensure that it has the ability to effectively and accurately assess a proper penalty on Jacobs. Jacobs remains on paid leave while the NFL considers the proper suspension to be imposed.

title: Lions' loss to Bills has panic level high after another poor performance by defense
summary: Detroit has yielded 30 and 41 points in back-to-back games
full_text:
Unless something drastically changes, the Detroit Lions will join another notable NFL team whose Super Bowl hopes were dashed by a woefully underperforming defense.
In 2000, the Rams boasted the NFL's best offense, but their toothless defense resulted in an early playoff exit. This year's Lions could suffer an even worse outcome. Their defense prevented them from making the playoffs in 2025, and that could very well happen again in 2026.
The issues started last week in New Orleans. After building a 21-0 lead, Detroit's defense was torched by Saints quarterback Tyler Shough , who threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns. The Lions prevailed in overtime, but the writing was on the wall.
Turnovers are a bad defense's best friend. That was the case in Week 1 as the Lions managed to force three turnovers of Shough. They were also able to sack him five times.
But Week 2 was a very different story. Allen was protected well, and he didn't commit a single turnover. More so, Allen ran circles around a Lions defense that simply had no answers him.
The Lions' defense couldn't contain Allen on the ground (he ran for 69 yards and two touchdowns on 14 carries) or in the air. Even more alarming was the lack of defenders around Allen's receivers. The biggest example of this was Josh Palmer's 43-yard touchdown catch that gave the Bills a 14-0 lead.
Josh Allen goes deep to a WIDE OPEN Josh Palmer for SIX DETvsBUF on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hle75KIFVt
We haven't even talked about James Cook III , who gashed Detroit for 135 yards and a score on 21 carries. Cook spent the night looking like Bo Jackson in Techno Bowl.
James Cookin' for 35 yards DETvsBUF – on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rNtH0sn6vo
To be fair, the Lions faced one of the league's best offense and arguably its best player in Allen, who is making a very early case for league MVP. But even when you consider the opponent, the fact that they were out-played that badly, it raises serious concerns about this team's ability to make the playoffs, let along compete for a Super Bowl.
Detroit has good defensive players. Aidan Hutchinson (who had one of Detroit's two sacks of Allen) is one of the NFL's premier pass rushers. Jack Campbell has become one of the league's most productive inside linebackers. The Lions just simply don't have enough good players on that side of the ball, though. Until they do, they are not going to be a legitimate threat to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl five months from now.
If Lions GM Brad Holmes wants to change that, he needs to work the phones in an effort to acquire someone -- anyone -- who can help his defense before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. His first call should be to Steelers GM Omar Khan about cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , who continues to be mired in a contract dispute.
There are reports that the Steelers' asking price for Porter is scaring teams off. Holmes, however, should give Khan whatever he wants -- within reason -- for Porter, a talented player who is just entering his prime. Holmes owes that to his defense, his talented offense, and most especially, to the Lions' long-suffering fan base who deserves to be rewarded for its decades of loyalty.

title: NFL Week 2 picks: Our experts face off on Giants at Rams, Bengals vs. Texans and more

full_text:
They say Week 1 is a liar, so who lied in their season opener? Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL , we watched Drake Maye and Jordan Love lose to backup quarterbacks, and the Los Angeles Rams aren't the super team some envisioned. This weekend, the new-look Cincinnati Bengals defense will get its shot at C.J. Stroud , the Broncos will look to get back on track with another AFC contender in the Jacksonville Jaguars , while the Kansas City Chiefs and Indianapolis Colts face off on "Sunday Night Football." For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 15 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.

The Patriots have had extra time to mull over their embarrassing loss to Drew Lock in the season opener, but with the point-spread being 4.5 points in a game where I'm expecting like 30 total points, I'm going to lean towards the underdog. Especially with A.J. Brown sidelined by a high ankle sprain. Believe it or not, the Steelers have won THREE STRAIGHT GAMES as an underdog of at least four points! I'll take Pittsburgh to keep it close. … Prediction: Patriots 16, Steelers 13

The Seahawks ' defense totally shut down everything that Drake Maye and the rest of the offense wanted to do, and it got ugly in the fourth quarter in particular. The Steelers, meanwhile, shut down everything the Falcons offense wanted to do on Sunday. But Maye is not Cooper Rush , and the Patriots are not the Falcons. This should be a relatively low-scoring game, but I still trust New England's offense a lot more than Pittsburgh's, and that should be enough to take home the win. … Prediction: Patriots 21, Steelers 13
Dajani ( Saints +7.5): The Baltimore Ravens were one of the big winners from Week 1. They eviscerated the Colts, 41-23, while racking up 500 yards of total offense. Derrick Henry ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns, while Zay Flowers registered a career-high 150 yards receiving and a touchdown ... in the first half. However, I would say that the Saints were one of the biggest "winner losers" from Week 1. I actually like that term. "Winner losers."
I was wildly impressed by Tyler Shough , who threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns to go with three turnovers vs. the Lions. It looked like he was flailing at the beginning of the second half with two straight turnovers, but the second-year signal-caller hung in there, relied on his playmakers like Chris Olave , and helped New Orleans overcome a 21-0 deficit on the road to get to overtime. It was remarkable. Dude is tough mentally and physically.
I'm going to take the Saints to cover the big number because Baltimore could be without two of its top wideouts in Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist). Plus, Shough is 8-2 ATS in his career as the starting quarterback. That's tied for the best mark since 1970. A gambler's dream QB! … Prediction: Ravens 28, Saints 24

Before Zay Flowers went out after aggravating his hamstring injury, Declan Doyle's group looked essentially unstoppable with Lamar Jackson targeting Flowers and Derrick Henry rushing through gaping holes in the line. The defense also limited the Colts to just 4.7 yards per play. It was a terrific debut. The only reason I'm taking the Saints here is the question about Flowers' availability, and the potential for New Orleans to secure a back-door cover in comeback mode, like it did against Detroit last week. … Prediction: Ravens 27, Saints 20
Dajani ( Texans -2.5): One of the games of the week. I found such joy in watching the Bengals' defense force three fumbles on the Bucs' first four possessions. The fans in the stands must have been crying tears of joy. Still, this was a competitive matchup that came down to the wire. As for the Texans, no one expected that defense to allow 36 points and for Josh Allen to register the first 300-yard passing game vs. Houston since 2024. If that's a sign of things to come, then the Bengals are winning this game. But I think DeMeco Ryans is going to have this defense ready to roll and rebound in their second straight home game. … Prediction: Texans 27, Bengals 23
Dubin (Texans -2.5): Houston lost a heartbreaker at home to Buffalo last week and now faces another explosive offense in a Cincinnati group that scored a lot but didn't necessarily even look its best in Week 1. Dajani (Jaguars +3): I'm sorry, but how am I supposed to feel confident laying points with the team that looked like the worst in the NFL last week? Yes, even worse than the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans . The Broncos were a nightmare of epic proportions in Kansas City on Monday night. Davis Webb couldn't get Bo Nix into a rhythm at all, Jaylen Waddle caught one pass for 2 yards and this vaunted defense registered a missed tackle rate of 29.8%. Absurd.
I know Week 1 is a liar and I expect the Broncos to be better than what we saw on Monday night, but this Jaguars team is for real. Denver knows that, as Trevor Lawrence came to Mile High and dropped 34 points on the Broncos in Week 16 last year to end Denver's 11-game win streak. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Broncos 23
Dubin (Push): Jacksonville looked just about as impressive as possible in its beatdown of the Browns in Week 1, while Denver looked like a two-way disaster in its blowout loss to the Chiefs. Predicting such a stark reversal feels wrong, but I felt really good about the Broncos coming into the season and don't want to back off that just yet. I think Denver finds much more offensive success than it did against Kansas City here, while Jacksonville slows down just a bit after its blistering start. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Jaguars 21
Dajani (Chiefs -6.5): The Colts are one of four teams with a winning record in the regular season vs. Patrick Mahomes , and their last meeting went to overtime. However, the new-look Chiefs are all about running the rock with Kenneth Walker , who exploded for 173 rushing yards and a touchdown on Monday night. That could be a problem, since the Colts allowed 202 rushing yards and 506 yards of total offense vs. the Ravens. Derrick Henry galloped for 144 yards and three touchdowns, while Lamar Jackson found paydirt as well. It was the worst yardage margin (-255) in any game for the Colts since 2017. There are plenty of trends that back up the Colts' case here, such as them being 3-0 ATS in their last three games vs. the Chiefs, but I'll take Kansas City to win by a touchdown at home. ... Prediction: Chiefs 24, Colts 17
Dubin (Colts +6.5): Indianapolis got run all over by the Ravens last weekend, and we could see a repeat of that this week with the Kenneth Walker-led run game for Kansas City, which looked both efficient and explosive against the Broncos last week. But if the Chiefs can't pass the ball more efficiently than they…

title: D.J. Moore injury: Bills wideout ruled out after injuring shoulder vs. Lions
summary: The injury occurred during the second quarter of Buffalo's home opener
full_text:
The only negative for the Bills during the first half of Thursday night's game was DJ Moore exiting the game in the second quarter after sustaining a shoulder injury and a stinger. Moore was ruled out for the game.
Moore sustained the injury after falling hard on his shoulder in the back of Detroit's end zone. He left the field and went into the locker room, where he received X-rays.
Moore didn't catch any passes during the first half. The Bills led the Lions ,27-10, at halftime after scoring touchdowns on each of their first four possessions.
Last week, Moore caught five passes for 100 yards while helping Buffalo post a 36-31 win over the Texans in Houston. That game was Moore's first for the Bills after he was traded from Chicago during the offseason.
The 29-year-old Moore spent his first five NFL seasons with the Panthers before he was traded to Chicago ahead of the 2023 season. From 2019-23, Moore posted four seasons with at least 1,100 receiving yards. His best season was back in 2023, when he set career highs with 1,364 receiving yards and eight touchdown catches.
We'll provide an update on Moore's status as soon as one is available.
You can follow our live blog for updates from Thursday's game.

title: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald describes mental health struggles during first season in Seattle
summary: Macdonald opened up about 'extremely difficult' first season in Seattle
full_text:
Mike Macdonald reached the height of his profession this past February after leading the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl title. The championship was the culmination of a two-year journey for Macdonald that included the most challenging period of his life.
Macdonald, 39, became Seattle's head coach following a successful, two-year stint as the Ravens ' defensive coordinator. He went to Seattle alone; then-Ravens coach John Harbaugh didn't allow Macdonald to take any of Baltimore's other assistant coaches with him, and his wife, Stephanie, initially stayed in Baltimore with the couple's dog, Bruce, who passed away expectantly at four years old after suffering a seizure.
Not long after, Stephanie announced she was pregnant with the couple's first child. And while that was undeniably good news, it was part of what was an extremely hectic time for Macdonald, who recently opened up about his struggles during that stretch of his life.
"It was an extremely difficult time," Macdonald told Graham Bensinger . "I've never felt like that in my life. I was sick. I'd get in bed as soon as I got home and I wouldn't get out of bed until I went to work. I'd be late going to work. I wouldn't get out of bed all weekend. You know, just sit in bed. It was crazy.
"Was it depression? I don't know. Maybe. I find it hard to like self-diagnose depression. There's serious cases of depression that are clinically diagnosed. For me, it's kind of irrelevant."
Eventually, Macdonald started to get better. He did so by talking to his wife and sisters, improving his diet, working out and taking long walks that sometimes included phone conversations with players. He started stacking what he called "physical and personal wins"
"I'd work out, walk, try to eat better," he said. "I was drinking a lot. That was probably the toughest, most difficult stretch of my life. Honestly, that first few months."
Despite his struggles, Macdonald managed to guide the Seahawks to a 10-7 record in 2024. The following season, he led the Seahawks to an unexpected Super Bowl championship, culminating in a dominant win over the Patriots in Super Bowl LX.
After the game, Macdonald celebrated the win with Stephanie and his son, Jack.
Mike Macdonald celebrates winning the Super Bowl with his wife, holding their sweet baby, talking about how that is really what matters. Mike’s wife: “You did it!” ⁰Mike: “We did it.” ⁰Mike’s wife: “And we did not care.” pic.twitter.com/xhJI29L2uH
As he did in previous coaching stops, Macdonald is continuing to have success on the gridiron. And after a rough start in Seattle, he's also having success off the field, too.
"I have joy," he said. "Am I always happy? ... I think I'm happy."

title: Cowboys' recipe for success in Week 2? Start fast and make a splash to help struggling defense
summary: After defensive struggles severely limited possessions in Week 1, Dallas is prioritizing explosive plays from CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to maximize every drive against Washington
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Dallas Cowboys All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb is always pacing.
Dallas' 27-year-old, five-time Pro Bowl receiver enjoys taking a walk up and down the sideline in between drives to clear his head and reset before sitting down to break down the action with his position coach. Dallas' defense gave Lamb a lot of time to get his steps in during the Cowboys' 28-20 "Sunday Night Football'' loss at the New York Giants. New York converted 82% of its third downs, 9 of 11, with one of those stops being the game-ending knee down. That figure was New York's best third-down conversion rate in a single game since 1978.
As a result, the Giants dominated the time of possession (36:40 to 23:20), and the Cowboys had just two drives in the second half. Both resulted in touchdowns, but Dallas still came up a drive short of victory.
"The second half, we scored on the two drives that we did have the ball. So, I feel like it's just making the most of the opportunity we do have. In this game, you never know when you're going to get the ball back," Lamb said Thursday. "You might get it right back the next play [after coming off the field]. Always being ready for a sudden change, and whatever the game throws. No one can really just plan out how an NFL football game is going to go. As for us on offense, what we can do is put the ball in the end zone when we get our opps [opportunities]."
In those moments, Prescott spends his time reviewing film and preparing for Dallas' defense to get a stop to get him the football back. It just didn't happen in Week 1. Based on defensive expected points added (EPA)/ per drive in TruMedia, the Cowboys' defense delivered the worst effort by any team in Week 1, and it was worse than all of their defensive games last year. Of the 576 defensive performances since the start of the 2025 season, it ranked 574th. Their seven defensive possessions yielded four touchdowns, one takeaway via fumble recovery, a punt and the game ending.
"Yeah, just making adjustments and looking at the tape or the pictures from the last drive and going and making sure the receivers and everybody knows when you get back and you get another chance, this is what we're going to do. These are adjustments we're going to make," Prescott said Thursday. "And just trying to root my guys on. I've got a lot of faith, and I've got a lot of optimism in me. So it's nothing but that when I'm on the sideline and just trusting those guys to go get a job done."
So how can the offense adjust to maximize their drives when they get them after a sloppy Week 1 debut for Dallas' new-look defense under new defensive coordinator Christian Parker? Start fast and start with a splash. The Cowboys didn't do that in Week 1 with an opening drive three-and-out before finding their rhythm later on.
"Starting fast, it's everybody. They scored on their opening drive, and we didn't. So I'm not speaking of just the offense when I say that," Prescott said Thursday. "Special teams has a play and a part in it too. They can help. They can make a big play. They can change the field position. So it's just as a team. As a team, as a whole, we've got to go in there, we've got to start fast. And like I said, it's about being disciplined, doing the things that we obviously can handle that are 100% in our control and going from there."
Big plays to both Lamb and Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens, whose 1,429 yards receiving ranked as the third most in the NFL in 2025, would be ideal for Dallas to get going early. When asked what Dallas can build on for Week 2, Pickens was direct with his answer: splash plays. He did drop a well-thrown go ball on a vertical route deep down the sideline with 1:24 left on the clock in the first half. Those are the things Pickens is working on correcting entering Week 2 against the Washington Commanders.
"Definitely splash plays when you can because now we know only two drives [in the second half in Week 1]," Pickens said Wednesday. "When you're limited, you want those as much as you can make them."
Both Pickens and Lamb could see more chances for those types of big play splashes on Sunday against Washington and their new defensive coordinator, Daronte Jones. Jones spent the last three seasons as the Minnesota Vikings' defensive backs coach/defensive passing game coordinator under defensive coordinator Brian Flores, the most blitz-heavy defensive play caller in the league. In Flores' and Jones' three seasons together in Minnesota, the Vikings blitzed at the highest rate in the NFL across the last three seasons at 47.1%. No other NFL team was above 40%. There will also be a mixture of defensive influence from head coach Dan Quinn, who likes to feature man coverage in his game plans. When Quinn was Dallas' defensive coordinator from 2021 to 2023, Dallas' Quinn-led defenses played man coverage at the third-highest rate in the league, at 33.8%. That's all music to Pickens' ears.
"Most definitely [feel like a big game is coming on Sunday]. A lot of different stuff too just by knowing what I am capable of after what I proved last year," Pickens said. That's also what we've been seeing, thinking it's going to be that [man coverage], and then organizations knowing they don't want to put themselves in that predicament [playing Pickens and Lamb in man coverage]. A lot of other stuff too."
When Brian Schottenheimer earned the job as the Cowboys' head coach, he made sure his offensive play call sheet included lengthy sections dedicated to feeding Dallas' dynamic duo of wide receivers, Lamb and Pickens. Perhaps he punches those buttons even earlier after starting each of the Cowboys' first two drives in Week 1 with handoffs to running back Javonte Williams. That could give Dallas the splashy start everyone in their building believes is just around the corner, after finishing Week 1 with consecutive touchdown drives. Doing so would certainly take a little pressure off their work-in-progress defense.
"You never know how the game's going to unfold. I didn't anticipate us going three-and-out on the first drive, but anytime I can get a ball to George and CeeDee, I'd like to do that. It's a big sheet with a lot of their numbers on there," Schottenheimer said on Wednesday. title: Previewing Lions vs. Bills: High-powered offenses kick off Week 2 as Buffalo unveils new stadium
summary: Josh Allen and Jahmyr Gibbs headline an explosive Thursday night showdown as Buffalo opens the new Highmark Stadium against Detroit's banged-up front line
full_text:
In the Week 2 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Buffalo Bills play host to the Detroit Lions in the first-ever game at the new Highmark Stadium.
Buffalo is coming off a rollicking win over a fellow AFC contender in the Houston Texans . Josh Allen and Co. put up a spectacular offensive performance against one of the league's best defenses, with Allen throwing for a pair of touchdowns and rushing for a couple more as the Bills came from behind to win 36-31 in Houston.
Detroit similarly played a wild game against the New Orleans Saints , during which the Lions blew a 21-0 lead and had to head to overtime to beat the Saints, who failed on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won them the game. Jahmyr Gibbs had his typical fantastic day with 186 total yards and two touchdowns, but the defense left much to be desired.
Follow the game in our live blog.
Which of these two teams will win what is expected to be another high-scoring affair? We'll find out soon enough. But before we break down some key storylines, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Over/Under total for this game is 54.5 points, which is the highest of the week by 4 full points. These two offenses combined for 67 points in their respective Week 1 games, while giving up 61 to offenses that aren't necessarily expected to be world-beaters in the Saints and Texans. Given the state of their respective defenses coming into this season, it's entirely possible that we see both offenses go off in a big way on Thursday night.
Allen threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more against Houston in Week 1. He now has nine such games in his NFL career, which is two more than the next two closest players (Steve Young and Cam Newton ) combined. He absolutely tore up what many people believe is the best defense in the league last week, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 11.5 yards per attempt. And he's set up to go off again here.
Gibbs split time and touches with David Montgomery through the first three seasons of his career. That split workload was no more in Week 1: he played 74% of Detroit's offensive snaps and touched the ball an incredible 34 times (most in the league) in Detroit's overtime win. He's built a bit slighter than your typical workhorse back at just 5-9, 202 pounds, but Dan Campbell has said that he'll be that workhorse for the offense this season. He was not lying. The Bills bottled up Montgomery for only 3 yards per carry last week, but they did yield three touchdowns to Gibbs' former teammate.
Moore got off to a bit of a slow start early in Week 1, but he came on quickly and had a massive afternoon: five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown on eight targets, and he also drew a pass interference penalty to set the Bills up with first-and-goal at the 1 for another of their drives. Moore ran 81% of the routes and was targeted 30.8% of the time he ran a route, numbers that represent elite usage for a No. 1 wide receiver, which is something the Bills have needed since Stefon Diggs left town.
Detroit will be without both left guard Christian Mahogany and right tackle Blake Miller for this game, as they were ruled out with hip and knee injuries, respectively. Ben Bartch came on in relief of Mahogany in Week 1, and Larry Borom is likely to take over for Miller at tackle. That could be an issue against a Bills defensive front that played pretty well against Houston, with Greg Rousseau , in particular, perhaps set up for a nice game against Borom on that right side of the offensive line.
This should be a ridiculously high-scoring game. Both the Bills and Lions have explosive offenses paired with defenses that could best be described as charitable, which we saw last week. There are matchup advantages all over the field for both teams. I could see all of Allen, James Cook , Moore, Dalton Kincaid , Jared Goff , Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams going off in a potential fireworks show. I lean toward the Bills for the win in the debut of their new stadium, but I like the Lions to keep it close enough that the Bills don't cover. Pick: Bills 35, Lions 31

title: Former Giants DC Wink Martindale takes veiled jab at Brian Daboll over Jaxson Dart, Cam Ward
summary: The development of Dart and Ward seems to be trending in opposite directions after their coaching changes
full_text:
Former New York Giants defensive coordinator Wink Martindale did not always see eye to eye with his old boss, Brian Daboll, during their tenure together. Following his exit from the franchise and a reportedly tense relationship with Daboll, Martindale has not been shy about taking digs at the Giants' old regime . Following New York's Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys , he again indirectly prodded at Daboll with his assessment of what seems to be an improved Giants offense.
Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart was excellent in the season-opening victory with a 23-for-29 effort through the air, 230 passing yards and three touchdowns. From a passer-rating perspective, it was a meaningfully better performance than any he logged as a rookie with Daboll as play-caller. Meanwhile, Daboll now orchestrates the Tennessee Titans offense, which floundered in his debut as coordinator. Quarterback Cam Ward struggled in a largely ineffective outing as the Titans posted just 10 points in a loss to the New York Jets .
Dart appears to have leveled up under new leadership while Ward's lack of second-year improvement coincides with Daboll's arrival as play-caller. And Martindale took that disparity as an opportunity to fire a veiled jab at the former Giants coach.
"I'm not ready to crown him yet, as far as Jaxson Dart being 'the' guy. Not ready to crown him yet. I think he's gotta go through some more games and get some more body of work," Martindale said on "Talkin' Ball with Pat Leonard." "But I will tell you this: He looked like a completely different quarterback. In the same instance, so did Cam Ward when you turned on the Titans-Jets game."
Ward closed his rookie year on a personal high with eight touchdown passes to just one interception over his final four games. He averaged a passer rating of 104 over the final three contests. In his first game under Daboll's tutelage, however, Ward regressed to his early-2025 level of play, posting an 80.2 passer rating and just 140 passing yards against a maligned Jets defense.
Time will tell if Daboll can help his quarterback live up to the hype that comes with being a former No. 1 overall draft pick. If he does not, and if Dart continues to play as well as he did in New York's win over Dallas, there could be something to the coaching element.
Dart now takes his directions from head coach John Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and appeared highly comfortable in their system just one game in.
"He looked like a completely different quarterback that understood the offense and what they wanted to do and how they wanted to do it," Martindale said. "I'm excited for the kid himself if he stays within himself and understands how important the team is. The one comment that I read where he said, 'This is the way we needed to play this game,' that's when I'm like, hey, he's starting to figure it out."

title: Browns expected to sign Shedeur Sanders' college WR teammate Jimmy Horn Jr.
summary: Horn was recently released by the Panthers and played with Sanders for two seasons at Colorado
full_text:
A couple of former Colorado Buffaloes are set for a reunion, as the Cleveland Browns plan to sign wide receiver Jimmy Horn Jr . to their practice squad, according to multiple reports . Horn will once again join forces with quarterback Shedeur Sanders , although it remains to be seen whether the two will take in-game snaps together at any point this season.
With Horn set to join the practice squad and Sanders still behind starting quarterback Deshaun Watson on the depth chart, there is no guarantee that their connection from college will play out in the regular season. It is not unlikely, though, considering Watson's grip on the starting job is tenuous at best and that Horn could be elevated to the active roster once he settles in with his new team.
Horn opened the season with the Carolina Panthers and played in their Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears . The Panthers had to clear a roster spot for linebacker Tyrel Dodson , however, and Horn became a casualty of the 53-man limit. Panthers coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that he hoped Horn would return to Carolina's practice squad, but he will not make it back to his old team, with Cleveland set to pick him up off waivers.
Across 14 career games, Horn has 11 receptions for 108 yards. He also opened 2026 as the Panthers' primary kick returner and was busy in Week 1 with five touches on kickoffs and two on punts. Horn muffed one of the Bears' punts in his debut in that role.
For Horn to make the Browns' active roster and carve out a spot in the receiving unit, he would need to at least assert himself as a weapon akin to Isaiah Bond , Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace , who opened the year on the second line of the depth chart. Cleveland features a young group with two rookies holding starting roles and could continue that youth movement by inserting a second-year player into the mix.
It may be pure coincidence that the Browns intend to sign one of Sanders' college teammates, or it could hint toward their plans for the quarterback position. Any further disastrous starts from Watson would only amplify the calls for Cleveland to swap him out in favor of Sanders, and with the home opener looming in Week 3, it is reasonable to wonder if the team wants to put a struggling Watson in front of the fans that booed him off the field in the preseason.
Sanders would have ranked last among qualifiers in QBR last season if his sample size was large enough, so if the Browns are to make the switch and place him back in the lineup this year, it behooves them to put as many weapons around him as possible. Rookie receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are new targets who could help him improve as a second-year pro, and his familiarity with Horn could warrant elevating the soon-to-be Brown from the practice squad.
Horn arrived at Colorado at the same time as Sanders, ahead of the 2023 college football season. The two developed an immediate bond through the air as Sanders hit Horn for a team-high six touchdowns in their first year together. Horn's production regressed in his senior campaign as he took a backseat to eventual Heisman Trophy winner Travis Hunter .

title: Zay Flowers injury: Who will step up if Ravens star WR misses Week 2 matchup against Saints?
summary: Flowers did not participate in Baltimore's first two practices this week
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens ' season-opening blowout of the Indianapolis Colts might have come at a high cost. Amid a 41-point outburst, the Ravens saw their top two wide receivers hit the bench early due to injuries. Rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is already ruled out for Week 2, and things are trending in the wrong direction for star pass-catcher Zay Flowers , too.
Flowers, who injured his hamstring in the 18-point win, has not practiced in advance of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints . He sat out practice Wednesday and Thursday, and if he logs a third DNP to close out the week, his chances of suiting up against the Saints will be bleak.
Any time Flowers misses would deliver a meaningful hit to the Baltimore offense. In Week 1, the Ravens scored 31 of their 41 points in the first half and came back down to Earth a bit after Flowers exited. He was in the middle of a monster performance before his departure, amassing a career-best 150 receiving yards and a touchdown on five catches in the first two quarters.
Flowers is already a two-time Pro Bowler but looks poised to jump into an even higher echelon. He signed a four-year, $140 million contract extension during the offseason that made him the fourth-highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL .
New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle deployed Flowers in a variety of looks and might be able to unlock the next level of his game once he returns to the field. For instance, only 17 of Flowers' 150 yards came from wide alignment, per Next Gen Stats. Doyle placed Flowers out wide on just 36.4% of snaps against the Colts compared to the star receiver's career rate of 67.7%, and it may be no coincidence that the shift in alignment coincided with his most productive half of NFL football.
Lane landed on injured reserve with a broken wrist, and Flowers is in danger of missing at least one full game with his hamstring problem. Those two absences would leave the Ravens thin at wide receiver and potentially even more dependent on superstar running back Derrick Henry against the Saints. With his three-touchdown effort last week, Henry showed that he remains capable of putting the offense on his back if needed. He could cash in against a New Orleans team that allowed 156 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 to the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs .
But the Ravens still have to pass the ball. Who will step up? Tight end Mark Andrews figures to be a major focal point. He finished second on the team last week in receptions (four) and has the most rapport with quarterback Lamar Jackson out of all the available targets on the roster.
At wide receiver, journeyman Chris Moore is the next man up. After starting the season on the practice squad, Moore was active for Week 1's win, where he hauled in one catch on two targets. The team again signed him from its practice squad on Wednesday, coinciding with Lane's placement on IR.
LAMAR JACKSON WITH BIG PLAY TO WR CHRIS MOORE!!! 🎯 Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @ParamountPlus . pic.twitter.com/Y1bsBMXJlq
"Major shoutout to Chris Moore," coach Jesse Minter said after the win . "We decided to activate him for the game, and he had a career high. I think he had 174 all-purpose yards. It's just a credit to the depth in that room."
Alongside Moore, Rashod Bateman is the next-best option to lead the Ravens' wide receiver group. The sixth-year veteran saw just one target in the opener but has been a mainstay in the lineup for half a decade and is just two years removed from a nine-touchdown season.
Beyond that duo, experience is limited. Minter and Doyle will have to challenge the trio of Devontez Walker (who will make his season debut after missing Week 1 with a groin injury), LaJohntay Wester and rookie Elijah Sarratt to step into expanded roles in the rotation.

title: Pro Football Hall of Fame cuts Super Bowl-winning coach and 24 others from selection committee, per report
summary: The committee is being reduced from 50 members down to 28, leaving Dan Fouts and James Lofton as the only enshrinees remaining on the voting panel
full_text:
Just before the NFL season started, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced that its selection process would be undergoing some massive changes this year and those changes are starting to take shape.
The HOF has totally revamped its selection process and one of the most notable changes was the Hall's decision to trim down the selection committee. For most of the HOF's existence, the committee has consisted of 50 members. Of that total, there was one representative from each NFL team/city (32), there were 17 at-large selectors and there was one member from the Pro Football Writers of America.
Starting this year, the number of members on the selection committee will be reduced from 50 voters down to 28. To make that happen, the HOF had to cut more than two dozen people from the committee and that process has been taking place over the past week.
Hall of Fame voter Paul Kuharsky (Tennessee) has been keeping close tabs on everyone who has been cut. Of the 25 cuts that have been made so far, two of the most notable ones are Tony Dungy and Bill Polian. Dungy and Polian are both IN the Hall of Fame, which means the Hall of Fame just fired two Hall of Famers. Dungy won a Super Bowl as the head coach of the Colts in 2006 and Polian, who was the general manager in Indy for 12 seasons, earned that Lombardi Trophy with him.
Here's Kuharsky's full list of members who have been cut , along with each person's city and the number of years they were on the committee
The HOF will be keeping 28 voters on the committee (25 voting, three nonvoting participants) and that list of people will be determined annually.
The newest members of the selection committee were unveiled on Thursday (You can see the full list here ). With Dungy and Polian off the selection committee, that leaves Dan Fouts, Jared Allen and Will Shields as the only Pro Football Hall of Famers left.
Although there was one representative from each of the 32 teams/cities under the old policy, that's no longer the case. There are five NFL cities -- Miami, New England, Cincinnati, Las Vegas/Oakland, Atlanta -- that don't have a representative on the new committee.
One interesting note is that the HOF will be keeping Vahe Gregorian of the Kansas City Star. Gregorian famously voted against Bill Belichick's induction last year and the six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach didn't end up making the cut. After Belichick was snubbed during his first year as an eligible candidate last February, there were questions about whether the Hall needed to start thinking about changing its selection process , and that's exactly what has happened.
Overall, it doesn't feel like any of these changes are for the better. When it comes to the committee, it felt like 50 was a solid number. When you trim down to 25 voters -- and you don't even have one representing each NFL city -- one vote means even more, and that's not necessarily a a good thing. The Hall also got rid of the seniors category, which will now likely make it almost impossible for older players to get inducted.
