title: Russell Wilson: Lamar Jackson could end his career as best dynamic QB of all time
summary: On CBS Sports' 'Set Hut,' Wilson made his case for why Jackson could pass Michael Vick in that conversation
full_text:
Anyone who has watched the Baltimore Ravens ' Lamar Jackson knows he has exceptional talent. But one former quarterback wants to take it even further. On the latest episode of CBS Sports' "Set Hut!" Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson said Jackson could end his career as the best dynamic quarterback of all time.
. @DangeRussWilson thinks Lamar Jackson might be the most dynamic QB of all-time pic.twitter.com/2YaJb7sKq8
When discussing quarterbacks who are a threat with both their legs and arm, Wilson, of course, mentioned Michael Vick as one of the all-time greats. But he believes Jackson could even surpass Vick as one of the top dynamic players by the time the Ravens' star hangs up his cleats.
Jackson already holds the NFL record for career rushing yards by a quarterback (6,562) and single-season rushing yards by a quarterback (1,206).
"He's as good as it gets," Wilson said. "There's not anybody better than Lamar Jackson in terms of his ability to run. ... Just the plays that he's making, I don't think people understand the difficulty of these plays."
Getting up from their seats to demonstrate, Wilson and Long lined up to show the difference in what the defense sees when Jackson is under center and running back Derrick Henry is behind him. They explained that with Henry directly behind Jackson, the defense doesn't know which direction he will go, making the back harder to stop and allowing the option of play action to still make plays downfield.
Wilson called Jackson's ability to throw the ball on top of using his feet the combination that "makes him really special" and explains how much of a "threat" it makes him as a quarterback. The ability to zone read, his speed and how he moves around are some of Jackson's most impressive traits.
Long made a great comparison of Jackson's performance last week, and one fitting for Halloween season, saying, "He was running like a kid that had candy that he wasn't supposed to have."
Ravens' new head coach Jesse Minter certainly had quite a debut, with his offense racking up over 500 total yards. Jackson threw for 324 yards and one passing touchdown, with 40 rushing yards and one touchdown on the ground. Baltimore tallied a 41-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts , marking its second straight season opener with 40+ points.
The Ravens will host the New Orleans Saints , who lost 31-30 to the Detroit Lions in Week 1, on Sunday in Week 2.

title: Russell Wilson explains why Joe Burrow could leave Cincinnati, find another place to win
summary: On CBS Sports' 'Set Hut,' Wilson said Burrow's competitive nature may propel him to find a new place to play
full_text:
The NFL season just started, but the bold takes are already in midseason form. One of the most discussed comments this week came from Super Bowl champion and CBS Sports' own Russell Wilson, who suggested Burrow may leave the Cincinnati Bengals after this season.
"If it doesn't go well in Cincinnati this year ... Joe Burrow is gone," Wilson said earlier this week. "I think he wants to leave, and what's going to be interesting is, where does he go?"
"If it doesn't go well in Cincinnati this year, Joe Burrow is gone." @DangeRussWilson 👀 pic.twitter.com/fbRWVZLuYN
Wilson explained his comments on this week's episode of "Set Hut!" with three-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Kyle Long.
"I made a comment about Joe Burrow; everyone started freaking out," Wilson said, laughing. Long chimed in, "I kinda liked it."
The former Seattle Seahawks quarterback emphasized how competitive Burrow is and how strong his desire to win is.
"It's just what I feel," Wilson said, backing up his comments that Burrow could make a change if the Bengals don't go far this season. "I feel like Joe is a rockstar, he's a baller, he's a guy who wants to win, he's a competitor ... he wants to be an all-time great, and I think he has that talent."
Wilson used an example from Burrow's college career to back his point, reminding fans that Burrow transferred from Ohio State to LSU for a better chance at winning. He called the QB's choice to leave "one of the best decisions of his life."
In Cincinnati, Burrow has Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase , who both got sizable contract extensions in 2025, and Wilson believes they are "two of the most dynamic receivers maybe to ever play." But he had a fair question for them as well.
"The question is, do Chase and Higgins get tired of losing? They gotta figure it out because that's so much talent there," Wilson said.
The team has a lot of talent, but glaring issues have kept them from progressing over the last few seasons. One was the defense, and the other big one was protecting QB1.
The front office has been heavily criticized for not doing enough to keep Burrow, who has dealt with significant injuries during his career, healthy. The quarterback was limited to just eight games last year and 10 games in 2023. Wilson says the key is keeping Burrow on the field, and that falls on the organization to protect him. The offensive line kept Burrow's jersey rather clean last week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , allowing just one sack. That was a promising start to keeping their star on the field.
The Bengals were in the Super Bowl not too long ago, losing to the Los Angeles Rams to end the 2021 season, and they made it to the AFC Championship the next year. Since then, the Bengals have watched the playoffs from their couch. If the streak extends to four seasons without a playoff appearance, the Tiger King could be suiting up in different colors in the future.
Long says the Bengals are making strides to become that Super Bowl contender again, and Wilson says they're "not that far away," especially with the improvements shown through Week 1. But Cincinnati doesn't have an easy division, with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers both threats in the AFC North. Every team in their division except the Cleveland Browns won their Week 1 game, the best overall record for a division in the AFC for opening week.
In their 33-27 Week 1 victory over the Bucs, Burrow had a 71.4% completion rate, 254 yards, one touchdown and one pick-six.  The Bengals now head to Houston to face the Texans in Week 2.

title: Chiefs' Travis Kelce admits he got away with obvious penalty on key play during Week 1 win over Broncos
summary: Kelce admitted on his podcast that officials missed an obvious holding penalty on Patrick Mahomes' opening touchdown run against the Broncos
full_text:
If you're an NFL fan who thinks that the Kansas City Chiefs seem to get away with everything, then you're definitely not going to like what Travis Kelce had to say on the latest edition of the New Heights podcast .
During a conversation with his brother, Jason, Travis was recapping everything that happened during the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos in Week 1. At one point, the two guys started talking about the first touchdown of the game, which was a 15-yard run by Patrick Mahomes , a play that should have been called back.
Near the end of the run, Travis grabbed Denver's Talanoa Hufanga by the neck, which should have led to a holding penalty being called, but no flag was thrown and the touchdown counted. During the podcast, Travis admitted that he probably should have been flagged.
"It was definitely a questionable play," Travis said. "That's one of those where you get up slowly like, 'Please don't be any laundry on the field.' I had the man up by his neck. Can't do it. Can't do it, almost cost us. And to be honest, that would've been Patrick Mahomes' second rushing touchdown called back in two plays, he literally did the same thing [on the prior play].
During the broadcast, ESPN's Troy Aikman even noted that Travis probably "got away with a hold."
Travis Kelce gets away with a hold on this touchdown run from Mahomes. Rules analyst claims this is a tough one for the refs to see that's why they didn't call it pic.twitter.com/srv0qMMxwH
After Aikman was done talking, ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk said he agreed that a penalty flag should have been thrown. The touchdown came on a second-and-goal from Denver's 15-yard line, so a holding penalty would have made it even more challenging for the Chiefs to score on what was their opening drive of the game.
"That would've taken us out of the red zone," Travis said of the penalty. "That was risky business right there. You know what? Sometimes you're just living right."
The Mahomes touchdown gave Kansas City an early 7-0 lead. As Travis noted, Mahomes appeared to score one play earlier. The Chiefs had second-and-goal from the 5-yard line and Mahomes ran into the end zone, but Kansas City got called for holding, which took them back to the 15-yard line. On the very next play, Mahomes scored again, and this time, the TD counted, despite the fact that Travis was clearly holding.
If you've spent any time on the internet, you may have noticed that there are a lof fans out there who seem to think that NFL officials show bias toward the Chiefs and this probably won't help that.
If this had been a closer game, the missed call probably would have been a bigger controversy, but with the Chiefs winning by three touchdowns, it wasn't something the Broncos really complained about after the game. The Broncos lost because they couldn't tackle Kenneth Walker III (23 carries for 173 yards), not because of the holding no-call on Travis, but it's still not a great look for officials to miss such an obvious call.

title: Kyrie Irving offers to pay Azeez Al-Shaair's fine for tribute to Palestinian girl killed in Gaza
summary: The Mavericks All-Star guard and Texans Pro Bowl linebacker have both been outspoken advocates for Palestine
full_text:
Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined $11,941 by the NFL for for wearing eye black that featured the name Hind Rajab, a five-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed by the Israel Defense Forces in Gaza in 2024. NBA star Kyrie Irving tweeted this week that he would pay the fine for Al-Shaair.
Al-Shaair's fine was for a violation of the NFL uniform and equipment rules, which do not allow for the display of a personal message without prior approval. He was also fined last season for wearing eye black that displayed the message "stop the genocide" during a playoff game.
I’ll take care of his fine https://t.co/RUo9jXkCFu
Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, has been an outspoken advocate for Palestinians, wearing cleats that support Palestinian causes through the NFL's "My Clause, My Cleats" program over the last few seasons. Irving, a nine-time All-Star who plays for the Dallas Mavericks, has also been an advocate for Palestine.
"If my platform can bring even a little hope to families in Palestine, then that is what I want to use it for," Al-Shaair said last year.
Hind Rajab was killed along with six members of her family by Israeli forces in Gaza City in 2024. Last month, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) acknowledged the killing of Rajab and her family and said it had opened an internal investigation into the incident, which occurred when the military opened fire on the vehicle they were in.
Al-Shaair, now in his eighth NFL season, was a Pro Bowler last year. He had eight tackles in the Texans' Week 1 loss to the Bills

title: Nico Collins' hamstring injury: Status unclear for Week 2, per report
summary: Collins had seven catches and a touchdown in Week 1, but he suffered a hamstring injury during Wednesday's practice
full_text:
The Houston Texans may have escaped a major injury scare, but they could also be without their star wide receiver this Sunday. Nico Collins met with doctors after suffering a hamstring injury in Wednesday's practice, and while the injury is not considered serious, his status is in jeopardy for the Texans' Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals , according to ESPN .
Collins got off to a strong start this season, posting seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown in Houston's season-opening loss to the Buffalo Bills . He's coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns and three consecutive 1,000-plus-yard, six-plus-touchdown seasons. He is widely considered one of the best X receivers in the league.
If Collins misses Sunday's game, the Texans could be in trouble. Houston already lost presumptive No. 2 wideout Jayden Higgins for the year to a torn ACL suffered during a preseason practice, while the explosive Tank Dell remains on injured reserve. He was not yet ready to return from the devastating knee injury he suffered during the 2024 season.
If Collins is out, the Texans will likely roll with Kayshon Boutte , Xavier Hutchinson , Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne as their top four wide receivers. They also have Lewis Bond , Josh Kelly , Daniel Sobkowicz and Mitchell Tinsley on the practice squad. Houston also has five tight ends — Dalton Schultz , Foster Moreau , Marlin Klein , Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan — on the roster and would likely lean into more 12 and 13 personnel looks in Collins' absence.
The Bengals looked somewhat improved defensively in Week 1, forcing four turnovers against the Buccaneers . But they still allowed 5.4 yards per play, which would have been an above-average offensive mark last season. Houston managed 5.2 yards per play in Week 1 against Buffalo with an inconsistent run game ( David Montgomery scored three total touchdowns but averaged just three yards per carry), and things could get even more difficult in Week 2 if the Texans are without Collins to open up the field.

title: Lions vs. Bills: Is this a battle of teams who blew their best SB window or is it still open in 2026?
summary: Two of the league's most successful yet snake-bitten teams square off in Week 2 on "Thursday Night Football"
full_text:
There may not be two more successful yet snake-bitten teams in the NFL than the two facing off on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 2: the Detroit Lions (1-0) and the Buffalo Bills (1-0).
Both squads are tied with the Philadelphia Eagles for the best record in the entire league since 2023 at 37-15. Detroit is the only team to play every season in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) and never reach the title game, while Buffalo has the best record in the NFL since 2020 (73-27, .730 winning percentage) and has not reached the Super Bowl since 1994. The Bills' 73 wins from 2020 to 2025 are the most in a six-season span ever without a Super Bowl appearance.
Thursday night's matchup, which will kick off the opening of the Bills' new Highmark Stadium, is guaranteed to have points. The last time these two teams met, Buffalo won 48-42 in a game with 90 combined points and 1,080 combined yards. Bills quarterback Josh Allen racked up 430 total yards and four total touchdowns, while Lions quarterback Jared Goff threw for 494 yards and five touchdowns. That made Goff the only quarterback in NFL history to lose a game with 400-plus passing yards, five-plus passing touchdowns and no interceptions, per CBS Sports Research.
The entire football world and their grandmas know Thursday night will be an offensive laser show, but is this game also a battle of teams that already blew their best Super Bowl window? Let's look at each team's best chance over the last decade to win it all and project who will get the closest to the Vince Lombardi Trophy in 2026.
Season they blew their best chance: 2023
Detroit went 12-5 and won the NFC North in 2023 with the NFL's No. 5 scoring offense (27.5 points per game) and Pro Bowl seasons from the following players: running back Jahmyr Gibbs , wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (also first team All-Pro), right tackle Penei Sewell (also first team All-Pro), center Frank Ragnow (also second team All-Pro), edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson and linebacker Jalen Reeves-Maybin (also second team All-Pro). Head coach Dan Campbell also had two current 1-0 NFL head coaches as his offensive coordinator ( Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears ) and defensive coordinator (Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets ).
The Lions beat their former face-of-the-franchise quarterback Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams 24-23 in the wild card round for their first playoff win since the 1991 season. They followed that with a 31-23 divisional-round victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . In the NFC Championship Game at the San Francisco 49ers , Detroit led 24-7 at halftime, appearing well on its way to its first Super Bowl appearance. But the wheels came off the wagon in the second half, with their first four possessions ending with: a turnover on downs at the 49ers' 28, a lost fumble, a punt, and a turnover on downs at the 49ers' 30. That dry spell helped the 49ers rip off 27 consecutive points (a field goal, two consecutive touchdown drives, a field goal and another touchdown drive).
A touchdown pass from Goff to wide receiver Jameson Williams with 56 seconds left wasn't enough for Detroit to recover from their meltdown, and Campbell summed up what was to come for his Lions quite well.
"Sometimes you can only say so much," Campbell told reporters after the Lions' 34-31 defeat. "(Sometimes) you gotta live it, unfortunately. You gotta get your heart ripped out, which we did. And it's a lesson learned. And look, I told those guys, 'This may have been our only shot.' Do I think that? No. Do I believe that? No. However, I know how hard it is to get here. I am well aware. It's gonna be twice as hard to get back to this point next year."
Detroit hasn't been back to the conference championship since, suffering an NFC divisional round upset as the No. 1 seed against the Washington Commanders in 2024 before missing the playoffs entirely in 2025.
Season they blew their best chance: 2025
From 2020 to 2024, each Bills' playoff runs ended against one of two opponents: Patrick Mahomes ' Kansas City Chiefs or Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals . In the 2025 postseason, neither team was present, and neither was two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson's Baltimore Ravens .
The AFC had never been more wide open for the taking than it was in 2025. The Bills waltzed into a postseason field where the conference's top seed quarterbacked was second-year passer Bo Nix . The Seattle Seahawks , who ended up winning the Super Bowl, had just +390 odds to do so on FanDuel Sportsbook, the fourth-longest odds by a Super Bowl favorite entering an NFL postseason all-time, per CBS Sports Research. Last season represented the most parity-filled, wide-open playoff bracket in recent memory.
Then came the AFC divisional round disaster in Denver. Allen committed a playoff career-high four turnovers (two interceptions and two fumbles lost). Allen became the first quarterback to record multiple interceptions and multiple fumbles lost in a playoff game since Carson Palmer in the Arizona Cardinals ' 49-15 meltdown in the 2015 NFC Championship Game. Despite all that, Buffalo still nearly won, falling 33-30 in overtime.
That's why Allen and left tackle Dion Dawkins were notably in tears at their postgame media availability, unlike in some other years this decade.
So which of these Charlie Brown-like franchises, who keep coming so close yet so far from Super Bowl glory, will get closest in 2026? Both have top-10 offenses with top-10 quarterbacks and running backs in their backfields. The gap between the two teams comes down to their defenses and their respective conferences.
Detroit's defense is just too injury-plagued, with both safeties, Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (chronic, degenerative left knee problem), still sidelined. Plus, they don't have difference-makers along the defensive line other than two-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson. Buffalo has playmakers at both defensive tackle ( Ed Oliver ) and edge rusher (Gregory Rousseau) while also possessing enough talent on the back end of their defense to get by.
Another issue for Detroit is that the NFC is absolutely loaded. It has the defending champion Seahawks, the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams, the feisty San Francisco 49ers, a Philadelphia Eagles squad with two Super Bowl appearances and a Super Bowl win since 2022, a rising Chicago Bears squad, a Green Bay Packers team that has made three consecutive playoffs and a Minnesota Vikings squad who continues to be their personal bogeyman at times.
The AFC is much more shaky. The Jacksonville Jaguars have some talent questions after a free-agent exodus, the defending AFC champion New England Patriots are in shambles after Week 1, the Houston Texans are limited at quarterback, the Denver Broncos are limited at quarterback and Burrow's Bengals haven't been able to get back to the playoffs the last three seasons.
Outside of the Chiefs with a revived Mahomes and the Ravens with a reinvigorated Jackson alongside new coordinator Declan Doyle, the Bills have as great a shot as any to represent the AFC in Super Bowl LXI. They'll get closer to Super Bowl glory than the Lions do in 2026.

title: Chiefs' Travis Kelce among the victims in Ponzi scheme, per report
summary: Kelce was named as an investor in a fund run by Siddarth Jawahar, who pleaded guilty in a federal fraud case
full_text:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce was reportedly among the victims in a multi-million dollar Ponzi scheme. Kelce was not named in the indictment or judgment in the case, but his name was briefly read in a St. Louis federal courtroom as being among the more than 64 victims, according to an investigative reporter for KMOV in St. Louis .
The defendant in the case is Siddarth Jawahar, who founded an investment fund called Swiftarc Ventures Lab Fund in which Kelce was identified as an investor in a 2021 Forbes article . Other notable investors included NBA players Tim Hardaway Jr., Gary Harris and Mason Plumlee. It was not reported whether any of that trio were also listed as being among the victims in the fraud case against Jawahar.
The indictment, which was obtained by USA TODAY Sports , stated that Jawahar took tens of millions of dollars from new investors and used a portion of the money to pay off his previous investors and used the remainer to fund a luxury lifestyle "including payments for flights on private planes, stays at luxury hotels, and expensive outings at lavish restaurants."
Jawahar pleaded guilty in January to federal wire fraud charges. He is currently in Ste. Genevieve County jail, according to KMOV. He was sentenced this week to 11 years in prison followed by three years of supervision and ordered to pay over $31 million in restitution to his various victims.
According to KMOV, Missouri Congressman Sam Graves (R) wrote a letter to the judge in the case, asking for leniency and a four-year sentence, but the judge did not heed the recommendation.
author: Jared Dubin

title: It wouldn't shock me IF ... NFL Week 2: Jets finally snap historic streak, Deshaun Watson benched
summary: Don't be surprised if we see these storylines develop over the course of Week 2
full_text:
Always expect the unexpected when it comes to the NFL . Once you think you have the league figured out, it'll humble you real quick with developments that you wouldn't have even dreamt were possible.
There's no better example than what transpired in some pockets of the opening weekend. For instance, who had the Cardinals pulling off the outright upset on the road against the Chargers ? What about the Bengals defense generating four turnovers in a winning effort? Or the Carson Wentz-led Vikings erasing a 12-point second-half deficit to beat the Packers ? Crazy!
While we didn't put those developments on your radar, we did clue you in to some key developments in last week's column. That included fantasy football waiver wire darling Devaughn Vele finding the end zone. That was our biggest bullseye, but we were sniffing around a few others. Most notably, we highlighted David Montgomery and predicted a big outing, but we suggested 100 yards rushing instead of the three total touchdowns he scored against Buffalo.
Meanwhile, we also wrote that we wouldn't have been surprised that Tua Tagovailoa would be one-and-done as the Falcons starter. Really, it appears like it'll be more of a none-and-done situation, as he did not play in Week 1 due to an oblique injury. Now, Cooper Rush is in line for another start unless Michael Penix Jr . makes his return. In any event, the Tagovailoa experiment didn't make it to Week 2, so we'll give ourselves half credit on that.
But now it's time for Week 2. Below, we're going to highlight a handful of potential storylines and/or individual performances that may sound far-fetched right now, but we wouldn't be shocked if they happened this weekend.
The New York Jets have gone 18 straight games without recording an interception, which just so happens to be the longest streak in NFL history. The last time they snatched the football away from an opposing quarterback came back during the 2024 season in a Week 18 contest with the Miami Dolphins . The New York Knicks won the NBA Finals more recently than the Jets have hauled in an interception! While this drought feels never-ending, don't be surprised if it ends this week as the Jets open up MetLife Stadium against the Packers.
Really, this is a play against Jordan Love , who did not have a strong game in Week 1 as Green Bay blew a 12-point second-half lead to Minnesota. He completed just 50% of his passes in the loss and recorded one interception, but his day could've been much worse. Love had two other interceptions dropped in the defeat and had an off-target rate of 23.8% (worst among all quarterbacks in Week 1). His turnover-worthy throw rate was 7.1%, which was second and only looking up to Deshaun Watson , Cooper Rush, and Drake Maye , who all had a 9.1% turnover-worthy throw rate.
Those underlying metrics from Love suggest that he's ripe for another turnover, and this new-look Jets defense could finally get the organization off the schneid.
The clock is going to strike midnight on Deshaun Watson sooner rather than later, and I expect it may come as early as this weekend when the Browns visit the Buccaneers . Watson did not look good in his 2026 debut, throwing an interception on their first possession of the game and nearly committing two other turnovers (another pick and a fumble) later on. The offense couldn't muster anything outside of a 46-yard touchdown heave in garbage time. When Jacksonville was firing on all cylinders in the first half before packing it in and preserving health over the final two quarters, the Browns' offense was outscored 24-0.
Watson's EPA per dropback was 25th among all quarterbacks last week, while his turnover-worthy throw rate was tied for the highest in the league (excluding Kyler Murray , who left Minnesota's game early in the first quarter). It's hard to imagine that they'll improve as they gear up to take on the Buccaneers.
While the 33 points allowed by Tampa Bay may have you thinking Watson and Co. may have an easier go of it in Week 2, there's some important context with that crooked number. First, Mayfield and the offense turned the ball over four times, and Cincinnati scored 20 points off of those turnovers. They weren't put in the best spots at times, but they did have some flashes, including rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter posting 11 tackles, a sack, and a pick-six. They'll be better in Week 2, and that's bad news for Watson.
If he continues to struggle and those almost-turnovers turn into actual turnovers while Baker Mayfield is slinging it around the yard against his former team, it's the perfect storm for Todd Monken to make an in-game switch and have Shedeur Sanders come in as Watson watches from the bench.
It was essentially a perfect outing from Trevor Lawrence in the Week 1 win against Cleveland. The Jags QB completed 18-of-23 for 245 yards and four passing touchdowns, which culminated in a 150.6 passer rating. The one aspect of Lawrence's game that wasn't on display in the opener, however, was his legs. With the game secure, Lawrence didn't need to tuck and run it in Week 1, totaling just three yards on two carries. That said, he's more than capable of being a factor on the ground, as evident in career-high 359 yards rushing and nine rushing touchdowns in 2025.
One of those nine scores came in Week 16 when Lawrence's Jaguars visited the Denver Broncos , which is who they'll be facing on Sunday. It was a lackluster effort by the Broncos' defense on Monday night against the Chiefs , missing 28 tackles. I expect them to take that personally and try to pin their ears back and make a statement in the home opener, which could force Lawrence out of the pocket and scrambling. As we saw with Patrick Mahomes , that is one way you can attack them, and we won't be shocked to see Lawrence calling his own number for a touchdown in Week 2.
Gambling angle to note : Trevor Lawrence is +350 anytime touchdown in Week 2 ( DraftKings Sportsbook).
Baltimore's receiver room took a hit in the opening win against Indy, with rookie standout Ja'Kobi Lane being placed on IR due to a wrist injury, while star receiver Zay Flowers ' status is uncertain after leaving the game with a hamstring injury. If Flowers is unable to go, that drastically concentrates the passing game for Lamar Jackson . That leaves Rashod Baeman and Devontez Walker as the top two receivers, but the real benefactor will most likely be Mark Andrews . The veteran tight end matched Flowers for a team-high six targets in Week 1, which he turned into four catches for 49 yards. That number could realistically double, considering where Baltimore's pass-catcher situation stands.
Remember, Andrews is the clear No. 1 tight end with the Ravens after Isaiah Likely left in free agency this offseason, with backups Durham Smythe and Matthew Hibner each catching just one pass in the opener. When Jackson drops back to pass, Andrews will be one of the few familiar options.
He's also taken on a sizable workload in the past, with his career-high in targets for a single game sitting at 15 (Week 18 vs. the Steelers during the 2021 season). However, the last time Andrews saw a double-digit target total in a game came all the way back in Week 9 of the 2023 season against Seattle. Andrews has only had 12 or more targets four times in his career, but it's conceivable here.
Meanwhile, this matchup with New Orleans has sneaky shootout potential, with the total sitting at 46.5 and is juiced to the over. In their overtime loss to the Lions , Sam LaPorta was the second-most productive pass catcher in Detroit's offense behind Amon-Ra St. Brown . Lost in the shuffle of Week 1 was Commanders third-round rookie receiver Antonio Williams balling out against Philadelphia. He led the team with 64 receiving yards on four catches. The Clemson product also caught a 1-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels in the fourth quarter. However, because the Commanders…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Upset alert for NFL Week 2? Why these 5 favorites could easily drop their matchup, including the Ravens
summary: Green Bay and Houston are also on upset alert
full_text:
The NFL isn't shy about throwing curveballs. Whenever you think you have teams pegged and know how a given week will unfold, the league reminds you that anything can happen.
We were reminded of that right out of the gate in Week 1, where there were several upsets across the league. The most noteworthy of them all came from the Arizona Cardinals . They were the biggest underdog of the entire Week 1 slate and, despite that, pulled off the outright win over the Chargers on the road. The New York Giants were another team that defied the odds and beat out the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night.
Those two upsets weren't on our radar last week, but we did guide you to two of them . We correctly put the Titans and Rams on upset alert, and they each came out of the opener 0-1, losing to the Jets and 49ers , respectively. We nearly had another in the Houston Texans , but Josh Allen's late-game heroics and C.J. Stroud's fourth-quarter fumble fumbled that opportunity away.
Now, we turn our attention to Week 2, where we've again identified five favorites that could be on upset alert.
All NFL odds via FanDuel Sportsbook.
We kick off Week 2 with a doozy of a matchup where points should come in bunches. Along with two high-octane offenses, the Bills will be opening up the new Highmark Stadium, so there will be plenty of buzz on Thursday night. While the narrative surrounding both teams centers on their offense, they each allowed at least 30 points on defense in Week 1.
Specifically, as it relates to Buffalo's defense and Detroit's chance of pulling off the upset, I'm not sure they fixed their inability to stop the run. While they held David Montgomery (3.0 yards per carry) in check from an efficiency standpoint, the Texans' back still totaled 60 yards on the ground and two touchdowns. He also caught all three of his targets for 19 yards and another score. Meanwhile, Woddy Marks rushed for 42 yards on just nine carries, and his longest rush went for just 12 yards, so there was success to be had against this unit that'll now try to contain Jahmyr Gibbs .
Gibbs is coming off a career-high 34 touches in Week 1 and was electric with each one of them. He rushed for 156 yards and two touchdowns, while forcing 10 missed tackles (per Next Gen Stats). If he can get rolling and help Detroit win the time-of-possession battle, it could go a long way toward helping the defense limit Josh Allen's impact.
Dan Campbell has also been superb at getting his team to play up for Thursday Night Football, owning a 4-0 record. Meanwhile, Jared Goff is 21-8 in primetime games since 2019.
Is Cincinnati's defense ... good? In the Week 1 win over Tampa Bay, the Bengals' defense forced four fumbles and totaled 20 points off of those turnovers. Their slew of new additions to that side of the ball made immediate impacts, namely edge rusher Boye Mafe and safety Bryan Cook .
Three of those forced fumbles were the Bengals getting after Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield , and they'll look to put a similar dent in C.J. Stroud. The Texans' signal caller doesn't have a reputation for being the most secure with the football and lost two fumbles in the opening loss to Buffalo, so there is an opportunity for Cincinnati to keep the turnover momentum rolling in Week 2.
If that happens and Joe Burrow and Co. have short fields, it'll only help them put points on the board against the Texans' defense. Speaking of Houston's defense, they didn't look like the shutdown unit they were in 2025 in Week 1.
If this is an early indication that the unit may regress (even slightly) from their stellar production last season, the Bengals could be live. Meanwhile, Joe Burrow has typically played well in this setting. In the last 11 games Joe Burrow has started as a road underdog, the Bengals have a +4.1 points-per-game differential.
The Green Bay Packers have my attention, and not in a good way. Not only did they blow a 12-point lead to the Carson Wentz-led Vikings , but Jordan Love left little to be desired in the process. He completed just half of his passes and had an off-target rate of 23.8%, the worst among all quarterbacks in Week 1. When you pair shaky quarterback play with a nonexistent running game and a defense that gave up 29 unanswered points in the second half, they are liable to get clipped by anyone. That includes the New York Jets.
That's especially true given that the Jets looked solid in their road upset win over the Titans in Week 1. Geno Smith's numbers won't jump out of the box score, but he was extremely efficient. Remember what I said about Jordan Love's off-target rate? Well, Smith's was the polar opposite, not throwing a single off-target ball in the win. Provided he keeps it clean again and doesn't make Green Bay's life easier, New York could mess around as a home dog and win outright.
Dating back to last year, the Packers are currently on a six-game losing streak, which coincides with Micah Parsons ' injury (he suffered a torn ACL in the first game of the losing streak). In that time, their production has fallen off a cliff, averaging 19.7 points per game while allowing 30.5 points per game.
Watching the Denver defense on Monday night was jarring. Their tackling was as sloppy as you'll see in the NFL, missing 28 on the night and allowing 247 yards after those misses, according to Next Gen Stats . Meanwhile, handing the offensive play sheet to Davis Webb feels like an unnecessary downgrade from Sean Payton, and the unit couldn't move the ball consistently down the field.
Whether it's Payton calling the shots or merely overseeing things from the sidelines, his Broncos teams have a propensity for starting slow. Payton has the most 0-2 starts (7) by a head coach in NFL history and is 2-8 over his Broncos tenure in the first three weeks of the season.
Meanwhile, going into Denver and pulling out a win isn't foreign to the Jaguars. Back in Week 16 of last season, they did just that in the form of a dominant 34-20 victory. Those 34 points allowed were the most Denver surrendered in any game last season.
The Baltimore Ravens look like they are back to being a juggernaut after a dominant win over the Colts , dropping 41 points in the process. While Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry will continue to be the straws that stir the drink of the offense, the receiver room did take some sizable hits in the winning effort. Standout rookie Ja'Kobi Lane is slated to undergo wrist surgery, while top wideout Zay Flowers ' status for Week 2 is in question due to a hamstring injury that knocked him out of the opener. If he's sidelined for this game or limited due to the injury, it takes some of the potency out of the Baltimore offense.
As for the Saints, their defense did keep the Lions offense in check in the first half, allowing just seven points. Things went off the rails in the second half and overtime, but they did show an ability to slow down a high-profile offense (at least momentarily). As for Tyler Shough , he shook off some early-game struggles and played well down the stretch against Detroit, finishing with 410 yards passing, three touchdowns, and two interceptions.
If this turns into another shootout, Shough has shown he can at least hang around.
I also wonder if this is quietly a look-ahead spot for Baltimore, which will travel to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, after this matchup for a Week 3 contest against the Dallas Cowboys.

title: What to know about Falcons – Panthers in Week 2
summary: Both the Atlanta Falcons and Carolina Panthers are seeking a win to bounce back from tough opening games. Naturally, only one of them can get the W, so who will it be? With NFC South games, that question is always a fraught one, but we’ll take a look at how Carolina has evolved and the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 16: Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson (7) reacts after scoring a touchdown during the NFL game between the Carolina Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons on November 16th, 2025 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Both the Atlanta Falcons and Carolina Panthers are seeking a win to bounce back from tough opening games. Naturally, only one of them can get the W, so who will it be? With NFC South games, that question is always a fraught one, but we’ll take a look at how Carolina has evolved and the key points in this matchup that might help determine it. Here’s what you should know about Week 2. How these two teams stack up It’s one game, but these Panthers looked like the polar opposite of Atlanta. Their offense was very good—they rank 4th in the NFL in points and 3rd in yardage—but their defense was abysmal and they’re dead last in points and yardage allowed. The Falcons, meanwhile, are 25th in points and 30th in yardage after Cooper Rush’s sad day at the office, but 10th in points allowed and 8th in yardage. It would be a mistake to think that’s going to hold up over time, but it makes for an interesting potential dynamic heading into Week 2. Otherwise, it’s too early to stack these teams up against one another, especially with Atlanta not actually getting to trot a starting quarterback out there who was higher than third on the depth chart heading into the season. Suffice to say the Panthers do have a very capable offense and a defense that’s better than what we’ve seen to this point, in the same way the Falcons do have a very capable defense and are likely to find life on offense sooner than later. How the Panthers have changed in 2026 Honestly, they haven’t changed much at all. They landed two big names in free agency, adding edge rusher Jaelen Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd, and added two new starting offensive linemen in center Luke Fortner and left tackle Rasheed Walker. They also brought aboard a pair of starters via the draft in right tackle Monroe Freeling and defensive tackle Lee Hunter. Their most impactful changes were inarguably along the offensive line, where they switched out three starters; Walker was awesome in Week 1 and Fortner and Freeling held their own. Otherwise, this is just a tweaked football team. They now have Kenny Pickett as their backup and mostly added peripheral pieces on offense, figuring an improved line would give Bryce Young and his merry band of playmakers more time to work with. The defense has four new starters in total—linebacker Bobby Okereke was also added—but is largely the same too. Carolina is making a big bet on a strong defense and improving offense gelling this year. In Week 1, that bet was a mixed bag. What to know about Week 2 This game will turn on two questions: Can Cooper Rush avoid costly turnovers and make on-time throws to his playmakers, and can the Falcons finally get Bryce Young under control? None of the Cooper Rush stuff applies if Michael Penix Jr. or Tua Tagovailoa are starting, but you’ll excuse me if I’m not thinking that’s particularly likely. Neither one is easy to talk about without getting an uneasy feeling. I have to think Rush will look better against a lesser defense, a week removed from back spasms, and with the team having a better idea of what he can and can’t do after a full game. What we do know is that Rush’s permanent limitations—the lack of arm strength, the shaky decision-making under duress, and the lack of mobility in the pocket—mean he’s essentially a turret you have to have aimed and ready to fire quickly. That will mean a ton of screens, but quick hitters to Bijan Robinson, Kyle Pitts, Zachariah Branch, and so forth will be necessary to keep him from getting killed. The deep passing game seems like it’s off the table entirely—Rush hit on route close to 20 yards and missed badly on every other shot he took—so the Falcons have to take something predictable and make it dynamic and difficult to defend. That’s no small task, but if Rush can be about 25% sharper and 25% quicker to get rid of the ball, the Falcons offense should at least stay afloat given that Bijan Robinson isn’t going to stop being Bijan Robinson. Young, meanwhile, has been a Falcons killer. He had one bad game against them in his first career start against Atlanta, tossing two picks and completing just 52% of his passes, but has not been under a 66.7% completion rate in four games since and has two monster efforts against Atlanta. One of them, unfortunately, was against Jeff Ulbrich’s defense last year, when Young went for 561 yards and three touchdowns last year combined with zero interceptions and a rushing touchdown.. The Falcons simply haven’t been able to pressure him, keep him in the pocket, and force him into mistakes despite and another round of that with a limited quarterback on Atlanta’s side means this one could turn into a genuine bloodbath. Managing Young, of course, means managing more than Young. It means keeping Chuba Hubbard and Jonathan Brooks in check, clamping down on a big target in Tet McMillan who had a monster game last year, and generally not getting pushed around at the line of scrimmage. The Falcons have a strong group on the interior and some promising rookies up front, but will need an opportunistic and talented secondary to force Young into errors to give this team a fighting chance. Beyond the two central quarterback questions, there’s plenty to think about. Bijan and Brian Robinsons should be able to run roughshod over a Panthers defense that just finished getting annihilated by the Bears, and they’re going to need to be able to do so to give this offense an edge. Kicker is worth watching after Nick Folk missed two kicks last week but comes back home to friendlier environs, while Ryan Fitzgerald is a bottom third of the league kicker—he was 23rd in field goal percentage and 24th in extra point percentage last year—who isn’t guaranteed to come up big when Carolina needs him. The Falcons and Panthers both missed too many tackles and piled up too many penalties a week ago—the Falcons had 9 for 96 yards and the Panthers had 11 for 84 yards—so the more disciplined team is going to have an obvious edge. As always, this is a divisional game, which increases the chances that something weird happens, and the Falcons and Panthers have already played plenty of very silly games over the past few seasons. If this team can cut down the penalties, get Rush on track, run well, and keep Young from taking over the game, they have a fine shot of winning their first game under Kevin Stefanski at home. If not, we could be ticketed for an ugly sort of afternoon right before a run of primetime games.

Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baltimore’s season opener gave us our first real look at the starting units on both sides of the football, and several players immediately stood out in the Ravens’ 41-23 victory over Indianapolis. Zay Flowers wasted little time reminding everyone why Baltimore committed to him with a massive contract extension this offseason, turning five receptions into 150 yards and a touchdown in only one half of football. Defensively, Tavius Robinson showed an intriguing combination of power and athleticism while generating seven pressures, and Trey Hendrickson’s Ravens debut provided an immediate example of how much his presence can change Baltimore’s pass rush. Here’s what stood out from that trio in Baltimore’s season-opening victory: WR Zay Flowers 20 snaps (11 slot, 7 wide, 2 backfield) | 5 catches (6 targets) | 150 yards | 1 touchdown Flowers opened the season with a statement performance, producing 150 receiving yards and a touchdown despite playing only one half of football. The efficiency of his performance was remarkable. Flowers averaged 13.64 yards per route run and Lamar Jackson posted a perfect 158.3 passer rating when targeting him. But the numbers only tell part of the story. Flowers consistently showed the traits that make him such a difficult matchup within Baltimore’s passing game. His spatial awareness stood out against zone coverage. On one reception, Flowers recognized two defenders closing around him and intelligently settled into the open window rather than continuing his route into coverage. That ability to understand spacing and make himself available to Jackson is an important part of his development beyond simply being an explosive athlete. Zay Flowers finished with 150 yards on 5 catches vs the colts Did a nice job finding open space against zone and sitting down, maintained his route pacing while dealing with physicality throughout his route. Ate up yards quick after the catch. pic.twitter.com/rIHaHFr1Mh — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 14, 2026 Against man coverage, his release quickness continued to create problems. Flowers consistently got off the line of scrimmage in a flash and generated separation multiple times by forcing defensive backs to immediately react to his acceleration. Once he got into space, there was another gear available. Flowers’ ability to transition from receiver to runner almost instantly remains one of the most dangerous elements of his game. That combination of route awareness, release quickness and open-field acceleration made him extremely difficult for Indianapolis to contain. Postgame takeaway: Flowers couldn’t have provided a much better opening statement after signing his extension this offseason. The 150 yards and touchdown will grab the attention, but the underlying performance was just as encouraging. His ability to manipulate space against zone coverage, separate against man and immediately accelerate after the catch gives Baltimore multiple ways to manufacture explosive plays through him. If Week 1 was any indication, Flowers looks ready to take another step as the centerpiece of Baltimore’s passing attack. EDGE Tavius Robinson 44 snaps | 14 run defense | 25 pass rush | 5 coverage | 7 pressures | 1 sack Robinson entered the season primarily known for his ability to defend the run and create pressure through power, but his performance against Indianapolis showed there may be more to his game. The biggest surprise was his athleticism in space. Robinson showed impressive pursuit ability for a player with his frame, chasing plays from the backside and covering considerably more ground than you would typically expect from a power-oriented defensive lineman. There were moments where the combination of size, length and pursuit was reminiscent of what Baltimore has gotten from Justin Madubuike when chasing plays outside the structure of the defense. Tavius Robinson looked extremely twitched up yesterday 5 pressures and 1 sack. We know about his power rush but impressed by his athleticism and pursuit ability pic.twitter.com/A9gTtx1AOR — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 14, 2026 His pass rushing was still built around his power. Robinson generated seven pressures, and on three of them he effectively converted speed to power. He used the distance between himself and the offensive tackle as a momentum amplifier, building speed into contact before using his long frame to transfer that momentum through the blocker and collapse the pocket. That ability becomes especially valuable when Robinson can force tackles to respect his athleticism around the edge. We also saw his value within Baltimore’s pressure designs. On one rep, Robinson effectively created a pick that helped collapse the interior and opened a path for another defender. It wasn’t a pressure that necessarily shows up entirely in his individual statistics, but it demonstrated how his size and physicality can create opportunities for the rushers around him. His sack came from another encouraging trait: patience. Robinson stayed disciplined on the backside of play action rather than immediately chasing the initial action. Once the quarterback became available, Robinson was left unblocked and finished the play. Postgame takeaway: Robinson’s seven pressures were impressive, but the athleticism he displayed may have been the more important development. His power has always been the foundation of his game, and his ability to convert speed to power remains his most reliable path to the quarterback. Adding better pursuit ability and functional athleticism to that profile makes him a considerably more versatile defender. With Robinson approaching an important contract decision this offseason, performances like this could make his future in Baltimore increasingly interesting. EDGE Trey Hendrickson 40 snaps | 10 run defense | 26 pass rush | 4 coverage | 8 pressures Baltimore brought Hendrickson in to change the complexion of its pass rush, and his first regular-season performance showed exactly why. Hendrickson generated eight pressures in his Ravens debut, but his impact extended beyond his individual production. With the four-time Pro Bowler on the field, Baltimore generated pressure on 58.6% of its opportunities. Without him, that number fell to 20%. That is the definition of a force multiplier. Indianapolis couldn’t consistently afford to give Hendrickson favorable one-on-one opportunities, and when those opportunities appeared, he repeatedly took advantage. His speed-to-power conversion was particularly effective. Trey Hendrickson had 8 pressures vs the colts Speed to power, speed to power and more speed to power. Got a ton of one on one opportunities and took advantage of it. Force multiplier pic.twitter.com/to5hZj8DnK — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 15, 2026 Hendrickson threatened offensive tackles with his get-off before transitioning into power and driving them backward toward the quarterback. Rather than simply trying to run through the tackle from the beginning of the rep, Hendrickson forced blockers to account for his speed before converting that momentum into contact. We also saw the depth of his pass-rush toolbox. Hendrickson flashed an effective dip-and-rip when attacking around the edge, giving tackles a completely different problem than his speed-to-power rush. More impressive was the consistency of his hands. His punch timing and hand fighting were exceptionally polished, allowing him to attack the tackle’s hands, prevent blockers from establishing control and transition between moves without wasting much movement. At times, the hand usage looked almost black-belt-like. That technical refinement is what separates Hendrickson from rushers who rely primarily on athleticism. He has multiple…

title: AFC North Preview, Week 2: Ravens, Bengals and Steelers seek 2-0 starts
summary: All but one team in the AFC North started the season off with a win in Week 1. The Baltimore Ravens are the only team on the road this Sunday, as they look to improve to 2-0 along with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns will look to bounce back with […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Derrick Henry #22 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images All but one team in the AFC North started the season off with a win in Week 1. The Baltimore Ravens are the only team on the road this Sunday, as they look to improve to 2-0 along with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns will look to bounce back with an upset victory. Division Standings: Baltimore Ravens 1-0 Cincinnati Bengals 1-0 Pittsburgh Steelers 1-0 Cleveland Browns 0-1 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ New England Patriots, 1:00pm EST After a 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1, the Steelers will face a much tougher task this coming Sunday as they travel to New England to take on the Patriots. While the Patriots are 0-1 and are down their No. 1 wide receiver in A.J. Brown, the reigning AFC Champions are well-coached, talented and will be eager to bounce back from their season-opening defeat. Furthermore, they’ll also have had a few extra days of rest and preparation entering this week’s matchup. The Steelers will need to be sharper offensively against a better defensive unit. In Week 1, they were just 3-for-13 on third down attempts and gained 264 total yards, narrowly edging the Falcons in most categories. They also struggled to run the ball, gaining 58 yards while averaging 2.8 yards per rush. Jaylen Warren was much more effective than Rico Dowdle despite playing less snaps. The running back split between both players will likely fluctuate week-to-week, but either way the Steelers will need better ground production in Week 2. Pittsburgh’s defense was able to wreak havoc last week with four sacks, five quarterback hits and two interceptions. They’ll need to be similarly disruptive against star quarterback Drake Maye, who is coming off a three-interception performance. The Patriots’ pass-catchers are less potent without Brown in the lineup, so expect the Steelers to make a concentrated effort to stop the run and force Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas to beat their secondary. Cleveland Browns Matchup: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1:00pm EST The Browns are coming off a putrid performance in Week 1, where they were routed in Jacksonville by a score of 34-10. They will remain on the road in Week 2 once again in Florida, this time taking on the Buccaneers. While this profiles as a more favorable matchup on paper, the Browns have a lot of issues to correct if they hope to avoid another 0-2 start to begin the year. For starters, the Browns only gained one first down last week and committed 11 penalties, two areas that need to be reversed. They also need to be more effective running the ball. They only rushed for 87 yards against the Jaguars and Deshaun Watson led the team with 38 of them. Their only notable offensive play was a long touchdown pass to rookie Denzel Boston late in the fourth quarter. A huge spotlight is on Watson in this game as his leash as the starting quarterback is very short. Watson took five sacks last week and had a QBR of 34.2. Defensively, the Browns may find life easier facing Baker Mayfield than Trevor Lawrence. Mayfield had multiple turnovers in Week 1. Creating takeaways to shorten the field for Watson and company should lead to greater offensive success. Tampa Bay still scored 27 points in spite of their turnover woes last week, though, demonstrating their scoring capabilities. The Browns’ defense will need to play more disciplined than they did against the Jaguars. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: vs. New Orleans Saints, 1:00pm EST The Ravens are returning home in Week 2 after a successful season opener in Indianapolis, where they defeated the Colts handedly by 21 points. Baltimore’s new-look offense under Declan Doyle totaled over 500 yards and scored 41 points, highlighted by multiple explosive plays both on the ground and through the air. Defensively, the Ravens forced two turnovers and created a ton of pressure on the quarterback. Against the New Orleans Saints, the recipe for a similarly success formula is ripe. The Saints have an underrated offense under Kellen Moore and a group of pass-catchers to support sophomore quarterback Tyler Shough, led by wide receiver Chris Olave. Olave had nearly 200 receiving yards in Week 1 and will be key for the Ravens to slow down. The Saints fell down big to the Detroit Lions in Week 1 before storming back to score 30 points and nearly escape with an overtime victory. Expect Jesse Minter to dial up pressure against Shough and try to force the young quarterback into turnovers, in a raucous road environment. The Ravens are short-handed at wide receiver following injuries to Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane. The latter is confirmed to be sidelined for at least a few weeks, whereas Flowers has a chance to play in this game but may be limited by his hamstring ailment. The Saints’ defense is plenty beatable, as the Lions demonstrated in Week 1, but the Ravens’ offensive line will need play a more complete game in pass protection and commit less penalties. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: @ Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST The Bengals enter Week 2 on the heels of a 33-27 victory over the Buccaneers, where they led by multiple possessions for most of the game. Cincinnati gained 26 first downs and converted over 50% of their third down attempts, totaling 351 yards. They weren’t efficient running the ball and superstar wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase was surprisingly quiet (two catches for 12 yards) — but the fact the team still scored 30+ points in spite of these factors may be a good sign. More importantly, the Bengals forced four turnovers on defense and scored points off all of them, including a fumble return touchdown to open the game. They will try to replicate more takeaway success defensively against the Texans this Sunday on the road. The Texans’ offense proved to be dangerous in the season opener, exceeding the 30-point mark in Week 1 with nearly 400 total yards. However, they may be without the services of their No. 1 wide receiver in this matchup, as Nico Collins is dealing with a hamstring injury. Houston’s passing attack is far less dangerous with no Collins or a limited version, so that would play into the Bengals’ favor. On-paper, the Texans present a huge challenge for the Bengals’ offense, as they were considered to be the top overall defense in the league entering this season. However, Houston’s defense was carved up by the Bills in Week 1 and allowed 36 points, so they may be vulnerable than many believed. The Bengals will likely need Chase to be much more involved in this game and find more balance in the run game. Quarterback Joe Burrow is reportedly dealing with a back injury this week.

title: DJ Moore injury: Bills WR avoids serious shoulder injury
summary: Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore headed to the locker room with a shoulder injury Thursday night. He dove for a pass in the back of the end zone and immediately grabbed at the area. On Friday morning, Adam Schefter reported Moore isn’t expected to miss much if any time. That is a big sigh […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 13: DJ Moore #2 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Houston Texans during the second quarter of the game at NRG Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore headed to the locker room with a shoulder injury Thursday night. He dove for a pass in the back of the end zone and immediately grabbed at the area. On Friday morning, Adam Schefter reported Moore isn’t expected to miss much if any time. That is a big sigh of relief. The Bills announced he was questionable to return with a shoulder injury and a stinger, but he was later downgraded to OUT and went for an X-ray. This Schefter report would indicate his collarbone is not broken. Moore was the marquee trade executed by the Bills to open up their pass offense this offseason and he’s delivered through six quarters. In addition to scoring his own touchdown and topping 100 yards, he’s drawn the secondary’s attention away from others. The Bills would move back to an “Everybody Eats” mentality without Moore in the lineup for an extended period of time. With Moore out, the Bills have Skylar Bell as a healthy scratch and he would move into the lineup. Brandin Cooks is a free agent and could return to Buffalo, as well. Trent Sherfield and Greg Dortch are on the practice squad and Dortch has used up two of his three game day elevations. Keon Coleman took the share of Moore’s snaps during the game, stepping up when the Bills needed him most.

title: Buffalo Bills OLB Greg Rousseau hunting QBs at a HOF pace
summary: There was a time when Buffalo Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau was able to hide a bit in the shadows of NFL’s trenches as a complete and steady 4-3 defensive end who often went about his business without a ton of outside fan fare. Drafted by the Bills 30th overall in the 2021 NFL Draft, […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Greg Rousseau #15 of the Buffalo Bills reacts after a defensive stop during the first half of the NFL game against the Detroit Lions at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a time when Buffalo Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau was able to hide a bit in the shadows of NFL’s trenches as a complete and steady 4-3 defensive end who often went about his business without a ton of outside fan fare. Drafted by the Bills 30th overall in the 2021 NFL Draft, Rousseau entered the team’s complex to great applause and he flashed brilliant ability during his rookie season. Yet for all of Rousseau’s unique abilities as a 6’7”, 266 pound defensive end, he too often appeared limited by former head coach Sean McDermott’s 4-3 scheme. Rousseau was asked to play tight in the trenches, which seemed to hinder his ability to explode off the ball and use his length to swipe away offensive linemen. In the five seasons leading up to the 2026 NFL season, Rousseau totaled 32 sacks with eight as the high-water mark (2022, 2024 seasons), also adding seven forced fumbles. His story told the tale of a very good player who trended a bit underappreciated. Fast forward to September 2026 with Rousseau two games into his sixth NFL season, and the tale being told is one of far grander horizons. In the course of those two games in five days, Rousseau has put NFL offenses on notice. Now making hay as an outside linebacker/edge rusher in a 3-4 base system coached by Jim Leonhard, it’s fair to say Rousseau’s feasting at the expense of nearly every offensive lineman in his path. His move off the line of scrimmage and out wider has allowed Rousseau’s explosion and length to carry him to new heights as a front seven defender. Following the Bills’ win over the Detroit Lions in primetime for Week 2, Rousseau has now totaled four sacks in two games. That’s better than half his total from last season, and represents the total number of sacks he tallied his rookie season. Rousseau’s now in rarified air where the only other Bills player to ever accomplish the same feat was Pro Football Hall of Fame defensive end Bruce Smith. That’s elite company, and speaks to the talent that president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane saw out of Rousseau in the lead-up to the 2021 draft. But Rousseau couldn’t have asked for a more productive start this season. Against Detroit, Rousseau finished with two sacks, four quarterback hits, and two tackles for loss among three total tackles. Those sacks played a key role in dismantling Detroit’s offense in the first quarter, which ultimately proved to be too much of a hole to dig out of late in action. In Week 1, Rousseau played the role of Grim Reaper, ending Houston’s opening drive with a strip sack that gave the ball back to Buffalo. Then during the final defensive stand against the Texans, Rousseau again bullied his way to another strip-sack and turnover, ending any chance of victory for the H-Town hopefuls. It’s fair to wonder if the Bills win in Houston without those two plays by Rousseau. Despite that, he wasn’t named AFC Defensive Player of Week 1. Will he find his way to the award in Week 2? Playing on a national stage certainly helps. Instead, you can bet that Rousseau is focused only on winning and playing the final game of the season in Los Angeles, eschewing All-Pro and Pro Bowl nods in favor of that elusive Super Bowl win. It still feels like Rousseau is one of the more underappreciated NFL players, but that may be about to change if his work in the first two games is an indication of the season ahead of him. Of course it’s unlikely he maintains such a pace through an entire 17-game season, but Rousseau is currently on pace to finish the regular season with 34 sacks. What a story that’d be for Rousseau, who appears to be in the midst of a career Renaissance under Leonhard’s direction. You can rest assured that Bills Mafia is here his come-up.
author: Matt Byham

title: Bills vs. Lions game analysis: Notes from 1st win at new Highmark Stadium
summary: Week 2 of NFL action began with a bang during Thursday Night Football, and the Buffalo Bills opened the new stadium with a 41-31 win over the Lions. Here’s everything I wrote down as it unfolded. Buffalo Bills insights from 1st half vs. Lions Buffalo Bills insights from 2nd half vs. Lions 1-0. Go Bills! […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills is pressured by Aidan Hutchinson #97 of the Detroit Lions during the fourth quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 2 of NFL action began with a bang during Thursday Night Football , and the Buffalo Bills opened the new stadium with a 41-31 win over the Lions. Here’s everything I wrote down as it unfolded. Buffalo Bills insights from 1st half vs. Lions Nice opening drive for the new stadium’s 1st drive. Josh Allen ran the entire field and closed the drive with a tush push TD. What a tush push merchant. (Allen finished the night with 248 passing yards, three touchdown passes, 69 rushing yards, and two more scores on the ground — five total touchdowns.) Spencer Brown can’t be left alone with Aidan Hutchinson. Brown is good, but Hutchinson is special. He’ll need help. (Hutchinson beat Brown for a sack on Buffalo’s defense opening series.) Great 1st drive by the D. Some nice stunt games by the DL. Gregory Rousseau and Deone Walker start on fire again. (Rousseau finished with two sacks on the night.) Khalil Shakir lined up outside could beat Rock Ya-Sin deep easily. Josh would like that one back with some pressure on his face after scrambling a bit. Good to see Shakir winning outside, though. This offense will be fun to watch. What a change from what we had with Joe Brady under Sean McDermott. I told you the O had a lot of McD on it. He wanted to run the ball, he wanted to methodically march down the field, control the clock, and keep his D off the field. Brady doesn’t really care about that — he has Josh, and he knows what it means. I love it. Again, it’s important to have a run game, especially in January. But with Josh Allen as your QB, he’s got to be the centerpiece of the offense. Everything has to run through him. Use the good run game to help him, not to try to win through it and ask Josh to bail the team out of a hole when it doesn’t work. (James Cook topped 100 rushing yards himself, finishing with a touchdown.) Groot is looking really good to start the season. Doing what’s expected of him against a backup RT, dominating the matchup. Run defense is still a problem, especially in nickel package. TD Lions. Defense is a work in progress and will have its ups and downs. O has got to keep the foot on the gas. See, after establishing Josh Allen, it’s even easier to run the ball. Dalton Kincaid is 100% ready for a breakout season. It’s happening. (Kincaid finished his day with 7 receptions in 8 targets, for 95 yards and a 16-yard touchdown catch.) Deone Walker is such a game-changer. His length affects how opposing QBs throw the ball very often. What a stud. No reason to bring DJ Moore back today. Hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he can recover with some extra time before Week 3. (Moore left the game with a shoulder injury and did not return.) An example of a disadvantage of being extremely aggressive on O on every drive — the bad two-minute drill gave the Lions O an extra shot. Wasn’t anything egregious, but it gave the Lions extra points on the board before they got the ball back in the second half. Something that wouldn’t have happened in McDermott’s days. Different football strategies. (The Lions closed the half with a 31-yard field goal, trailing 27-10 and getting the ball back after the break.) Buffalo Bills insights from 2nd half vs. Lions Bad two-minute drill on O ended up costing a 10-point difference. Again, that’s something that would never happen under McDermott. It’s not like the new and refreshing Brady’s way is always the best way. Bills’ O is showing they can also put together a long, methodical drive to rest their D and burn some clock as they score another TD. Bills’ D is showing they can allow back-to-back 20+ yard plays and nullify the good job the O just did to help them. (Jared Goff finished with four touchdown passes on the night.) Jordan Hancock had some good snaps in for a hurt Dee Alford. Davison Igbinosun is very grabby for a man corner. (Igbinosun was flagged for defensive holding on a fourth down that kept a Lions drive alive.) Bills’ CBs, in general, are struggling in man coverage for the second consecutive week. Christian Benford also had a bad flag in the end zone. Frank Gore Jr. is clearly Ty Johnson’s backup in blocking situations. Great block on a Josh power run. Shakir with bad hands? Not common. (Shakir dropped a third-and-8 pass that ended a Bills drive.) Defense comes back and, despite a lot of bad, does its job in a moment the Lions could have made it a three-point game. (I don’t know how — just like Simba, they refuse to die.) DJ Moore has been missed. Keon Coleman with a clutch third-down catch. This game has been a good confidence builder for him. Another PA, and Josh finds Coleman for his sixth reception on six targets to move the chains. Amazing how Josh can wait for the absolute last moment to throw it fading away, changing his arm angle, right on the money. It set up two James Cook runs to seal the win with another TD, Bills 41-24. Bills have seven more minutes of ball possession at this point in the game. Good to see the defense adjust and stop the run during the game and do its job when it was needed. They allowed the Bills to open up an advantage, then stopped their offense when the game was on the line. As Brady said in the interview after the last game, “a lot of ugly in between,” though. A little more ugly with a 4th-and-18 conversion, and another TD pass — a 30-yarder from Goff to Amon-Ra St. Brown, with backups already on the field. (St. Brown finished with nine catches for 142 yards and two touchdowns.) The Bills’ dominance in this game felt way bigger than the 10-point difference in the final 41-31 score. The end-of-first-half swing made the win a little more difficult than it should have been. It’s important to find the sweet spot between being very aggressive and minimizing the opponent’s chances of a comeback. Ball game. Josh Allen with 9 TDs in 2 games. It’s definitely a new era. Great to see the team open the new stadium with another beautiful performance. (Allen’s five touchdowns Thursday made it nine across Buffalo’s first two games.) 1-0. Go Bills! Catch up on all this and more with the latest edition of Leading the Charge!
author: Fernando Schmude

title: James Cook passes Joe Cribbs on Buffalo Bills’ all-time rushing list
summary: James Cook just keeps climbing. The Buffalo Bills running back entered Thursday night’s game against the Detroit Lions needing 130 rushing yards to pass Joe Cribbs and move into fifth place on the franchise’s all-time rushing list.  He got there in the fourth quarter. Cook’s 22-yard run that set up his one-yard touchdown rush a play later pushed him past Cribbs’ 4,445 career rushing yards in a Bills uniform […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Running back James Cook III (4) of the Buffalo Bills carries the ball during an NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Billsat Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York, USA, on Thursday, September 17, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images James Cook just keeps climbing. The Buffalo Bills running back entered Thursday night’s game against the Detroit Lions needing 130 rushing yards to pass Joe Cribbs and move into fifth place on the franchise’s all-time rushing list. He got there in the fourth quarter. Cook’s 22-yard run that set up his one-yard touchdown rush a play later pushed him past Cribbs’ 4,445 career rushing yards in a Bills uniform and gave Cook another spot in Buffalo’s record book. And this one comes with some history behind it. Cribbs arrived in Buffalo as a second-round draft pick in 1980 and immediately became one of the NFL’s most productive running backs. He topped 1,000 yards in each of his first two seasons, then did it again in 1983. After spending the 1984 season in the USFL, Cribbs returned to Buffalo for one final season in 1985. By the time his Bills career was over, Cribbs had rushed 1,082 times for 4,445 yards and 21 touchdowns across 64 games. Cook has taken a very different route to essentially the same place. Buffalo selected Cook in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft, but he wasn’t immediately handed the workload Cribbs received four decades earlier. Cook had just 89 carries as a rookie before becoming the Bills’ primary running back in his second season. Now, in his fifth season with Buffalo, Cook also passed a player who spent five seasons in a Bills uniform — but he did it on considerably fewer carries. Cook entered the game with 4,316 rushing yards on 855 attempts, 227 fewer carries than Cribbs needed to reach 4,445. With Cribbs now behind him, only four names remain ahead of Cook on the Bills’ all-time rushing list. Josh Allen entered the night fourth with 4,744 yards, followed by Fred Jackson with 5,646. Both are catchable this season. After that, the climb gets a whole lot steeper: O.J. Simpson sits at 10,183 yards, with Thurman Thomas atop the franchise record book at 11,938. For now, James Cook can add another line to an already growing résumé. He’s one of the five most prolific rushers in Buffalo Bills history.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Joe Brady makes Buffalo Bills HC history with franchise’s first 2-0 start
summary: Joe Brady has only been the head coach of the Buffalo Bills for two games, but apparently that was long enough to make a little franchise history.  With Buffalo’s 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night, Brady became the first head coach in Bills history to begin his Buffalo career 2-0. And there have been plenty of chances.  […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Head coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills communicates during an NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Billsat Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York, USA, on Thursday, September 17, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Joe Brady has only been the head coach of the Buffalo Bills for two games, but apparently that was long enough to make a little franchise history. With Buffalo’s 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night, Brady became the first head coach in Bills history to begin his Buffalo career 2-0. And there have been plenty of chances. Brady is the 19th different man to serve as head coach of the Bills since the franchise began play in 1960. Three of those coaches — Marv Levy, Jim Ringo, and Forrest Gregg — are members of the Pro Football Hall of Fame, although Ringo and Gregg earned their spots in Canton primarily for their playing careers. Until Brady, only three of those coaches had even managed to win Game 1. Levy did it in 1986, Rex Ryan followed in 2015, and Sean McDermott joined the list in 2017. But all three lost the following week, leaving 2-0 as a mark no new Bills head coach had reached. That is, until Thursday night. If Brady was going to be the one to finally do it, the setting wasn’t bad either. The win came in Buffalo’s home opener, which also happened to be the first regular-season game played in the new Highmark Stadium. Brady took over a team with plenty of expectations and, while two games certainly isn’t enough to tell us what the Joe Brady era will ultimately look like, it is enough to put his name somewhere no other Bills head coach has been. Maybe he’ll even need to change up his usual post-game tweet — at least for this week. 2-0.
