title: Colts LBs coach weighs in on rookie CJ Allen’s complete lack of initial playing time
summary: Once a projected starter, Indianapolis Colts rookie linebacker CJ Allen was limited solely to the sidelines for what many thought would be his pro debut during last weekend’s blowout home loss to the Baltimore Ravens. While Allen dressed and wasn’t listed as a healthy inactive pregame, he didn’t play a single snap for the Colts […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Atlanta Falcons running back Tyler Goodson (25) runs past Indianapolis Colts linebacker CJ Allen (53) for a touchdown during the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Once a projected starter, Indianapolis Colts rookie linebacker CJ Allen was limited solely to the sidelines for what many thought would be his pro debut during last weekend’s blowout home loss to the Baltimore Ravens. While Allen dressed and wasn’t listed as a healthy inactive pregame, he didn’t play a single snap for the Colts in Week 1—and may as well have been in street clothes. Not on defense. Not on special teams. For a Colts defense whose linebackers clearly struggled on Sunday, Allen didn’t see the field. This was a rookie that at one point, the Colts coaching staff may have initially expected to don the green dot, wearing the sole helmet transmitter for relaying the defensive play-calling to his teammates on the field. Instead, Allen didn’t play at all. Now, it’s way-too-early to write Allen off yet. He was largely limited throughout training camp with a calf and hamstring strain respectively. He fell behind and as a rookie, wasn’t able to catch up. Even though he was the projected starter ahead of Week 3 of preseason , he didn’t play like he belonged there quite yet. After an underwhelming final preseason performance, he was rightfully relegated back to the 2nd-team defense with fellow Indianapolis rookie Bryce Boettcher. If you ask his Colts linebackers coach James Bettcher, there’s no real cause for concern yet. Allen is simply making up for lost time on the field, doing all of the right things off the field, and gradually improving. Consequently, Bettcher believes his time will eventually come: “He’s getting better every day,” said Bettcher via 1075 The Fan’s Kevin Bowen . “Continues to get reps in practice. His preparation’s been awesome. Comes in early, stays late. There’s not anything that CJ’s not doing from a preparation standpoint. It’s just time on the grass for him.” “I think we all understand how different the NFL game is to the college game. At the second level, at the linebacker position, things happen fast, and coverages change. Fronts change. Run fits change. And just the opportunity to get the reps doing that, he’s getting better every day, and his time will come.” “When it does, he’s going to go out there, and he’s going to play well.“ Sometimes, it takes a young player some time to get their first footing. Allen is only 21-years-old, and left after his junior season at the University of Georgia. It’s possible that after missing a large portion of training camp, he just needs a little more time to develop, adjust to the pro level, and could still play a meaningful role at linebacker later this season. Nothing’s guaranteed though either. We’ve seen other Colts’ past second round picks, particularly at defensive end such as Kemoko Turay and Ben Banogu, that it never clicked for here, and the jury is still out on 2025 2nd rounder Jaylahn Tuimoloau, who hasn’t consistently shown enough flashes on the field yet in over a season of play—even at times, being a healthy scratch last year. There’s still realistic hope that Allen can be a core starting linebacker for the Colts for years to come, but at the same time, expectations needs to be clearly tempered as it relates to his rookie campaign—as he’s not ready yet.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Colts’ green dot gaffe falls firmly on coaching staff’s shoulders
summary: Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen indicated earlier this week that veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither would wear the defense’s lone helmet transmitter, and thus, be denoted with the infamous green dot for rapidly communicating the defensive play-calling to his teammates on the field. Having previously bestowed that honor to veteran safety Cam Bynum, it clearly […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Bynum #0 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates after breaking up a pass against the Baltimore Ravens during the second quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen indicated earlier this week that veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither would wear the defense’s lone helmet transmitter, and thus, be denoted with the infamous green dot for rapidly communicating the defensive play-calling to his teammates on the field. Having previously bestowed that honor to veteran safety Cam Bynum, it clearly didn’t work out during Sunday’s blowout loss to the Baltimore Ravens, as the Colts defense clearly experienced numerous communication issues pre-snap and resulting blown coverage assignments thereafter. The Colts defense may have already been in for a long day going up against the likes of Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry in Week 1—and an entire offseason for them to prepare, but that only made it longer. The Colts had entered training camp with the notion that either rookie 2nd round linebacker CJ Allen or Bynum would don the green dot, but after Allen was limited throughout training camp with injuries and relegated to the 2nd-team defense, the nod ultimately went to the latter, which turned out to be a major mistake in hindsight. Look, I get the Colts coaching staff’s rationale to some extent. Longtime linebacker Zaire Franklin previously wore the green dot for the Indy defense. After he was traded to the Green Bay Packers this past offseason, the Colts didn’t have a clear and obvious answer at starting linebacker. Davis-Gaither is a veteran, but it’s his first year with Indianapolis, and the thought is that he’s more of a stopgap than core starter going forward. It also wasn’t a guarantee that he’d be safely penciled into the starting lineup at linebacker—as he had to earn it, just like his defensive teammates. Bynum was locked in at starting safety. The Colts ideally wanted Allen to stand out in training camp and preseason and also earn a starting job, and thus, the green dot outright, but that obviously didn’t happen. So instead, they bestowed the honor on Bynum, who’s already played a season in Indianapolis as part of Lou Anarumo’s defense and is considered a veteran leader in backend of their secondary and entire unit collectively. There’s a few major issues I have though are as follows: No other NFL team in the entire NFL deploys a green dot on their starting safety , as it’s all linebackers. The Colts may have thought they were being a trendsetter, but sometimes you have to question if you’re the only one swimming in the deep end of the pool, maybe there’s good reason for it. The Colts had at least the preseason finale when their starters initially played to test out Bynum effectively donning the green dot for their defense. Maybe the Detroit Lions purposefully didn’t show them exotic offensive looks. After all, it’s only preseason, but did they notice it was an issue at all? Even from like a practical and logistics standpoint when Bynum had to run a mile back to the defensive huddle? Davis-Gaither is new to the Colts at a free agent signing this past offseason, but he also played under Anarumo previously as a member of the Cincinnati Bengals defense from 2020-24. It’s not a brand new defense out of the box by any means for him. Even in the short-term, it would’ve made sense for him to handle interim green dot duties, at least until either Allen or fellow rookie Bryce Boettcher got up to speed. When shedding light on the precarious situation and rightfully being relieved of ‘green dot duty,’ Bynum seem rather relieved himself. While he didn’t directly throw the coaching staff under the bus, he clearly was more than comfortable with the team’s abrupt decision to transition the helmet transmitter assignment to Davis-Gaither instead: “Yeah, there’s a few scenarios, where there’s a deep ball and I’m playing post safety, and you know I’m running to the ball, incomplete pass, and then I have to run back to the huddle,” said Bynum during Wednesday’s post-practice media availability. “I’m not saying it’s not possible, but there’s times where if the offense is on the ball quick, and I’m coming from afar, I’m running to the huddle listening to the call, and I’m trying to get it back.” “So I think, like I said, I think it’s really good for a linebacker to do it, and I think it’ll help the defense also to play a lot better this week. . . . I think it’s a really good move to have Akeem do it, especially knowing that he’s a good veteran, and that he can do that part also.” It’s not Bynum’s fault by any means. He was being a pro, and accepted the additional play-calling responsibilities as the coaching staff requested from him. It’s the Colts coaching staff’s for asking him to do it in the first place.
author: Luke Schultheis

Richardson who is the teams primary […]

Wednesday’s practice report for #INDvsKC . pic.twitter.com/pDVrNmzCkM — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) September 16, 2026 Quarterback Anthony Richardson (groin) missed practice on Wednesday. Richardson was seen during the open to the media portion of practice without a helmet and a towel over his head. Richardson who is the teams primary back up quarterback appears to have injured his groin despite not logging any snaps last Sunday. Wide receiver Ashton Dulin (ankle) missed practice Wednesday. Dulin who has moved up in the depth chart with Alec Pierce still nursing an ongoing heel injury. Dulin is a core special teamed for the Colts and is a big leader on that phase of the game too. Linebacker Austin Ajake (hamstring) was a limited participant. Ajake missed last weeks game against the Ravens due to the hamstring injury. Wide receiver Keenan Allen (rear) was also a limited participant. Allen is more than likely going to join the veterans on the team who had scheduled rest days as the season continues. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (ankle), wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) and linebacker Akers Davis-Gaither (knee) were all full participants at practice, despite being listed on the injury report.

title: Jaguars vs Broncos: Matchup History Through the Decades
summary: The current AFC South Division leaders, the Jacksonville Jaguars, will be on the road for Week 2 to face off against the Denver Broncos. The Jaguars and Broncos series is tied 8-8. Experts do not like the Jags’ odds, but here’s hoping they deliver the upset two seasons in a row and take the series […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 12: The line of scrimmage between the Denver Broncos and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Invesco Field at Mile High on October 12, 2008 in Denver, Colorado. The Jaguars defeated the Broncos 24-17. (Photo by Tom Hauck/Getty Images) | Getty Images The current AFC South Division leaders, the Jacksonville Jaguars, will be on the road for Week 2 to face off against the Denver Broncos. The Jaguars and Broncos series is tied 8-8 . Experts do not like the Jags’ odds , but here’s hoping they deliver the upset two seasons in a row and take the series lead while we revisit Jacksonville in Denver through the decades. The 1990s AFC Divisional Playoff at Mile High Stadium on January 4, 1997 Final score: Jaguars 30 – Broncos 27 Attendance: 75,678 The Jaguars recorded 22 first downs, 443 total net yards, and a 32:24 time of possession, compared to the Broncos’ 21 first downs, 351 total net yards, and 27:36 time of possession. Natrone Means, Keenan McCardell, and Jimmy Smith scored touchdowns. Mark Brunell completed 18 out of 29 attempted passes for 245 yards and was sacked twice for a loss of five yards. Natrone Means led the team with 140 rushing yards, and Jimmy Smith led with 71 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made the three attempted field goals. Eddie Robinson registered a sack on John Elway. The 2000s Week 3 at Invesco Field at Mile High on September 23, 2007 Final score: Jaguars 23 – Broncos 14 Attendance: 76,463 Reggie Williams and Greg Jones scored touchdowns. David Garrard completed 14 out of 20 attempted passes for 154 yards and was sacked three times for a loss of 14 yards. Fred Taylor led the team with 84 rushing yards, and Marcedes Lewis led with 44 receiving yards. John Carney made the three attempted field goals. Sammy Knight had an interception, and Reggie Hayward recorded a sack on Jay Cutler for a loss of four yards. The 2010s Week 4 on September 29, 2019, at Empower Field at Mile High Final Score: Jaguars 26 – Broncos 24 Attendance: 76,219 Ryquell Armstead and James O’Shaughnessy scored the Jaguars’ two touchdowns during the third quarter. Minshew completed 19 out of 33 attempted passes for 213 yards and was sacked five times for a loss of 27 yards. Leonard Fournette was on fire with 225 rushing yards, and Dede Westbrook led the team with 66 receiving yards. Lambo made the four attempted field goals. Jarrod Wilson and Quincy Williams led the team with eight combined tackles each. The 2020s Week 16 on December 21, 2025, at Empower Field at Mile High Final Score: Jaguars 34 – Broncos 20 Attendance: 76,858 The two teams traded punts during the first quarter, until the Broncos decided to go for it on fourth down and get the needed yardage for a field goal. Unfortunately for them, Lutz’s kick hit the uprights. The Jaguars’ offense started cooking, leading to a Parker Washington touchdown. The Broncos started the second quarter striking back with a touchdown by Sutton and a field goal by Lutz to bring Denver’s lead to 10-7. Strange puts another seven on the board for Jacksonville, and following a punt by the Broncos, Cam Little increases the lead by three. The second half starts with the two teams trading touchdowns. With roughly four minutes left in the third quarter, the offense scores again for Jacksonville. The Broncos try to decrease the deficit but fumble the ball, and the Jags recover. Little’s kick is good to increase the lead to 34-17. Denver kicks a field goal, and Jarrian Jones intercepts the ball during their next drive. The Jags succeed with the upset. title: Chiefs-Colts: 5 things to watch in the Week 2 matchup
summary: This week, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2 on “Sunday Night Football.” The game kicks off at 7:20 p.m. Arrowhead time and will be broadcast locally on KSHB. The Chiefs are riding high after a 31-10 victory over the Denver Broncos on Monday Night. The game saw quarterback Patrick […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 23: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs meets with Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts following the game, at Arrowhead Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2 on “Sunday Night Football.” The game kicks off at 7:20 p.m. Arrowhead time and will be broadcast locally on KSHB. The Chiefs are riding high after a 31-10 victory over the Denver Broncos on Monday Night. The game saw quarterback Patrick Mahomes return to the field, along with a host of new Chiefs making their NFL and team debuts. The lopsided win made waves across the NFL and put the rest of the league on notice. The Colts ran into a buzzsaw in week one, getting blown out 41-23 by the Baltimore Ravens . A few garbage-time touchdowns kept it respectable for the Colts, but the majority of the game did not go their way. Colts head coach Shane Steichen is 0-1 against Andy Reid head-to-head, and the loss came last season when the Chiefs narrowly beat the Colts 23-20 at home last season in overtime. Here are five things to watch in another AFC battle: 1. Improving the passing attack Despite the Chiefs’ Week 1 win over Denver, the pass game struggled for most of the night. Mahomes completed just 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns, and threw an interception. Tight end Travis Kelce led all pass catchers with 71 yards, and no player had more than three receptions. When you take receptions away from tight ends and running backs, the Chiefs’ wide receivers combined for a measly five receptions for 37 yards: two for Rashee Rice and three for Xavier Worthy. “I gotta be better… There were times where those guys were open, and I was a little bit quick with my reads and getting the ball out of my hand.” Patrick Mahomes on the lackluster passing attack vs Denver pic.twitter.com/oyHugIUqgg — KC Sports Network (@KCSportsNetwork) September 15, 2026 Tight ends and running backs will remain engaged in the passing game, but the Chiefs’ receivers must turn in a much better performance than they did in week one, and Mahomes must as well. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton and rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen each had only one target in the contest, but the staff should consider giving each more looks, especially given Rice and Worthy’s struggles. In Week 1, Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw for over 300 yards and a touchdown, while receiver Zay Flowers caught five passes for 150 yards, and the Colts seemed helpless to stop the onslaught. Last season against the Colts, Mahomes threw for 352 yards, with Rice having 141 of them, and Worthy chipping in with 59 as well. The Colts return much of the same defense they played in 2025, so it will be worth watching to see if the Chiefs can duplicate last season’s performance. 2. Stopping Jonathan Taylor The Colts offense looked dormant for long stretches on Sunday, but star running back Jonathan Taylor still had a productive game, putting up just under 100 yards and two touchdowns. Taylor was third in the NFL in 2025 with 1,585 rushing yards, and led the league with 18 touchdowns on the ground. The Chiefs ranked ninth in the NFL in 2025 in rushing yards allowed, giving up only 1797, and were tied for sixth in yards per carry allowed at four per handoff. #Chiefs LB Nick Bolton on containing Jonathan Taylor Sunday night: “He’s been one of the best backs in the league since I got here—it’s definitely a challenge, it’s going to take all eleven of us.” — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) September 16, 2026 Against the Colts last season, Kansas City bottled up Taylor, allowing only 58 yards on 17 handoffs, and kept him under four yards a clip. In Week 1 against Denver, the Chiefs allowed 54 yards to running backs, but with the Broncos handing the ball off only 11 times, the sample size was small. Taylor is the Colts’ catalyst for offensive success, and the front seven and linebackers need to be ready to stop him. 3. 3rd down dominance The Chiefs defense dominated on crucial downs in Week 1, holding the Broncos to only two conversions over 12 third downs. That effort kept Denver from getting any offensive rhythm and helped the Chiefs hold them to three points in the second half. That was an R Mason Thomas third-down stop. Chiefs have been missing this type of player. — Pete Sweeney (@pgsween) September 15, 2026 The Colts struggled on third down in Week 1, converting only three in 10 attempts. The Chiefs secondary played outstanding in the opener, allowing only six total first downs through the air, and the revamped pass rush put consistent pressure on quarterback Bo Nix all game, sacking him four times and recording five total hits while consistently forcing him out of the pocket. Stopping third downs kills momentum, and the Chiefs emphasize this when looking to stop the Colts. 4. Starting fast In their Week 1 performance, the Colts trailed by three touchdowns with five minutes to play in the first half. On the other end, the Chiefs jumped up by two scores on the Broncos early in the second half and never looked back. HE'S BAAAAACK DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Ew5xE6qhMy — NFL (@NFL) September 15, 2026 Colts quarterback Daniel Jones struggled to get his team back in the game and posted a lowly 28.7 quarterback rating while throwing an interception and taking two sacks. The Colts lost wide receiver Michael Pittman this offseason, and now, No. 1 wide receiver Alex Pierce (Heel) is missing practice Thursday; he didn’t participate after practicing in full to begin this week. By jumping ahead early, they can force Indianapolis into passing situations and make Jones the player who beats them. On the other end, the bigger the lead the Chiefs build early, the more effective their running attack with Kenneth Walker will be later in the game. The Chiefs came out hot against the Broncos in Week 1, and if they can replicate that energy, they can put the Colts in a bind early. 5. Emmet Johnson While Kenneth Walker stole the show in week one, the Chiefs rookie running back quietly turned in a solid outing. While he rushed for only 24 yards on eight carries, Johnson showed his smooth open-field running and cutting ability on two screen passes for 44 yards. Stiff arm. Juke. Rookie Emmitt Johnson pulling out all the moves on this catch-and-run 😤 DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6kzvLoZHxJ — NFL (@NFL) September 15, 2026 Walker had 26 total touches in Week 1, so it will be interesting to see if his workload helps get the rookie more snaps. One elite back is great, but having another with the potential to be an impact-making player will only make the team stronger down the stretch.

title: Dave Toub hypes up the return of the fullback for the Chiefs
summary: In Week 1, the Kansas City Chiefs used a practice-squad elevation to add fullback Ben VanSumeren to the active roster for their 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos on Monday night. After being signed to the practice squad following cutdown day, VanSumeren played 79% of the team’s special teams snaps and saw the field on […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 1, the Kansas City Chiefs used a practice-squad elevation to add fullback Ben VanSumeren to the active roster for their 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos on Monday night. After being signed to the practice squad following cutdown day, VanSumeren played 79% of the team’s special teams snaps and saw the field on offense for three plays. On Wednesday, Kansas City signed him to the active roster after linebacker Cooper McDonald was placed on the Reserve/Injured list; he will miss a minimum of four games. Special teams coordinator Dave Toub described VanSumeren during his press conference on Thursday, building excitement for the return of the fullback . “The good thing about him is that he is a linebacker, really,” Toub told reporters. “He has a linebacker history in a fullback body. But he’s a fast guy; he runs in the [4.4-second range.] He’s a big guy, so he can really help you on special teams. That’s why we elevated him last week, and it’s why he is now on the 53.” Ben VanSumeren is up. 9.62 RAS coming out of Michigan state as a LB. Converted to FB last offseason before suffering a season-ending knee injury on the opening kickoff. Curious to see how much he's utilized, but he was used like this at times during preseason in 2025. https://t.co/zfqDM0EQbP pic.twitter.com/7AakRXC4Bb — HBTC (@hbtCHIEFS) September 14, 2026 As a linebacker prospect out of Michigan State in the 2023 NFL Draft class, VanSumeren was measured 6 feet 2 inches tall and 231 pounds at his Pro Day. He ran the 40-yard dash in 4.45 seconds with a 1.52-second 10-yard split. He had a 42-1/2 inch vertical leap and a 10-foot 11-inch broad jump. “He’s going to be a four-phase guy for us going forward,” Toub revealed. “I’m excited about that. Andy’s excited about having a fullback again, too. All of those things are helpful for our football team.” “He was a special teams guy before at both places, and a lot of the stuff is interchangeable,” Toub elaborated. “He just has to learn our terminology, but we catch him up really quick with a lot of reps.” Look for No. 47 on offense and special teams in Week 2; the more he — or defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga — is on the field with quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the more it represents the team’s turn to physicality this season.

title: Numbers Never Lie: 3 Chiefs stats and what they mean for this season
summary: Numbers never lie, right? There are so many statistics to parse through during the NFL season that some can be misleading. After each game, it’s a good exercise to review NFL “Next Gen Stats” and “Premium Stats” from Pro Football Focus and find the numbers that paint a picture not only of the game, but of what to expect […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos gets tackled after a reception against L'jarius Sneed #38 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Numbers never lie, right? There are so many statistics to parse through during the NFL season that some can be misleading. After each game, it’s a good exercise to review NFL “Next Gen Stats” and “Premium Stats” from Pro Football Focus and find the numbers that paint a picture not only of the game, but of what to expect from the Kansas City Chiefs moving forward. Here are three statistics from the Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos and what they could mean for the rest of the season: 1. The Chiefs generated pressure on 46% of dropbacks That was the fourth-highest rate of any NFL team in Week 1, looking up in the rankings at only the Baltimore Ravens , Minnesota Vikings and Philadelphia Eagles . It’s a good group to be in. The Chiefs blitzed on nearly one-third of the pass plays the team faced. However, when you take away those reps, Kansas City still generated pressure on 36% of pass plays. That ranked 10th among all NFL teams while rushing only four players. Last year, the Broncos allowed the fewest sacks (23) & 2nd-lowest team pressure rate (28%) in the NFL Chiefs got 4 sacks & 46% pressure rate Wk1 I've seen some of Spags' best pass-rush groups get swallowed up by a good OL at home… feeling good about this year's four-man rush — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) September 16, 2026 The reason this number has staying power is the opponent: the Broncos were the NFL’s best team at keeping quarterback Bo Nix off the turf and away from pressure last season. In Week 1, the Chiefs generated four sacks, while Denver allowed an average of 1.4 sacks per game last year. 2. The Chiefs’ offense faced 8 or more men in the box on 14 plays Only the Ravens and Las Vegas Raiders faced heavy, packed defensive formations more frequently than the Chiefs did in Week 1. The game script, especially in the fourth quarter, certainly helps explain the high number, but it also shows the gravity of running back Kenneth Walker (and rookie Emmett Johnson) when they run the ball as efficiently and explosively as they did on Monday night. The Chiefs averaged 7 yards per carry when the Broncos presented a light box to defend the run; as the game wore on, Denver needed to bring more players close to the line of scrimmage. As less-talented pass defenses are forced to respect the run this season, the Chiefs will have more opportunities to throw the ball behind crept-up linebackers and safeties. 3. L’Jarius Sneed had a league-leading 3 ‘Hustle Stops’ According to Next Gen Stats , a “Hustle Stop” is a tackle that results in negative EPA for the offense in which the defender covered 20 yards of in-play distance from snap to tackle. Sneed finished Week 1 tied for third-most solo tackles among all NFL players (7). If you thought the veteran cornerback, in his first year back with the Chiefs, was flying around against Denver, the numbers back it up. The Chiefs' outside cornerback trio of Mansoor Delane (1 drive), Nohl Williams & Kristian Fulton's combined stat line Week 1 (PFF) 9 targets – 4 catches 29 yards (Long completion: 9 yards) 1 INT + 1 PBU + No penalties — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) September 16, 2026 It’s a very encouraging sign for a pass defense that looked sharp on the outside. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane may have had only one drive to contribute, but the outside cornerback group — mostly Nohl Williams and Kristian Fulton — performed strongly against a talented receiving corps. The group forced five incompletions and committed no penalties. Sneed’s strengths as a player are centered on being physical. If Kansas City has the youth on the outside to match up with top receiving threats, Sneed will continue to simply be a playmaker out of the slot for the Chiefs.

summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ quarterback turns 31 years old today. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates after defeating the Denver Broncos in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ quarterback turns 31 years old today. It’s a reminder that the 31-10 Week 1 beatdown of the Denver Broncos may have just been the first chapter of the second half of Mahomes’ historic NFL career. There are plenty more pages to write. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Happy Birthday, Patrick Mahomes! See the Kansas City Chiefs Quarterback’s Family Photos with Wife Brittany and Their 3 Kids | People Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, are the proud parents of three little ones: Sterling Skye Mahomes, who they welcomed in February 2021, Patrick “Bronze” Lavone Mahomes, who arrived in November 2022 and newborn Golden Raye Mahomes, who was born in January 2025. Whether it’s dressing up for Halloween or taking trips to Disneyland, when the Kansas City quarterback is not busy on the field, he’s often spending quality time with his family. As Patrick turns 31 on Sept. 17, 2026, see the most adorable photos of the family of five. Ken Walker Earns AFC “Offensive Player of the Week” Honors | The Mothership Walker earned AFC “Offensive Player of the Week” honors for Week 1 after the veteran tailback amassed a career-high 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in Monday night’s victory over Denver. The reigning Super Bowl MVP recorded 179 yards after contact in the game, breaking a league-most 14 tackles along the way. He also ripped off two runs of 20+ yards in the game, nearly matching the Chiefs’ combined total number of runs as a team all of last year (3). How tackle Khyiris Tonga became Chiefs’ most versatile player in just one game | The Kansas City Star “I’m just here to do whatever I can,” Tonga said. Usually that will be playing in the middle of the defensive line. That’s where Tonga has played throughout his six-year career with four teams until signing with the Chiefs. Last season, playing for New England, Tonga took 14 offensive snaps. “I’d like to claim I brought him in to play fullback,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said. “We knew he had done that before.” Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Tom Brady Has Seen Enough: Patrick Mahomes Is Back To Being Himself | FOX Sports Mahomes didn’t have the strongest stat line in the Chiefs’ 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos on Monday night. He completed 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. But he also ran for a 15-yard score in the first quarter, making a vintage Mahomes-like play. “Patrick Mahomes, are you kidding me? He might be able to contribute something to this offense as well,” Brady said. He wasn’t avoiding any contact [on Monday night]; I’m sure of that. Why Kahlil Benson Deserves the Starting Right Tackle Job When Josh Simmons Returns | Sports Illustrated Aside from a first-quarter holding call that nullified a Mahomes touchdown run, Benson had no other major blemishes during his excellent debut. The 2026 national champion didn’t allow a single pressure in the first half and gave up just one in 32 pass-blocking snaps. Although Moore has seen more action at left tackle than the right side in his career, the Chiefs trusted Benson over him, and he couldn’t have done any better. His 3.2% pressure rate was the best among rookie offensive tackles in Week 1. Around the NFL Bengals’ Joe Burrow dealing with back tightness, expects to play vs. Texans | The Athletic “I feel good,” Burrow said. “Just normal game day soreness, that’s for sure, but I will be all right.” Burrow called the injury “back tightness.” As for the notion that he would sit out Sunday as a precaution, he didn’t hide his feelings. “That’s ridiculous,” Burrow said. Colts’ Keenan Allen formally charged, faces two misdemeanors | ESPN Allen, 34, was arrested by Indianapolis police on Aug. 30 and preliminarily charged. On Tuesday, prosecutors officially filed charges of operating a vehicle with alcohol concentration equivalent to .15 or more and operating a vehicle while intoxicated. According to a probable cause affidavit obtained by ESPN, Allen’s blood-alcohol level was tested at .224, triggering a more serious Class A misdemeanor charge per Indiana law. Operating while intoxicated is considered a Class C misdemeanor. Ryan Fitzpatrick: 0-17 season ‘within reach’ for 2026 Dolphins | NFL.com Before the season began, former Miami Dolphins quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick predicted the Fins could go 0-17 in 2026. After one week, he’s not scrambling away from that suggestion. On a promotional tour for Amazon Prime’s first Thursday Night Football game this week, the QB-turned-analyst doubled down in comments to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald. Fitzpatrick’s logic stems from Miami’s overhauled roster, thanks to deals given out by the previous front office. “Part of it is self-inflicted with all the dead money,” Fitzpatrick told Jackson. “They’ve got over $180 million in dead cap. Tua (Tagovailoa), Tyreek (Hill), Jaylen Waddle, (Bradley) Chubb, (Jalen) Ramsey, Minkah (Fitzpatrick) — all those guys that are on the books but not on the roster; that’s part of it.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride There’s a ‘pretty good chance’ Mansoor Delane is back for Chiefs in Week 2 In addition to the positive news about Delane, there was an unfortunate update on second-year linebacker Cooper McDonald. Last year’s rookie minicamp tryout signing has been placed on the Reserve/Injured list and will miss at least four games. He suffered a knee injury during Monday night’s game. Reid also said safety Chamarri Conner (Knee) and left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) would not practice Wednesday. summary: The Los Angeles Chargers should be preparing to play their Week 2 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders without wide receiver Ladd McConkey. full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Ladd McConkey #15 of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. His status for the game against the Raiders is very much in doubt. On top of McConkey sitting out of practice, defensive back Elijah Molden, offensive tackle Trey Pipkins III, and defensive lineman Dalvin Tomlinson were not seen on the practice field. Defensive lineman Teair Tart was limited with an ankle injury, while defensive back Deane Leonard was limited with an abdomen injury. With McConkey likely missing the game this week, the Chargers will rely on Quinton Johnston and second-year pro Trey Harris a little more than they normally would. The team elevated Gary Jennings and signed him to the active roster, while they also added Marquez Valdes-Scantling, a two-time Super Bowl champion, to the practice squad. For the Raiders, tight end Brock Bowers was not on the practice field because he underwent knee surgery last week. He was joined on the injury report by cornerback Darien Porter, who’s dealing with a foot injury, and third-string quarterback Aidan O’Connell, who missed practice due to personal reasons. Kickoff between the Raiders and Chargers is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 p.m. PT inside SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: Chargers face must-win game vs. Raiders in Week 2
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers did not expect to lose their season opener against the Arizona Cardinals, but they were on the wrong end of the upset alert. A 26-14 loss to one of the worst teams in the league in 2025 definitely has the Chargers feeling a sense of urgency going into Week 2 against […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Chargers did not expect to lose their season opener against the Arizona Cardinals, but they were on the wrong end of the upset alert. A 26-14 loss to one of the worst teams in the league in 2025 definitely has the Chargers feeling a sense of urgency going into Week 2 against the division rival Las Vegas Raiders, who were also one of the NFL’s cellar dwellers last year. A loss to the Raiders, who would be up two games in the divisional standings, could sink the Chargers before their schedule reaches its toughest stretch. “The Chargers are almost in a must-win situation with the schedule they face in the next six weeks. The loss last week at home to the Cardinals was embarrassing. The Raiders beat the Dolphins, but this is a big step up for them,“ CBS Sports contributor Pete Prisco wrote. Prisco believes the Chargers will bounce back at home and beat the Raiders 24-16. The Chargers definitely got a dose of reality after losing to the Cardinals. They won’t be able to coast against even the perceived weakest opponents in the league. After this week, Los Angeles faces seven consecutive games against teams that made the playoffs in either of the last two years. They will be competitive in those games, but a loss against the Raiders at home could get them off on the wrong foot, leading to a poor stretch of momentum against the meat of their schedule. BFTB community, do you view this week’s game as a must-win for the Chargers? Let us know in the comments section below.

Bleacher Report writer Kristopher Knox listed the Chargers as a potential landing spot for Tennessee Titans defensive lineman Solomon Thomas if he were to be traded. “The Tennessee Titans acquired Thomas in an offseason trade with the Dallas Cowboys. After getting blown out in Week 1, it’s hard to imagine Tennessee becoming playoff-relevant before then,” Knox wrote. “Thomas probably isn’t a starter at this stage of his career, but the 30-year-old recorded 27 tackles and three tackles for loss in a rotational role with Dallas last season.” Thomas entered the league as the third overall pick in the 2017 NFL draft out of Stanford, just two picks behind reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett, who was traded to the crosstown rival Los Angeles Rams earlier in the offseason. title: In absence of Myles Garrett, Rams look to Wesley Bailey
summary: Wesley Bailey was considered a better prospect in the CFL than the NFL, but less than six months after his name wasn’t called in the 2026 NFL draft, the edge rusher finds himself in a position to support the L.A. Rams in the absence of superstar Myles Garrett. The Rams placed Garrett on injury reserve […]
full_text: Wesley Bailey was considered a better prospect in the CFL than the NFL, but less than six months after his name wasn’t called in the 2026 NFL draft, the edge rusher finds himself in a position to support the L.A. Rams in the absence of superstar Myles Garrett. The Rams placed Garrett on injury reserve on Thursday, guaranteeing he will miss at least four games. There is no corresponding move on the roster yet, but the only help coming at edge rusher for Monday’s game against the New York Giants has to come from players already signed to the team. That includes Bailey, an undrafted free agent out of Louisville who Sean McVay called out as someone who the team would be counting on in the interim during his Monday appearance on the “Coach McVay Show” with J.B. Long. “He’s another guy that we’re going to be counting on,” McVay said. “Whether that’s making an impact on teams, whether that’s continuing to understand the roles and responsibilities dependent upon which grouping we’re in. Where is the role and responsibility that he’s playing? He’s another guy that’ll be asked to step up, for sure.” A standout in training camp, Wesley Bailey wasn’t drafted but he’s the Rams rookie most likely to have an impact this season. While Ty Simpson, Max Klare, and C.J. Daniels are likely to be healthy scratches this week (and third-round tackle Keagen Trost is on IR), Bailey is on track to potentially get his first snaps on defense against the Giants. Bailey played two special teams snaps in the Week 1 opener against the San Francisco 49ers. He may have to do more than just special teams work against the Giants. Wesley Bailey now becomes important. For a big guy, pretty quick, nice use of hands here, a club/swim then a double swipe to the outside, went around back of QB, but gap was left (IMO) by inside rushers. Not saying he can do this vs NFL starters, a TE and tackle, but nice anyway pic.twitter.com/8eSSczkuka — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) September 15, 2026 A hair under 6’5, weighing 260 lbs, Bailey posted impressive numbers at his pro day, including a broad jump over 10’ and a vertical of 35” with a 40-yard dash time of 4.69. A second round pick in the CFL Draft (Bailey is Canadian), Bailey spent six years in college with the first five at Rutgers and the final one at Louisville. He had 15.5 sacks during his college career but looked perhaps even more impressive during the 2026 preseason. That earned Bailey an unlikely spot on McVay’s 53-man roster and now he could do the improbable by helping L.A. keep their heads above water without the reigning DPOY. It probably won’t be a big role. The Rams still have Byron Young starting and Josaiah Stewart needing to step up for a bigger starting role in Week 2. Stewart had six tackles in Week 1. There’s also the presence of veteran Desjuan Johnson, as he played 15 snaps in Week 1. A call-up like Jamie Sheriff could happen too. There’s just not a lot of juice coming from L.A.‘s edge rusher unit as a whole, so maybe the added spark of Bailey could provide a boost that the Giants won’t see coming. Frankly, the loss of Garrett is one of the worst things that could have happened to the Rams, not just because he’s so good, but also because the room didn’t have any depth once Les Snead agreed to give up Jared Verse. Imagine how much easier this transition would feel with Verse. Instead, the team is looking to Wesley Bailey, among others. That’s intriguing, but not ideal.

title: Would a win over Giants really fix the Rams?
summary: Who are the 2026 Los Angeles Rams? Apparently not who we thought. LA was considered a “super team” and a historical Super Bowl favorite entering the year. They were blown out by the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Next to nothing went right for the Rams. The team’s second game—against the New York Giants […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who are the 2026 Los Angeles Rams? Apparently not who we thought. LA was considered a “super team” and a historical Super Bowl favorite entering the year. They were blown out by the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Next to nothing went right for the Rams. The team’s second game— against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football —is unlikely to bring many answers outside of potential confirmation that the Rams are on a downswing. A win would be positive but not overly noteworthy. A loss would send shockwaves across the NFL. Los Angeles opened as 8.5-point favorites over the Giants. The line is now closer to 7.5. In short, this is a game the Rams are expected to win . Victory doesn’t mean everything is OK and the team is back on track, although it would certainly be encouraging. The three games that follow New York will be more informative in terms of how the Rams stack up against other contenders: Week 3 at Denver Broncos Week 4 at Philadelphia Eagles Week 5 vs Buffalo Bills The Australia trip didn’t go as well as you wanted. It’s over. Beat the Giants . Show us your true colors against the Broncos, Eagles, and Bills. Then we can talk. In the meantime, these are the looming questions that we should track closely: Will Matthew Stafford bounce back, or are there long-term concerns? Only Bo Nix and Deshaun Watson were worse in Week 1. Can we chalk up Stafford’s bad game to a long Australia trip, or could the end of his career be approaching? How will the defense fare without Myles Garrett? I’d expect Desjuan Johnson to play on run downs. Josaiah Stewart will see a lot of run as a pass rusher and coverage changeup. Can LA get by for at least the next four weeks? What difference will Aaron Donald make, assuming he plays? If Donald participates against the Giants , will he look like his old self? Will a rising tide lift all boats across the defensive line? Can Rams get their money’s worth out of Jaylen Watson? Allowed two touchdowns in his first game as a Ram according to some outlets. He was brought in to limit bigger receiving targets and Mike Evans had his way against the defense. Are special teams really that much better? Deebo Samuel ripped off long returns in Australia. Special teams has cost Rams several games in recent seasons. Can they avoid disaster or will it be more of the same? Did the Rams err by doubling down on 13 personnel? LA’s passing game is less effective with three receivers . It’s also difficult to come from behind with heavier personnel on the field. Will we look back and say the Rams should have invested more in a third receiver over the offseason?
author: JB Scott

title: Giants’ run game will be a major test for the Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were poor across the board in Week 1, but especially against the run, nearly giving up 200 yards to the 49ers. With New York coming to town, the Giants’ running game will pose one of the tougher challenges to the Rams’ iffy run defense this season. In the 20-point season-opening loss, […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs the ball in the second quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams were poor across the board in Week 1, but especially against the run, nearly giving up 200 yards to the 49ers. With New York coming to town, the Giants’ running game will pose one of the tougher challenges to the Rams’ iffy run defense this season. In the 20-point season-opening loss, LA gave up the fourth-most rushing yards in the NFL at 174, behind the Panthers (291), Broncos (220) and Colts (202). While the defense didn’t give up a 100-yard rusher, they still allowed Niners running back Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to rush for at least 65 yards. Things must tighten up quickly, or the Rams risk being run out of their own stadium against an unexpectedly physical Giants attack. New York rushed for 165 yards against a supposedly improved Dallas defensive front, fifth-most in the league in Week 1. Second-year running back Cam Skattebo led the way with 81 yards on 18 carries. The offense also has plenty of mouths to feed at RB. Veteran Devin Singletary is closing in on 5,000 career rushing yards through his first seven seasons. Third-year back Tyrone Tracy Jr. is coming off back-to-back 740+ yard campaigns. The trio of Skattebo, Singletary and Tracy combined for 1,587 yards last season. That is remarkable production at its finest, and is exactly why the team finished fifth in rushing a year ago. How effective was their ground attack? NY currently has the lowest rate of runs stuffed in the NFL. The Giants violently barrel down people like they’re owed lunch money, which bodes well for the run game, proving so far that it ‘25 was no fluke, even with a different coaching staff. What’s crazier is that the unit could actually improve as the season progresses. Giants had the lowest rate of runs stuffed in the NFL in week 1. Talked about it on the mailbag but the run game is sustainable and has a higher ceiling than what we saw on SNF. Beautiful to see principles preached about the run game come into fruition. https://t.co/BW1gChP7Rn — Bobby Skinner (@BobbySkinner_) September 16, 2026 A powerful run game defines a John Harbaugh offense, dating back to his Ravens tenure. From 2008 to 2025, Baltimore averaged an NFL-leading 139.8 rushing yards per game, which was 10 yards more than the second-best team, according to the Giants team website . Additionally, the Ravens led the NFL in rushing yards five times in their last seven seasons, including 2019, 2020, 2023, 2024 and 2025. So, the G-Men will be running the ball plenty on Monday night. Now the question becomes whether the Rams can stop it when they know it’s coming. Run defense woes reared their ugly head in Week 1 The Rams had seemingly made strides against the run in 2025, but experienced lapses towards the end of the season. Los Angeles gave up eight 100-yard rushing games last season, which, overall, isn’t bad. However, five of those games came after the team’s bye, including the Falcons piling up a staggering 219 yards in Week 17. During LA’s 17-3 win over Harbaugh’s Ravens in October 2025, Baltimore racked up 179 yards on the ground, the second-most the Rams had given up after the Atlanta game. That total came without two-time MVP Lamar Jackson out of the lineup due to injury. Had Jackson played, the Ravens could’ve easily gone over 200 rushing yards. The bleeding didn’t exactly stop in the playoffs, even if LA had allowed one opponent to amass well over 100 team rushing yards (Bears, 160). In total, the Rams gave up 318 rushing yards and four touchdowns in three games. Between the regular season and playoffs, the team gave up 100-yard games in nearly half of its 20 games played. Two-thirds of that came after their bye alone. Clearly, the Rams have adjustments to make in their run defense, as they reverted to the inconsistent play that plagued them in the back half of last season. Knowing full well what Harbaugh and the Giants intend to do this week, LA must be better prepared than it was against the Niners, given that New York poses one of the tougher challenges to the Rams on the ground this season.
author: Evan Craig

title: Bills, Bears, and Jags beat Rams at their own game
summary: The Los Angeles Rams became so synonymous with 13 personnel in 2025 that using three tight ends practically became called “the Sean McVay style”, but in Week 1 the copycat league beat the Rams at their own game. The Rams ran 13 personnel on 36.8% of their plays against the 49ers last week, which is […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 13: Tight end Dalton Kincaid #86 of the Buffalo Bills screams after a first down reception during the NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Buffalo Bills on September 13, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX.(Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams became so synonymous with 13 personnel in 2025 that using three tight ends practically became called “the Sean McVay style”, but in Week 1 the copycat league beat the Rams at their own game. The Rams ran 13 personnel on 36.8% of their plays against the 49ers last week, which is higher than their league-leading rate in 2025, but not the highest rate of Week 1, as the Buffalo Bills called for the formation on 40.4% of their offensive plays. And the Bills were much more successful than the Rams, winning 36-31. In fact, teams that ran 13 personnel on at least 15% of their plays went 6-1 in Week 1; the single loss belonged to Sean McVay. Teams were in 13 personnel 8.1 percent of the time in Week 1, up from 4.5 percent in Week 1 a year ago. Teams who used it most often this week: Bills (40.4%) Rams (36.8%) Jags (17.9%) Jets (17.5%) Bears (15.7%) Ravens (15.6%) Cards (15.3%) — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) September 14, 2026 The Rams ran 13 personnel (three tight ends, one running back) on 30.8% of their plays in 2025, which was more than double the second-place rate of 13.1% of the Pittsburgh Steelers, and L.A. led the league in scoring at 30.5 points per game. The league-average was only 5.3%, putting the Rams at a rate six-times higher than a normal NFL offense. We could easily predict that the NFL would copy the Rams, and that was obviously the case in Week 1, nearly doubling the league average from Week 1 of 2025. What nobody predicted was that the Rams would be the only team in the league that failed to score 10 points in Week 1. Or the Matthew Stafford, his supporting cast, and McVay would all look so off of their games in losing 27-7 to the 49ers. This was the opposite of how L.A. looked in a 13 personnel-heavy offense in 2025, as detailed in this recent explainer video by Michael MacKlevie. Other 13 personnel teams Here’s how the other teams performed in Week 1: Bills (40.4%) Beat Texans 36-31 Rams (36.8%) Lost to 49ers 27-7 Jags (17.9%) Beat Browns 34-10 Jets (17.5%) Beat Titans 23-10 Bears (15.7%) Beat Panthers 59-37 Ravens (15.6%) Beat Colts 41-23 Cards (15.3%) Beat Chargers 26-14 With the exception of the Rams, every offense beat the pants off of their opponent in Week 1, even including Mike LaFleur’s Cardinals, just a year after leaving McVay’s 13 personnel scheme and taking it to Arizona. The Cardinals even have Hunter Long, a tight end who was on the Rams a couple of years ago. Many of these teams also have first-round tight ends: Dalton Kincaid, Kenyon Sadiq, and Colston Loveland, plus Trey McBride, a second-round tight end who is perhaps the best in the NFL now. The Rams have a lot of tight ends, but do they have a single one who is a top-tier receiving/blocking package at the position as of now? We also know that 13 personnel means leaving only one receiver on the field, suggesting you the offense might be sort of a “one-receiver” type offense: Puka Nacua, D.J. Moore, Parker Washington, Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, Michael Wilson. We may not see the Bengals run 13 personnel, for example. We should not expect Week 1 to deter McVay from using a heavy rate of 13 personnel, nor would these results from the other teams suggest that the rest of the NFL won’t consider increasing their rate of 13 in Week 1 — 59 points! 41 points! — but to what degree will the Rams adjust? They might have to copy the copycats.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams-Giants keys to victory: 3rd down success
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will look to bounce back in Week 2 when they face the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. For keys to victory in Week 1, I mentioned how the Rams needed to run, run, and run some more on offense. They ran the ball in the first half, but they […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will look to bounce back in Week 2 when they face the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. For keys to victory in Week 1 , I mentioned how the Rams needed to run, run, and run some more on offense. They ran the ball in the first half, but they didn’t stay committed to the running game in the second half. As for the defense, I stated that the unit needed to limit Christian McCaffrey. McCaffrey received a limited number of touches but when he touched the ball, he gained valuable yards. For Los Angeles, there are two areas that could ultimately determine whether the team moves to 1-1 or 0-2. Here are the offensive and defensive keys to victory for the Rams heading into Monday night’s matchup. Offensive Key to Victory: 3rd Down Success Earlier this week, I wrote about the Rams necessity to win on third down week-to-week. Well guess what, the best way for the offense to get on track is keeping the ball in its hands. If we want to see the 2025 version of Matthew Stafford, getting into a rhythm is vital. He will only be able to find that rhythm if the offense is moving the sticks. The Rams’ offense needs to make third down a strength rather than an obstacle. Defensive Key to Victory: Make the Giants a passing team New York demonstrated in Week 1 that it can control the game with a combination of efficient offense and a strong rushing attack. The Rams cannot take four quarters of physical bruising from Cam Skattebo and Patrick Ricard. The defensive line is also not created to take on those type of plays over and over. They are much more effective getting to pin their ears back and get after the quarterback. Jaxson Dart has made growth in Year 2 but he has yet to be tested and evaluated when his rushing attack is neutralized. The Rams defensive front must slow it down and test the second year quarterback.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Who faces more pressure in Week 2, Sean McVay or Chris Shula?
summary: I’d argue that the headline is a bit of a trick question, as both Sean McVay and Chris Shula need to get the Los Angeles Rams, and their respective units back on track after a disappointing showing against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Both are under tremendous pressure. Where was the complimentary football? […]
full_text: I’d argue that the headline is a bit of a trick question, as both Sean McVay and Chris Shula need to get the Los Angeles Rams, and their respective units back on track after a disappointing showing against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Both are under tremendous pressure. Where was the complimentary football? The first game of the year for the Rams didn’t start out all bad, they forced an interception and had a chance to add points before Matthew Stafford gave the ball back to the 49ers on a questionable throw. The defense tried, but failed to keep the Rams in the game as L.A.’s offense faltered, and faltered some more as the 49ers took advantage of their opportunities far more than the Rams did. You can blast Chris Shula, he deserves blame, but the offense wasn’t good either. The complimentary football McVay talked about so much last year wasn’t there consistently in Week 1. The pressure is on both McVay and Shula to turn things around. However, if we are being honest, one of those coaches has a much higher chance to lose their job than the other. McVay’s job shouldn’t be in jeopardy, but the pressure is on nonetheless to get this season on track. The Rams need to get right in Week 2, and it’s not just one side of the ball that needs to look better. Everything needs to look better against the New York Giants, or else the Rams may fall to 0-2. If you think the negative press this week was bad, just wait for an 0-2 start. Of course, the Rams can avoid that with a win, but they need to win, and winning in the NFL, is the hardest thing to do. Sean McVay addresses narrative that Rams didn’t play to their new CBs’ strengths (ramswire) “After the Rams added tremendous talent to their secondary , spending $175 million on contracts for Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, Los Angeles believes it has a secondary that could win championships for years to come. However, their defensive coordinator, Chris Shula, is being doubted after such a poor performance. Not only did the 49ers strike through the air, but they were also nearly unstoppable on the ground; San Francisco put up 379 yards of total offense, including 174 rushing. So, was the issue scheme, ability, both, or a mix in addition to other factors? Head coach Sean McVay addressed the issue with the secondary and the developing narrative that despite their corners excelling in man coverage, they were used as zone defenders in Melbourne.“ West Coast Read: Can Sean McVay Turn Rams’ Nightmare Into Expected Dream Team? (foxsports) “Since being anointed a super team this offseason, McVay has done his best to guard against complacency, tamping down talks of the Rams engineering a perfect season and hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in February for the second time in his head coaching career in the team’s home stadium. The Rams’ media onslaught crescendoed with an appearance on “60 Minutes” over the weekend. But after laying an egg on national television in the league’s first international game Down Under, McVay just wants to get things back to normal and win a game.“ Chris Shula will have to crank up the heat for Rams defense to survive (ramblinfan) “That’s especially true with Myles Garrett, an organic megasource of pass-rush pressure, on injured reserve. Having Aaron Donald back would help on the interior, but there’s no way Shula can repeat his passive strategy against the Giants on Monday and expect better results. Chris Shula needs to reimagine this Rams defense Shanahan’s dismantling of Shula and the Rams defense was a masterclass in exacting death by a thousand papercuts. Aside from one 39-yard bomb for former LA receiver DeMarcus Robinson, no play the 49ers called gained more than 18 yards – on a Brock Purdy scramble.“ Rams’ Matthew Stafford Breaks Silence After Bad News (heavy.com) “It’ll be a collective effort to kind of pick up where he is not there. But at the same time, we all just have to play a little bit better. Obviously, we can help on the offensive side of the ball, scoring points and doing the things that we’re supposed to do, too. Football is a great team game. This will be an opportunity for us to prove that for a few weeks now, as he’s recovering.” There are significant concerns about Garrett and his health, both over past instances and his future on the field.“ Rams’ Myles Garrett Receives Major Concern From Surgeon (sports.yahoo) “ Dr. Robert Klapper sat down with ABC7’s Curt Sandoval to speak about the concern that Garrett’s swelling is something that could be a problem. “If you are dealing with swelling over weeks and weeks, that tells you there is more of a chronic situation going on. Is it the meniscus? Yes, but how much has the cushion- the meniscus acted like sandpaper to irritate the cartilage in addition?” Dr. Klapper said. Garrett will undergo surgery, but that could potentially not be enough to fully heal the issues or irritation that Dr. Klapper is speaking about.“ Los Angeles Rams vs. New York Giants: How to watch, listen to and live stream Monday Night Football Week 2 (ramswire) “The Rams and Giants last met in Week 17 of the 2023 season on New Year’s Eve where the Rams won 26-25 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 317 yards and one touchdown, with two interceptions. Wide receiver Puka Nacua had a team-leading 118 receiving yards on five receptions. Running back Kyren Williams had 87 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. Defensively, defensive end Kobie Turner had five total tackles, including two for loss, and 2.5 sacks. Defensive end Aaron Donald also had five total tackles and two for loss, adding two sacks. Outside linebacker Byron Young had four total tackles, including two for loss, and one sack. title: 5Qs, 5As with Big Blue View: Will Jaxson Dart continue playing ‘unafraid’?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams look to rebound in Week 2 with a home date against the upstart New York Giants. New York is 1-0 under new head coach John Harbaugh, whose team appears to be a much tougher opponent than previously thought. Much of the Giants’ success in the season opener is due to second-year […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants directs his team during the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams look to rebound in Week 2 with a home date against the upstart New York Giants. New York is 1-0 under new head coach John Harbaugh, whose team appears to be a much tougher opponent than previously thought. Much of the Giants’ success in the season opener is due to second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart . The Ole Miss product looks to build on a promising start to his NFL career. This week, I spoke with Giants writer Ed Valentine from Big Blue View to learn more about Dart, the culture under Harbaugh and more. Q – The John Harbaugh era kicked off in style with a 28-20 win over the Cowboys on Sunday night. What are your early impressions of the Harbaugh era thus far, and how do you expect the Giants to fare in his first season? A – John Harbaugh is the right coach at the right time for the Giants. He has brought credibility and set a standard of expectation for everyone in the organization that the Giants badly needed. I think eight or nine wins is fair. Remember, this team won just seven games combined the last two seasons. Q – Jaxson Dart had an excellent game against Dallas in Week 1, throwing three touchdown passes and adding 54 rushing yards. What are his strengths and possible weaknesses that the Rams’ defense could exploit, even with Myles Garrett out? A – Dart is tough. He is unafraid. He is smart. He can make plays with his legs, and there is some magic when he is off-script. He is still a young quarterback, though, and he doesn’t always see everything correctly. Case in point: the sack/fumble Sunday when he was hit by Caleb Downs on a blitz. There was no blocker for Downs, and it was the QB’s responsibility to see that blitzer and get the ball out. Dart didn’t see it, and nearly turned the ball over. Q – New York played smashmouth football in the opener, rushing for 165 yards and a touchdown on 37 carries. If you were Chris Shula, how would you limit the damage of the Giants’ physical rushing attack? A – First of all, tell his guys to buckle. The Giants will be physical. They come at you with a 300-pound fullback, a running back who lives to run through people, and an attitude that they will run the football and win the line of scrimmage. The Giants did what they wanted offensively against the Cowboys. They ran it when they wanted to. They threw it when they wanted to. I think teams will eventually opt to crowd the line of scrimmage. Q – Who are some offensive standouts LA fans should keep an eye on this week? What about on defense? A – Offense — If you watched on Sunday, you know how important tight end Isaiah Likely is for Dart. He is what I call the “gotta have it” guy. That’s where Dart wants to go when the Giants have to have a play. I’m curious if RB Najee Harris has a role after being inactive in Week 1. And, of course, there is a guy named Beckham who did not get a target in Week 1. I think that will change on Monday. Defense — Arvell Reese, the No. 5 overall pick in the draft, had a quiet game against the Cowboys. He won’t be quiet forever. I also think Abdul Carter, last year’s No. 3 overall pick, is going to have a huge season. Q – The Giants are 7.5-point underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook . What is your prediction for this game? A – I think the Rams win, but this Giants team is no pushover. As I answer this, the line is 7.5. I’d take the Giants with the points.

title: Raiders Week 1: Special teams returns to form in win over Dolphins
summary: How do you know a season has truly gone awry for the Las Vegas Raiders? When even special teams flounders. Such was the case during a disastrous 2025 campaign. Naturally, when the Klint Kubiak era of the Silver & Black descended upon us, my curiosity piqued at the new head coach’s eventual special teams coordinator […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images How do you know a season has truly gone awry for the Las Vegas Raiders? When even special teams flounders. Such was the case during a disastrous 2025 campaign. Naturally, when the Klint Kubiak era of the Silver & Black descended upon us, my curiosity piqued at the new head coach’s eventual special teams coordinator hire and how the Raiders would reverse course in 2026. And after one game into the new campaign, there’s most definitely encouraging signs. New special teams boss Joe DeCamillis had the Silver & Black returning to form in the return, kick, and punt game and while the coverage units have areas of opportunity, a pure-hustle play by recently signed wide receiver Cody White to run down and stymie a would-be kick return touchdown, saved the day in Las Vegas’ impressive 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins this past Sunday. . @Raiders WR Cody White earned that game ball after he made a game-changing play on special teams 🗣️ @insidetheNFL Week 1 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/ve4UaZgSNV — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 Game Ball Worthy Sometimes, a team’s late-addition to the backend of the roster can make a significant impact. Such is the case for White, a wideout by trade but more of a special teamer, who signed to the Raiders practice squad back on August 31. A gameday practice squad elevation — alongside tight end Chris Myarick the day before the Week 1 opener — the 6-foot-3 and 227-pound undrafted free agent out of Michigan State is another Seattle Seahawks import, alongside fellow wide receiver and special teamer Dareke Young. And what a fortuitous decision to bring the 27-year-old from the taxi squad and active against the Dolphins as he showcased true grit on a Raiders kickoff coverage miscue as Miami running back Jaylen Wright made people whiff on a would-be touchdown return. Instead, White ran down Wright and limited the speedy return man to just a 79-yard return. Instead of becoming a 27-20 ball game, Las Vegas defense stood its ground and all Miami got out of the drive was negative five yards on four plays and a missed field goal. Lane discipline is an area of opportunity for DeCamillis’ units as the Raiders embark on the rest of the 2026 campaign, but watching a bigger receiver who clocked a 4.66-second 40-yard dash run down a tailback that ran a 4.38 40 was impressive. Las Vegas Raiders: Dylan Laube hits the turbo button on 50-yard kick return https://t.co/4gFj3L0AvP — McRaider (@McT228) September 13, 2026 Net Returns Speaking of lane discipline, that was one of the call outs Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley had when asked about the team’s kick and punt return woes against Las Vegas in the season opener. A pair of Raiders took advantage of this providing the Silver & Black solid field position for Kubiak’s offense in running back Dylan Laube and rookie wide receiver Malik Benson. Benson’s 23-yard punt return after Las Vegas defense forced Miami to put during its second drive slashed the Dolphins 59-yard punt. And nine plays and 38 yards later, the Raiders generated a 10-0 advantage. Then, it was Laube’s turn to dazzle after Miami responded with a field goal of its own to make it 10-3 in the second quarter. The reserve running back and core special teamer sprinted 45 yards on the ensuing kick off which put Kubiak’s offense in prime position to operate and seven plays and 54 yards later, quarterback Kirk Cousins found running back Ashton Jeanty for a 13-yard touchdown, 17-3 Raiders. Laube wasn’t done as he ripped a 50-yard kick return on Las Vegas’ second possession of the second half helping the team respond to Miami’s touchdown drive that cut the lead to 17-13. In an interesting coincidence, Laube’s big return also netted a Raiders touchdown — another 13-yard touchdown reception by Jeanty from Cousins. In total, Laube generated 95 yards on his pair of kick returns while Benson posted 35 yards on his two punt returns. Continuing to get this kind of production — alongside a return for touchdown at some point — helps bolster Kubiak’s Raiders in what’s expected to be a grueling 2026 slate of games. Former NC State punter AJ Cole impressed in the Raiders’ 27-13 win over the Dolphins: 3 punts 190 total yards (63.3 avg.) Long of 72 yards 1 punt downed at the 3-yard line pic.twitter.com/ZoMr3EIHAW — Noah Fleischman (@fleischman_noah) September 13, 2026 Boom-bastic When FOX Sports analyst Mark Schlereth openly calls AJ Cole III the best punter in the NFL, it’s hard to argue. The 30-year-old that stands 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds uses every bit of his angular frame as he produced an absurd state line in Sunday’s win: Three punts for 190 yards with a long of 72 yards. After one game in the books, Cole stands atop the league punting mountain with his 63.3 yards per punt average (the Kansas City Chief’s Matt Araiza and Buffalo Bills’ Tommy Doman are tied for second at 54.5 yards per boot). Whether it’s power, direction, touch, and hang time, Cole put on a show. And Las Vegas is likely set to rely on their elite punter to flip the field this season — despite getting the call only three times in the opener. His kicking battery mate — veteran kicker Matt Gay — drilled both of his field goal opportunities with the longest boot a 47-yarder. In between the Raiders punter and kicker duo is longsnapper Alex Ward who showcased accurate zip on his snaps which Cole is the recipient — as both punter and holder on Gay’s field goals. Sunday’s broadcast featured an illegal snap by Ward, but that appeared to be done on purpose to give Cole more room to boom and the Raiders punter and coverage units responded by pinning Miami’s offense deep downing the 55-yard punt on the Dolphins one-yard line. Quote of Note: “Dylan’s a hard worker, Dylan’s intelligent, football is important to him, little things are important to him, and that showed up in the return unit game, and then when he played on offense. So, I think it’s great for anyone that’s in a special teams role that’s maybe playing a backup position, but they know they can affect the game on teams, and that’s what he did for us yesterday.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on running back and special teamer Dylan Laube this past Monday Point After If you’re curious why I have an affinty for special teams, this is a major reason why: When peoples ask me why I love special teams. This is why: https://t.co/0R7JdEWCJ5 — Ray Aspuria (@AsukalAspuria) September 13, 2026
