title: Ashton Jeanty-Daiyan Henley headline Las Vegas Raiders-Los Angeles Chargers Week 2 key matchups
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers came into the 2026 season with very different expectations, with the Raiders considered to be rebuilding while the Chargers are anticipated to be contenders. However, the two clubs had very different results in Week 1, with Las Vegas beating the Miami Dolphins by 14 points and Los […]
full_text: (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers came into the 2026 season with very different expectations, with the Raiders considered to be rebuilding while the Chargers are anticipated to be contenders. However, the two clubs had very different results in Week 1, with Las Vegas beating the Miami Dolphins by 14 points and Los Angeles falling to the Arizona Cardinals by 12. That raises the stakes for this Week 2 contest for these AFC West foes, as the Raiders have a chance to turn some heads if they can win the key matchups below. Jeanty vs. Henley With Brock Bowers out last week, Ashton Jeanty became the focal point of Klint Kubiak’s offense and had one of his best games as a pro. Not only was Jeanty the team’s leading rusher with 23 carries for 102 yards (4.4 ypc) , but he also hauled in six catches for 45 receiving yards and a pair of scores to be the Raiders’ top receiver. With Bowers’ status up in the air at the time of writing, expect that trend to continue. Kubiak used the running back in a variety of ways against the Dolphins, splitting him out wide and even putting him at fullback or tight end for a handful of snaps. That’s similar to what the former Seattle Seahawks’ offensive coordinator did with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba last year. Obviously, the two players have different natural positions, but the point is that the coach likes to find a variety of ways to get his best player the ball. So, expect to see Jeanty lining up all over the Raiders’ offense on Sunday, and it wouldn’t be surprising if the Chargers’ best linebacker, Daiyan Henley, shadows him. Over the last couple of years, Henley has established himself as an up-and-coming linebacker in the league, logging triple-digit tackles in back-to-back campaigns. Diving deeper, he’s more than just a volume tackler with 74 ‘ defensive stops ’ in the 2024 and 2025 regular seasons combined, per Pro Football Focus . The former college wide receiver is also an impressive athlete who can make plays in coverage. He’s notched 13 passes defended and three interceptions during the two-year window mentioned above. However, Henley is susceptible to giving up completions and yards, yielding an 81.3 completion percentage and 574 yards last year, per PFF . The latter was the ninth-most among linebackers, and he gave up three completions on three targets for 28 yards (9.3 ypc) in Week 1. Additionally, Jeanty is known for his ability to make defenders miss, ranking fifth among running backs with 61 missed tackles forced as a rusher and tied for sixth with 23 as a receiver in 2025. Meanwhile, Henley had just eight missed tackles and was 20th among linebackers (minimum 229 snaps) with a 7.9 miss rate during the 2025 regular season. Henley and the Chargers were able to limit Jeanty to about 50 yards per game in the two contests last season, but that was without Kubiak calling the plays. Expect this to be the big prize fight on Sunday. Crosby vs. Alt It’s no secret that Maxx Crosby is the Raiders’ best pass-rusher. The season opener served as more evidence of that, as he recorded 1.5 sacks and had eight pressures, according to PFF . The latter tied teammate Kwity Paye for third among edge defenders, and Crosby’s 33.3 win percentage topped the charts. For reference, Paye was at 9.5 percent to settle the competition between Vegas’ rushers. What’s interesting about the five-time Pro Bowler’s production last Sunday was that 40 of his 45 total snaps came as left defensive end or left outside linebacker, meaning he was consistently lined up on the right side of the offensive line. That sets up for plenty of one-on-one battles between Crosby and Joe Alt. While the Chargers have issues on the offensive line, that’s entirely on the interior. Left tackle Rashawn Slater and right tackle Alt are excellent bookends who both excel in pass protection. For context, the latter is entering his third season and has yielded just 31 pressures on 815 opportunities in his career, per PFF . Los Angeles had plenty of issues in the trenches last week with quarterback Justin Herbert getting sacked three times, but the 2024 first-round pick wasn’t part of the problem, pitching a shutout as a pass blocker. Crosby and Alt have seen each other before, but it’s been a couple of years. Alt battled injuries last season and only played in the first contest against the Raiders, lining up at left tackle after Slater suffered a season-ending injury in training camp. Meanwhile, Crosby only spent 10 out of 57 snaps on the right side of the defensive line (offense’s left) in that contest. However, when the Notre Dame product made his NFL debut two years ago, he yielded just one pressure against the Raiders/Crosby, with the pass-rusher taking 32 of 57 snaps as a left end or outside backer. Crosby was on injured reserve during the second matchup that year. That sets up for a noteworthy battle in the trenches. Johnson vs. McConkey For clarity, Ladd McConkey suffered a rib injury in Week 1 and is questionable for Sunday at the time of writing. But if he is on the field, the wideout should be the Raiders’ primary focus defensively. In a contest where almost nothing was working for the Chargers’ offense last week, McConkey provided a glimmer of hope moving forward. He caught five passes for 82 yards and a touchdown before taking a hit that led to a rib injury and knocked him out of the game in the third quarter. That resulted in one of the most efficient outings for a wide receiver, as the third-year pro had the sixth-best yards per route run (4.56) among receivers with at least two targets, per PFF . McConkey’s usage and production during the season opener were interesting. He spent 70 percent of pass snaps in the slot but recorded just two catches for 22 yards when lining up inside, according to PFF . His touchdown grab was from the slot; however, less than 30 percent of his yards came from that alignment. That being said, expect Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel to test Raiders nickelback Taron Johnson with McConkey if the wideout plays. Johnson has a second-team All-Pro bid on his resume and is a physical defender at the apex of Las Vegas’ defense. However, the nine-year veteran’s coverage skills haven’t been the same since he suffered an injury a couple of years ago. That showed up in the season opener when he was beaten in man coverage by Dolphins rookie receiver Caleb Douglas for a 30-yard catch. To be fair, Johnson was targeted two other times, giving up one catch for a loss of a yard and the other was an incompletion. However, the other end of that is the incompletion was a drop that would have resulted in a first down. So, if Las Vegas wants to slow down the only aspect of Los Angeles’ offense that was working last week, the nickelback has to be tighter in coverage. Raiders OTs vs. Chargers EDGEs Defensively, Los Angeles has a trio of intriguing edge rushers with Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu and Akheem Mesidor. Mack isn’t nearly the same caliber of player he used to be, but he can still turn speed to power on the edge, collecting 39 pressures and 5.5 sacks on just 264 pass-rush snaps last year, per PFF . Tuipulotu is the up-and-comer who has a diverse pass-rush arsenal and is coming off a career year with 13 sacks and 70 pressures on 422 opportunities. Then there’s the rookie, Mesidor, who isn’t a typical first-year pro. The 25-year-old had a quiet NFL debut last week with just one pressure and no sacks last week. However, he should be able to bounce back quickly since his age and extensive college experience can help ease the transition to the league. Coached by Hall of Fame pass-rusher Jason Taylor at the University of Miami, Mesidor had the best hand usage of any edge prospect in last year’s class, which was evident during his 12.5-sack performance in 2025. Meanwhile, Las Vegas’ offensive tackle duo is coming off an excellent…

title: Miami Dolphins vs San Francisco 49ers injury report Week 2 2026 includes downgrade
summary: The Miami Dolphins’ Week 2 injury report is a little more impactful than the report they had heading into last week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders when everyone finished the practice week available for the game. This week, as the Dolphins prepare to face the San Francisco 49ers, Miami may find themselves without key […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson (44) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins’ Week 2 injury report is a little more impactful than the report they had heading into last week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders when everyone finished the practice week available for the game. This week, as the Dolphins prepare to face the San Francisco 49ers, Miami may find themselves without key players. Linebacker Ronnie Harrison, who played nearly half of Miami’s special teams snaps against the Raiders, remained sidelined at Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout as well. He is dealing with a hamstring injury. Edge rusher Chop Robinson was also out of Thursday practice as he deals with a concussion. He was a limited participant on Wednesday, marking a downgrade in his status and bringing his availability for Sunday into question. Long snapper Tucker Addington, who sustained a shoulder injury against the Raiders, and rookie tight end Seydou Traore, dealing with thumb and Achilles injuries, were both limited in Thursday’s practice. That matched their participation status from Wednesday. Safety Dante Trader, Jr., and quarterback Malik Willis were both listed on the injury report but participated fully in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. Trader is dealing with a hamstring issue, while Willis has a toe problem. The 49ers’ side of the injury report included kicker Eddy Pineiro and wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling missing practice Thursday. They both also did not workout on Wednesday. Pineiro has an illness while Stribling has an ankle injury. Running back Kaelon Black, defensive end Nick Bosa, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle, and defensive end Keion White were all limited on Thursday. Black was added to the injury report with a groin issue. Bosa returned to practice after a rest day on Wednesday, but is also dealing with a knee injury. Juszczyk has a finger issue, while Kittle has an Achilles injury and White has a back issue; all three were also limited on Wednesday. San Francisco listed linebacker Dre Greenlaw, defensive end Khalid Kareem, running back Christian McCaffrey, cornerback Upton Stout, and tackle Trent Williams as full participants at Thursday’s practice. Greenlaw, McCaffrey, and Williams all returned from a rest day on Wednesday; Greenlaw is also dealing with an Achilles issue. Kareem is an upgrade from being limited on Wednesday as he works through a shoulder injury while Stout remained a full participant despite an Achilles issue. Both teams will update their injury reports on Friday, providing a game status designation. The biggest question for Miami will be the availability of Robinson, who is the top edge rusher on the Dolphins’ depth chart.

title: Miami Dolphins 2026 salary cap move is unprecedented
summary: It’s well documented that a large portion of the Miami Dolphins’ 2026 salary cap is going toward multiple players who are no longer on the team. Tua Tagovailoa is costing more than $50 million in actual cash and will count $55.4 million on the cap. Tyreek Hill ($28 million), Jaylen Waddle ($23 million), Jalen Ramsey […]
full_text: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 05: Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Miami Dolphins passes to Tyreek Hill #10 of the Miami Dolphins in the first quarter during the NFL match between Miami Dolphins and Kansas City Chiefs at Deutsche Bank Park on November 05, 2023 in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s well documented that a large portion of the Miami Dolphins’ 2026 salary cap is going toward multiple players who are no longer on the team. Tua Tagovailoa is costing more than $50 million in actual cash and will count $55.4 million on the cap. Tyreek Hill ($28 million), Jaylen Waddle ($23 million), Jalen Ramsey ($21 million), Minkah Fitzpatrick ($13 million), Bradley Chubb ($11 million), and Terron Armstrong (11 million) all have cap hits north of $10 million and aren’t on the roster. Because of these massive cap hits for players off the roster, the Dolphins have needed to do some gymnastics to get under the salary cap and create space in order to sign injury replacements during the season. According to Jason Fitzgerald at Over the Cap, the Miami Dolphins may be the first team in NFL history to restructure every single contract they were able to restructure. “The Dolphins did four minor restructures to save about $2.516 million in cap room this year,” said Fitzgerald. “They now have $9 million in cap room. I believe they have no players remaining on the roster to save any cap room as those were the only players left with any savings. The restructures were as low as $340,000.” Typically, restructures involve multi-million-dollar contracts. The reason some contracts can’t be restructured is that they are already making the NFL league minimum for their years of service. How does an NFL contract restructure work? An NFL contract restructure works because the Collective Bargaining Agreement allows you to spread out signing bonuses up to five years. The team converts as much of the player’s base salary as possible to signing bonus. Now only 20% of that cap hit will count in the current year. Here’s an example using round numbers. Player X is scheduled to make $6 million in 2026. The team would pay him $5 million up front leaving him with a minimum salary of $1 million. Then that $5 million is spread out evenly over five years on the cap at $1 million per season. Instead of the player counting $6 million on the cap, they would only count $2 million with $4 million still to be accounted for in future years. The bill always comes due — every cent that is paid is eventually accounted for — but as the salary cap goes up every year (except during COVID), you’re planning on spending that increase before it happens. When a player leave the team via trade, retirement, or release, the remaining dead cap accelerates. That’s what happened with most of the players we mentioned in the first paragraph of the article. Think of it as maxing out the credit card but without the compounding interest. You’ve pushed as much current and past spending into the future as you possibly could. Why would the Dolphins restructure so many contracts now? Like every NFL team, the Dolphins need some wiggle room during the season. You can’t restructure the contracts for as much space during the season once salary has started to be paid. If an injury pops up and you need a million bucks to sign a replacement, you wouldn’t be able to create that space. Most teams like to have $15 million in reserve heading into the season. Miami maxed out everything to get to $9 million. That way they can add a few players down the line. Eleven NFL teams have less cap space than Miami, but this gives the Dolphins the chance to potentially claim some players during the season that are cast off from their existing teams with their existing contracts as they build for the future.

title: Vikes Views: Who Ya Got? Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears
summary: The Minnesota Vikings travel to the unfriendly confines of Soldier Field for Week 2. The Vikings roll into Chicago riding high after destroying the Green Bay Packers in the 4th quarter last week. However, the Bears (at least the offense) had a great time Week 1 against the Panthers. They went on the road to […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 16: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings eludes Noah Sewell #44 of the Chicago Bears during the second half of an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings travel to the unfriendly confines of Soldier Field for Week 2. The Vikings roll into Chicago riding high after destroying the Green Bay Packers in the 4th quarter last week. However, the Bears (at least the offense) had a great time Week 1 against the Panthers. They went on the road to Carolina and came away with a 59-37 scorigami win. Series Record: 69-59-2 Road Record: Streak: L1 Largest Victory: 31-0, 1969 Largest Defeat: 38-7, 1989 The Vikings have faced the Bears more than any other team in the league. The team’s first ever game was against the Bears in 1961. The Vikings stunned the Bears 37-13. The Vikings have won seven of their last ten trips to Soldier Field. Kevin O’Connell’s teams are 4-1 at Soldier Field, with the lone loss a 12-10 defeat in 2023, thanks to four interceptions from the Passtronaught. KOC is 6-2 overall against Chicago The Vikings have scored 27 or more points in four of their last five road games against the Bears. Justin Jefferson hasn’t had a 100 yard game in Chicago since his rookie year in 2020. The Vikings haven’t intercepted Caleb Williams…yet. However, he’s 1-3 against the Vikings in his young career. This one is a little harder for me to pick than last week’s game. The Vikings defense dominated the fourth quarter against Green Bay, but the offense struggled until it was given several short fields to work with. The Bears are coming off a dominant offensive performance, although their defense left plenty to be desired. Chicago steamrolled Carolina on the ground, rushing for 291 yards as a team. D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both topped 100 yards while Caleb Williams added another 65 yards and a score with his legs. The group combined for six rushing touchdowns. The Vikings defense is not the Carolina defense, however. Sunday’s matchup feels like strength versus strength. If Minnesota can slow down the running game and force Williams into obvious passing situations, they’ll have a chance to steal one on the road. As always, the turnover battle looms large. Right now, I have a little more faith in Caleb Williams protecting the football than I do Carson Wentz. Bears 24 – Vikings 21

title: Vikings-Bears Second Injury Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears released their second injury reports this week in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Soldier Field. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Chicago Bears Injury Report Terms and Glossary Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears released their second injury reports this week in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Soldier Field. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason RB Thumb DNP DNP IR-OUT Blake Cashman* LB Wrist LP FP Jauan Jennings WR NIR DNP DNP Kyler Murray* QB Concussion LP LP Andrew Van Ginkel* OLB Chest LP LP Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP DNP Chicago Bears Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Coby Bryant* S Knee DNP DNP IR-OUT Neville Gallimore DT Illness DNP FP Grady Jarrett* DT NIR-Rest DNP FP Darnell Wright* RT Knee DNP LP Kyle Monangai RB Hamstring LP LP Malik Mohammad* DB Ankle LP LP Dayo Odeyingbo* DE Shoulder LP LP D’Andre Swift* RB Ankle/Knee LP LP Ozzy Trapilo* LT Knee LP LP Xavier Woods DB Groin LP LP Joe Thuney* LG NIR-Rest — DNP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Bears, starting right tackle Darnell Wright did not practice due to a knee injury, which appears to be a new injury after the Panthers game in which he played every snap. No details on the severity, but Wright not being able to go on Sunday would be a significant loss for the Bears as he is arguably their best offensive lineman. Wright was upgraded to limited in Thursday’s practice which suggests he’s likely on track to play on Sunday. Ozzy Trapilo is working his way back from a torn patellar tendon injury and is likely to start at left tackle when he is ready. Unclear if he’ll be ready to return this week, however. Both Bears running backs were limited in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practice. I don’t think at this point either will not play on Sunday, but depending on the severity of their injuries, they could be less than 100% on the field. Hamstring injuries can be tricky injuries that can sometimes require rest even if they don’t seem severe to prevent a worsening condition. There is no reason to believe the other players on the list for the Bears will be unable to go on Sunday, as Gallimore and Jarrett were upgraded to full participation in Thursday’s practice. Joe Thuney had a veteran rest day on Thursday. For the Vikings, the news of the day is Jordan Mason going on short-term IR for a broken thumb, which will sideline him for four games. That is a significant loss. Deejay Dallas is being promoted to the active roster in a corresponding move. He appears to be ahead of Demond Claiborne at this point on the depth chart. The other news is Kyler Murray being limited after suffering a concussion early in the Packers game. Reports from coaches are that he hasn’t been suffering any lingering symptoms so there is a chance he could play against the Bears on Sunday. There is a protocol that needs to be followed, but it seems his chances of playing on Sunday look more promising than they did earlier in the week. Murray was shown taking snaps in Thursday’s practice, which might suggest he’s at stage four of the concussion protocol, which includes participation in non-contact football-related team activities. If that’s the case, Murray would just need to pass final evaluations by team doctors and the independent neurologist to be cleared to play on Sunday. We’ll see. On Thursday Blake Cashman was upgraded to full participation in practice and it would seem unlikely he’ll go into Sunday’s game with an injury designation. Brian O’Neill, on the other hand, did not participate in Thursday’s practice, which raises some questions about his availability on Sunday. We’ll see what clarity the final injury report tomorrow brings. Jauan Jennings missed another day of practice as he deals with a personal family matter. Lastly, Andrew Van Ginkel was limited again in Thursday’s practice with a chest issue. There hasn’t been any talk of this being a serious issue so my guess is this is just something he plays through rather than something that keeps him out. We’ll see what insight tomorrow’s report brings. Stay tuned. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Patriots mailbag: Will the Steelers follow the blueprint against Drake Maye?
summary: It’s been a long wait in between the New England Patriots season-opening loss and their home opener on Sunday, where they will look to get into the win column against the Pittsburgh Steelers. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What happened to the deep-ball/explosive-play game vs. Seattle? My impression was that Seattle did […]
full_text: It’s been a long wait in between the New England Patriots season-opening loss and their home opener on Sunday, where they will look to get into the win column against the Pittsburgh Steelers. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What happened to the deep-ball/explosive-play game vs. Seattle? My impression was that Seattle did a really good job taking away the deep ball, and I’ve seen some All-22 guys say the same. Is that what you saw, or was Maye also missing open guys? If so, why? More broadly, I suspect we’ll see a lot more teams try to replicate Seattle’s approach against Maye/Pats. Which upcoming opponents are best equipped to do it? My understanding of Seattle’s formula is four-man pressure/stunts + strong run defense despite the light front, versatile second-level defenders, and especially split-safety/quarters-Cover 6 structures designed to take away explosives, with CBs good enough to hold up. Pittsburgh has the pass rush. Can they replicate the other pieces of Seattle’s formula that gave Maye problems? – Maye The Force Be With You This is now the blueprint against Drake Maye: Take away the deep ball and force him to take the profits underneath in order to string together long drives. In last year’s playoffs, teams played two-high safeties against Maye 51% of the time. Against Seattle on Wednesday night, the quarterback faced split-safety coverages at a 57% clip. For three quarters, Maye played the effective but rather boring brand of football he needed to, living in the underneath area of the field to build a 10-0 lead. Then, he admittedly lost his patience and started throwing downfield, which led to three interceptions and a blown lead. “You can’t get bored taking what they give you, and that goes for everybody,” Mike Vrabel said. As Vrabel said, beating these defenses moving forward will start with Maye being comfortable playing boring football. The Patriots also need to straight-up run the football better against lighter boxes, which would force defenses to move the second safety down into the box and open things up downfield for Maye. They’ll get an immediate test again with the Steelers, as they played every dropback in zone in Week 1 while defensive coordinator Patrick Graham ran a similar strategy against the Patriots last season when he was with the Raiders. Who takes Brown role while he’s out – XGhost-PepperX There isn’t a 1-for-1 replacement when it comes to a player like A.J. Brown. It will be a group effort, with the Patriots utilizing multiple players and their versatility. The biggest two are Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins. From a production standpoint, Doubs simply needs to be better than his debut in Week 1 (0 catches, 3 targets), while Hollins has already proven his chemistry with Drake Maye. From a skill-set standpoint, both players have the ability to play Brown’s primary X spot, with the other working off of them at the Z spot. Hollins filling in at the X spot could also open the door for Efton Chism III to see the field in a blocking role. Behind them, Kyle Williams will factor more into the mix due to his ability to play on the outside as well. The Patriots’ offense needs an injection of Williams’ speed, especially now in Brown’s absence. When Gonzalez covered JSN, he had 1 catch for 5 yards; not covered by CG? 7 receptions for 117 yards & a TD. Even without the 45 yard TD, it was 6 receptions for 72. Should CG have been on JSN more, especially given that Drew Lock focused on JSN for half of his passes and 2/3rds of his yards? – PatsFanFromNH Having your No. 1 cornerback follow the opposition’s No. 1 wide receiver all game sounds nice in theory. But it’s much more difficult to execute. Beyond tipping your hand when you’re playing man coverage by having Gonzalez follow JSN across the formation, there is a domino effect in zone coverages when moving your secondary around. Gonzalez would then need to know the zone assignments from wherever he ends up on the field, which would force the other defensive backs to play in different spots and then adjust based on the original movement. That creates a tall task for everyone when playing a team like Seattle, which moves JSN around the offense quite a bit. Perhaps it’s more doable against a team like Pittsburgh this week, which largely staples D.K. Metcalf to the outside. Do we think Maye’s shoulder injury is 100% healed? In Week 1, a lot of his deep attempts came out like ducks very similar to how they did in last year’s playoffs. The flea flicker to Brown was particularly egregious – Brown had him beat by a decent margin and that ball was significantly under thrown. Even some of the shorter throws to check downs in the flat came out pretty weak. – Prontocosmo215 Any noticable change to Maye’s throwing mechanics from last year regular season, to post season, to week one this season? Obviously there’s injury claims floating around – Leoa888 I believe he’s healthy and have noticed nothing on the mechanics. I think the biggest issues for the velocity was just Maye playing his first game in seven months and a lack of decisiveness on some of the throws. The flea flicker falls more in the bucket of timing, as Brown takes off downfield before Stevenson flips the ball back to Maye, who then is rushed and does not want to overthrow Brown as the receiver is running out of room vertically. Hey Brian. Do you think we see a more even distribution of snaps with the running backs this week, considering Henderson seems to be trending towards playing and Rhamondre’s heavy workload last week? – Pat In Agawam Yes, I would expect it to be more balanced. Stevenson playing 85 percent of the snaps in unattainable moving forward. The Patriots also could Henderson’s big-play ability and just overall speed on the offense Last year’s team had great chemistry. Why on Earth would they not try harder to resign Gibbens, Chaisson, & Tonga? All 3 positions lacked depth going into the season. You can’t build chemistry with 1 year rentals every season. And every draft pick they made on Day 3 is garbage. That’s why our depth will be our downfall this season. – VinnieBoombatz71 Tonga got priced out in Kansas City for the Patriots liking. Chaisson wasn’t a fit for what they were looking for off of the field. Gibbens was an interesting choice due to his value and history with Mike Vrabel, but did struggle a bit down the stretch. We’ll see if the depth ultimately improves or costs them. What are some of the things to be excited about the next week? – sumeetw Football is back in Foxboro, that’s worthy being excited about. But seriously, a bounce back Drake Maye game would be huge and while A.J. Brown’s injury is a tough loss, I am excited to see who steps up in the wide receiver room (Kyle Williams?). Will we win a single game this season? Some fans think we’re heading towards 0-17! – tsarsyrup1215 I believe they can. In fact, I’m picking them to do just that this Sunday. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.
author: Brian Hines

title: Josh McDaniels knows defenses are adjusting to Drake Maye. Now the Patriots must respond.
summary: In his first year playing under offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, quarterback Drake Maye started 21 games as he led the Patriots to the Super Bowl while finishing second in MVP voting. After seeing what Maye was capable of during his breakout season, opposing defenses are now adjusting. “There’s evidence of things he does, things he […]
full_text: In his first year playing under offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, quarterback Drake Maye started 21 games as he led the Patriots to the Super Bowl while finishing second in MVP voting. After seeing what Maye was capable of during his breakout season, opposing defenses are now adjusting. “There’s evidence of things he does, things he does in our offense, things we use him to do, how we use our players, etc,” McDaniels said Thursday. “I think there’s a natural progression in this league because the coaches on the other teams, the players on the other teams are so talented and when you have a year like Drake did last year, there’s going to be a reaction and a response to that. And it’s been that way every year I’ve been in the league.” As defenses have looked for ways to slow down Maye, a blueprint of sort has started to emerge. That basis of that plan: taking away Maye’s special ability to make plays down the field. In the Patriots’ last five matchups, which have come against top defenses such as Seattle (twice), Denver, Houston and Los Angeles, Maye has faced two-high safeties just over 50% of the time. In the season opener, the Seahawks ran those split-safety looks at a 57% clip. The result is forcing Maye to play a boring brand of football living in the underneath area of the field, which he did to start Week 1 and build a 10-0 lead before he admittedly lost his patience and fired three interceptions all down field. Based on those results, defenses have little reason to abandon that game plan against Maye moving forward. “You might not be able to get them out of it,” McDaniels said. “It depends, I’d say, how productive you are with whatever you’re doing. The layman’s concept would be run it until they have to drop the safety down. Well, I mean, that’s not just the easiest thing to do all the time. And there’s a lot of different variables that go into what they do in split safeties and shell defense. So, you can try to be patient and do that. There’s also ways to try to throw it against those types of coverages to to be effective. “I would say no matter what you do, you just got to try to continue moving the ball forward and make positive plays and eventually score enough points to potentially force a defense to adjust. If you don’t do that, there’s really no need to expect them to change wildly.” As McDaniels noted, one of the best way to force a defense to bring the second safety down into the box is with a successful running game. Dating back to last season, however, New England’s rushing attack has struggled. That trend continued in Week 1 in Seattle, as the Patriots’ backs finished with just 62 yards on 24 carries as they ranked last in the NFL in rush EPA. “The running game is really about execution and toughness,” McDaniels said. “I thought our guys hung in there and we ended up having some of our best runs in the fourth quarter. And patience is important. So, if you’re going to hate a two-yard run in the first quarter, then you might not get to the 10th, 11th, 12th, 25th, 33rd run of the game. “So, I’ve called a lot of games and sometimes I had a great, great, great, great mentor that told me that volume of runs is important to the overall average eventually — and that was Dante Scarnecchia. And so, if you’re sitting there and you want every run in the first quarter to be 4.5 yard average, you might be hoping and wishing for a while. In this league, it’s hard. But if you give us 23, 25, 32 runs, eventually some of those two, three yarders early might become four, five, six yards later. And so, if the game is in a state where you can maintain your balance and stay patient with it, eventually you hope that it bears more fruit.” The Patriots next test will come in their home opener in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, who played zone coverage on all of their defensive drop backs in Week 1 — a similar strategy defensive coordinator Patrick Graham used against the Patriots in Week 1 of last season with the Raiders. While Maye stressed remaining patient under center following the season-opening loss, McDaniels is focused on a slightly different word as the Patriots learn how defenses will approach their quarterback this season: discipline. That distinction will be important as they must remain ready to attack any opportunity that presents itself. “I think what we’re going to find out as we go through this season is, people will do different things. We will see different things and it will require us to be, I would say, in my words, discipline because patience sounds like a passive word to me,” McDaniels said. “The fine line there is protecting it and doing the right thing when they take things away from us and being really aggressive and not taking away one of [Maye’s] greatest attributes, which is to be able to do things down the field and be wonderful throwing the ball. So I think you can do both. I think we’ll see a development from him as he sees how people play him now differently. But this is an extremely exciting opportunity for us to live through this and to see the differences and then mature, grow, and continue to get better.”

title: Patriots vs. Steelers weather forecast for NFL Week 2
summary: The New England Patriots will host their 2026 home opener on Sunday, but fans might have to bring some rain gear to the game. The upcoming Week 2 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers could become a wet affair. According to NFL Weather, rain showers could move through Gillette Stadium throughout the day, with the chance […]
full_text: The New England Patriots will host their 2026 home opener on Sunday, but fans might have to bring some rain gear to the game. The upcoming Week 2 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers could become a wet affair. According to NFL Weather , rain showers could move through Gillette Stadium throughout the day, with the chance of precipitation hovering around 40-45%. Temperatures, meanwhile, will not exceed 63°F and are expected to drop to as low as 58°F by the fourth quarter. The National Weather Service shared a similar projection with “a chance of showers, mainly after noon.” The chance of precipitation has been calculated at 50% for Sunday afternoon. For both the Patriots and Steelers, this would present a change compared to their respective season openers last week. Whereas New England played the Seahawks in sunny conditions at Seattle’s Lumen Field, the weather was cloudy but dry in Pittsburgh on Sunday versus the visiting Falcons. The Patriots did practice in the rain in training camp, but they have not played a game in wet conditions since the AFC Championship Game — a contest that was impacted by heavy snowfall. Their last true rain game took place a full calendar year ago: the 2025 home opener versus the Raiders, a game New England lost 20-13. Kickoff between the Patriots and Steelers is scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 20 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots rooting guide for NFL Week 2
summary: And just like that, the second week of the 2026 NFL regular season has arrived. The New England Patriots will enter the action on Sunday with a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, one of 16 total games on the menu between Thursday and Monday. Here’s who to root for in the 15 contests not featuring […]
full_text: And just like that, the second week of the 2026 NFL regular season has arrived. The New England Patriots will enter the action on Sunday with a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, one of 16 total games on the menu between Thursday and Monday. Here’s who to root for in the 15 contests not featuring Drake Maye and company. Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET Detroit Lions (1-0) at Buffalo Bills ( 1-0 ) : Go Lions! The Patriots’ biggest division rival started the season with a win. Naturally, a follow-up loss especially to an NFC side would be the preferred outcome. It happening at the first game at Buffalo’s new state-of-the-art stadium would be the cherry on top. | Prime Video Monday 1 p.m. ET Carolina Panthers (0-1) at Atlanta Falcons ( 0-1 ) : Go good game! Neither team is on the Patriots’ schedule or in any other way directly tied to the team. | FOX New Orleans Saints ( 0-1 ) at Baltimore Ravens ( 1-0 ) : Go Saints! While a Saints win would negatively impact the sixth-round draft pick the Patriots will get from them next year — shoutout Ja’Lynn Polk — it is the preferred outcome with the 2026 season in mind. | CBS Minnesota Vikings ( 1-0 ) at Chicago Bears ( 1-0 ) : Go Bears! With both on New England’s schedule, the tiebreaker goes to the team that has a more valuable Patriots draft pick tied to its fortunes. A Vikings loss would be good news for the seventh-round selection obtained as part of the Walter Rouse trade. But why not root for the Vikings then? Because the highest of the Patriots’ two fifth-round picks — including the Bears pick received for Garrett Bradbury — will go to Philadelphia anyway via the conditions of the A.J. Brown move. | FOX Cincinnati Bengals ( 1-0 ) at Houston Texans ( 0-1 ) : Go Texans! The pick acquired through the Marte Mapu trade would suggest rooting for Cincinnati, but the desire for a close AFC playoff race forces us to go with Houston in this one. | CBS Green Bay Packers ( 0-1 ) at New York Jets ( 1-0 ) : Go Packers! NFC team over Patriots division rival. Easy choice. | FOX Cleveland Browns ( 0-1 ) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers ( 0-1 ) : Go Buccaneers! Another case of picking the NFC team over AFC team. | CBS Philadelphia Eagles ( 1-0 ) at Tennessee Titans ( 0-1 ) : Go Eagles! We are going NFC over AFC yet again, because there are no ties to the Patriots in this game as well. | FOX 4:05 p.m. ET Jacksonville Jaguars ( 1-0 ) at Denver Broncos ( 0-1 ) : Go Broncos! The game does not matter in terms of the Patriots’ strength of schedule, but a Denver win would put both teams at 1-1 as opposed to one pulling away in the AFC playoff race. Sure, New England has to beat them both this year, but the rivals cannibalizing wins against one another is still the preferred outcome. | CBS Las Vegas Raiders ( 1-0 ) at Los Angeles Chargers ( 0-1 ) : Go Chargers! Both teams are on the Patriots’ schedule, so we are going with the one with the worse record. The Raiders might ultimately turn out to be the worse team this season, but until there is actual proof of that we are playing it safe. | CBS 4:25 p.m. ET Seattle Seahawks ( 1-0 ) at Arizona Cardinals ( 1-0 ) : Go Seahawks! This pick is solely made with the Patriots’ strength of schedule tiebreaker in mind. | FOX Washington Commanders ( 0-1 ) at Dallas Cowboys ( 0-1 ) : Go good game! Neither team has any direct ties to the Patriots, meaning that the result matters only marginally at this stage in the season. | FOX Miami Dolphins (0-1) at San Francisco 49ers (1-0): Go 49ers! Once again, we are picking the NFC team over the Patriots’ division rival. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Indianapolis Colts ( 0-1 ) at Kansas City Chiefs ( 1-0 ) : Go Colts! The Chiefs are on the Patriots’ schedule, but as mentioned above the preferred outcome is their AFC rivals taking wins off of one another. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET New York Giants ( 1-0 ) at Los Angeles Rams ( 0-1 ) : Go good game! Neither the Giants nor the Rams have any direct ties to the Patriots’ fortunes this year or in the 2027 draft, so there is no use in picking one over the other in this game. | ESPN/ABC

title: Patriots’ TreVeyon Henderson facing backlash over another social media post
summary: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson is in the spotlight again. Not only has the second-year running back returned to practice and is seemingly trending toward making his season debut on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers, he also is facing backlash over a post he made on social media. If that second part sounds […]
full_text: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson is in the spotlight again. Not only has the second-year running back returned to practice and is seemingly trending toward making his season debut on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers, he also is facing backlash over a post he made on social media. If that second part sounds familiar, it’s because this is not the first time this happened. The latest issue involves Henderson commenting on a story posted by Fox News, which misrepresents the case of a then-15-year-old who was separated from her parents after charges of physical abuse were filed against the father. Court records show that the man was accused of punching and threatening the child, and that a restraining order was filed against both him and the mother. The parents, on the other hand, claim that the Massachusetts Department of Children and Families is aiding the teenager’s gender transition against their will. Fox News picked up the story, giving it national attention and prompting Henderson to comment on it — a comment that has drawn over three million views. The God we serve commands parents to “Direct your children onto the right path, and when they are older, they will not leave it.” Proverbs 22:6 Yet, this God given right that these parents have is being stripped away from them by the state. These parents who want to honor our… https://t.co/HFSBVkOPVV — TreVeyon Henderson (@TreVeyonH4) September 15, 2026 On Thursday, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald asked the Patriots running back about his tweet and whether he was aware of the full facts surrounding the story. The exchange, as posted by Callahan on Twitter/X , reads like this: Q: “When you posted this [tweet], were you aware that the father in this particular case had been charged, charges he denies, with abusing the child?” Henderson: “What abuse?” Q: “Physical abuse. He was charged two years ago, so the parents have — he’s been separated from the daughter and told to stay away. And so in that particular case, that’s why they’ve been apart for almost [two] years.” Henderson: “I think the biggest thing what I saw on my end is, I saw the the state take away someone’s child because they didn’t want to affirm their daughter as a boy, and I heard that the school, without the parents’ permission, tried to transition a child or do some sort of thing to transition her into a boy, and I don’t believe that’s right. I believe the family being a Catholic family and having certain morals that they go by and live by. I think it’s they have the God-given right to raise up their kid to know the Lord, to honor the Lord. But of course, we all have free will, as well. But with that kid being under their parents’ authorities, like we’re called, I’m called to honor my parents and respect my parents as long as it aligns with God. And I think what they were doing, trying to raise up their kid the right way, from from what I from what I’ve read and heard, I think I think that the family did right by not affirming their daughter as a boy, but choosing to affirm her the way that God created her to be as a girl.” Q: “So [the charges] weren’t included in that clip, and that’s why I asked if you were aware that they had been separated because of the accusations filed [in January 2025] that had been brought by the daughter, and that’s what caused her to be removed. Because (the family) can reconvene in December, if the father continues to stay away from her, and that [started] this entire incident. Were you aware of that?” Henderson: “I think — so, I’m still doing research. I’ve heard that charges were filed. But at the end of the day, they were filed. It doesn’t mean that he was guilty of those charges. It’s just accusations, just as the same way people make accusations against me. It doesn’t mean that those accusations are true. It’s just accusations at the end of the day. And so, yeah, I think you’re innocent until you’re proven guilty. So if he was guilty, then that’s on me, because I didn’t know all of that. But if he’s not guilty, if these are just accusations, that they’re making about the father, then I don’t think I don’t think that’s right to run away with that and say the father did this, so we have to take his daughter away. I still don’t think that’s right.” Henderson, a devout Christian who is not afraid of sharing his beliefs, was criticized by the online community both for his original comment and his conversation with Callahan. It is not his first rodeo after a similar situation occurred during the offseason. In March, the 23-year-old seemingly expressed support for NBA player Jaden Ivey after he was released by the Chicago Bulls following apparent anti-LGBTQ+ remarks. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was later prompted to confront Henderson and address the matter both privately and publicly. “I want them to be able to express what they believe in their heart and in their mind, but also want to make sure that they’re educated,” Vrabel said at the time . “And we want to be inclusive. Everything we want to do, wants to provide an environment for people to one, feel comfortable, but also to share their personal beliefs. And then also, we represent the team and we represent the organization.” “We’ve had a great conversation,” Henderson later told the media . “He was very respectful about my beliefs. He expressed that aloud to this team, and so I really appreciate Coach for that.” The Patriots will host the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium on Sunday. Henderson, who missed the season opener with an ankle injury, made his return to practice earlier this week and has been listed as a full participant on both Wednesday and Thursday.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Romeo Doubs ready to move past rough Patriots debut
summary: Romeo Doubs’ Patriots debut did not start off on the right foot. The veteran wide receiver is ready to move forward. “I appreciate the question. What happened in the past must stay in the past,” Doubs said Thursday. “So, thank you.” Doubs saw three targets in his debut, failing to corral any of them. That […]
full_text: Romeo Doubs’ Patriots debut did not start off on the right foot. The veteran wide receiver is ready to move forward. “I appreciate the question. What happened in the past must stay in the past,” Doubs said Thursday. “So, thank you.” Doubs saw three targets in his debut, failing to corral any of them. That included a fourth-quarter drop, which he owned up to, that preceded an interception, along with another target in his direction that was picked off. Even with the lack of results, head coach Mike Vrabel is not worried about the receiver he signed to 4-year, $68 million contract in free agency. “He dropped a pass. You know what I mean? Guys, everybody drops a pass. Everybody misses a tackle,” Vrabel said. “You talk to him the same way you always talk to him. Figure out a way to make a play to help us win, and he did a lot of great things during camp, just like everybody did. And so, I know he’s excited to get back out there, get to work and to find a way to help us win.” Vrabel wasn’t lying. “It’ll be exciting,” Doubs said when asked about Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Patriots will simply need a better version of the 26-year old moving forward as top wide receiver A.J. Brown is sidelined at least four weeks with a high-ankle sprain. That leaves Doubs atop the depth chart, followed by Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III. Doubs, and his quarterback, have confidence in his ability to rebound. “I have a ton of confidence in myself, but I look forward to keeping my humility sane and doing what I do,” he said. “You guys saw it in camp, and his ability to make plays,” Drake Maye added. “He has had a great response [this week]. I am looking forward to seeing him on Sunday.”

Newman-Johnson, 27, had been hosted by the organization on the heels of being released from the New […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 13: Mike Vrabel of the New England Patriots and Xavier Newman #65 of the New York Jets embrace after the NFL 2025 game between New York Jets and New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on November 13, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images After making a midweek visit to Gillette Stadium, Xavier Newman-Johnson will be staying around. The New England Patriots officially signed the veteran offensive lineman to the practice squad on Thursday as part of a reshuffle along the interior. Newman-Johnson, 27, had been hosted by the organization on the heels of being released from the New York Jets’ practice squad. The 6-foot-2, 297-pound guard stands 25 games into his run in the NFL and has made five starts. Originally entering the league with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022, Newman-Johnson spent parts of two seasons with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former club before heading to the AFC East. The Baylor product resided between the practice squad, 53-man roster and injured reserve while in Florham Park. His career includes 338 snaps on offense, 68 snaps on special teams and time at center in addition to both guard spots. To make room among the group of 17, the Patriots released rookie offensive lineman Jacob Rizy from the practice squad, as first reported by the Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan . Rizy, 24, entered the NFL as a member of New England’s 2026 undrafted class in May. The 6-foot-5, 306-pounder played 155 snaps at center through three preseason games before being waived in advance of the league’s 53-man roster deadline. After going unclaimed, he signed to the practice squad at its formation on the final day of August. A former second-team and first-team All-Ivy League selection, Rizy spent three campaigns at Harvard and two campaigns at Florida State. The 27-game starter saw work at center, left guard, right guard and right tackle during his collegiate career. The Pittsburgh Steelers visit Foxborough on Sunday. The home opener is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots vs. Steelers: Who has the edge in Week 2?
summary: The New England Patriots and Pittsburgh Steelers are historically pretty familiar with one another; Sunday’s game will be their 37th meeting overall. But while the Patriots have recently dominated the series, it was the Steelers who earned a victory the last time the two franchises squared off in Week 3 of the 2025 season. A […]
full_text: The New England Patriots and Pittsburgh Steelers are historically pretty familiar with one another; Sunday’s game will be their 37th meeting overall. But while the Patriots have recently dominated the series, it was the Steelers who earned a victory the last time the two franchises squared off in Week 3 of the 2025 season. A similar outcome would be bad news for this year’s New England squad, and drop it to 0-2 after a loss in the season opener against Seattle. That said, the oddsmakers feel strongly about a Patriots victory in what will be their home opener, as do we. Passing game Patriots pass offense vs. Steelers pass defense: The Patriots passing offense did not have its best day in Week 1 against the Seahawks, but that was mainly due to Drake Maye’s fourth-quarter collapse. Even with him tossing three straight interceptions to end the game, the unit ranked 15th in expected points added per dropback (0.127) and eighth in success rate (52.3%) in Week 1. This shows: it generally performed well, at least when Maye stayed on track and before, by his own admission, he lost patience down the stretch. Of course, A.J. Brown’s absence will be an issue this week, as will be blocking the likes of T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nate Herbig. That said, if Maye picks his targets wisely, he should be able to find success even against what was statistically the best pass defense in football last week (-0.638 EPA/play). | Edge: Patriots Patriots pass defense vs. Steelers pass offense: The last time Christian Gonzalez faced off with DK Metcalf, in Week 2 of his 2024 sophomore season, he held him to four catches for 27 yards. A similar performance would be enough to seriously limit Pittsburgh’s passing game and put the pressure on other players to step up. Running back Jaylen Warren and tight end Pat Freiermuth in particular are worth keeping an eye on in that regard, especially given New England’s comparatively modest athleticism at linebacker. On the whole, however, the defense still gets the edge in this one: Gonzalez and the rest of the secondary should be able to limit Seattle’s receivers, while the interior pass rush could create problems for a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers. | Edge: Patriots Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Running game Patriots rushing offense vs. Steelers run defense: The Patriots rushing offense had a rough time getting going against Seattle, and as a consequence finished Week 1 dead-last in the league in expected points added per run (-0.451). Getting TreVeyon Henderson back should help, but the team needs better blocking up front as well: Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Reggie Gilliam in particular need to be able to create a more consistent push at the line of scrimmage. Unfortunately, doing so against a stout Steelers front that is disciplined both inside and on the edge will be a tall task. The goal will be to take advantage of any potential lighter boxes New England will face — a byproduct of having Drake Maye at quarterback — but unless the Patriots show they can do so, we cannot pick them in this 1-on-1. | Edge: Steelers Patriots run defense vs. Steelers rushing offense: The Patriots’ run game was bad in Week 1, but the Steelers’ was only marginally better: its own -0.252 EPA per run ranked 27th. Like New England against Seattle, it simply failed to create a consistent push up front versus Atlanta; as a consequence, Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle gained only 13 of their 61 combined rushing yards before contact. Warren was still able to do some damage on the ground, but that model of attack — as the Patriots very well know themselves — is hardly sustainable. That is especially true against a defense that was solid versus the run in the opener, ranking eighth in EPA per play (-0.195) while looking much-improved on the edge. | Edge: Patriots Special teams The Patriots didn’t make any game-changing plays in the kicking game in Week 1, but they looked decent for the most part. The same cannot be said for the Steelers: Atlanta averaged 11.0 yards on its three punt returns on Sunday, and also gained an average of 30.8 yards on four kickoff returns. New England taking advantage of the latter is not a given, despite showing some signs of life in that area, but Pittsburgh’s punt coverage could be in for a tough ride versus Marcus Jones. Unless the team finds a way to neutralize him — by consistently aiming to kick out of bounds, for example — the NFL’s all-time leader in punt return average could become a major factor in the game. | Edge: Patriots Coaching The Patriots coaching staff might not be happy with all of its decisions in Week 1, but overall had the team in a position to win. The Steelers actually did manage to win, even if said W came against a lesser opponent than the reigning world champions. Still, on the whole we are giving the advantage in the coaching matchup to New England. Its staff has superior experience working with each other, and all in all has shown an ability to get the most out of the talent available (see: Gabe Jacas). Pittsburgh’s Mike McCarthy is, of course, one of the most successful head coaches of his era, but that difference in intra-staff experience — plus more time to prepare — is enough for us to give New England the nod here. | Edge: Patriots Verdict In spit of their loss in Week 1 and A.J. Brown since landing on injured reserve, the Patriots are the more complete team top to bottom. The difference might not be as drastic as our comparison might suggest, but we can see the defense put the clamps on Aaron Rodgers and company while Drake Maye bounces back from arguably the worst quarter of football he has played since entering the NFL. This should be enough to earn a victory in the home opener, and any other outcome would frankly be worrying even at this early stage of the season.

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 07: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens runs with the ball as Tyrann Mathieu #32 and Cameron Jordan #94 of the New Orleans Saints defend during a game at the Caesars Superdome on November 07, 2022 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints face the Baltimore Ravens in the second road game of the season. The Saints had an exciting but unfruitful overtime finish last week in Detroit, a game that they could have truly stolen. Ultimately, they just couldn’t convert on a game-winning two-point conversion attempt. Now the Black and Gold turn their attention to an even tougher road test in Baltimore. Pulling out a road win against this perennial AFC power will take even more of what they showed in the second half in Detroit. For the first half and early third quarter last week, it seemed the Saints had no drive, no clue, and sadly, no heart. Then, without warning, they struck, and proved to the fans, and to themselves, they had heart, and a lot of it. Now they must overcome the team named after Edgar Allen Poe’s famous story “The Raven”, and the Saints will have to bring back that energy once again in order to earn their first win of the season. Despite taking that loss a week ago, the Saints showed a lot of heart, and much like Poe’s titular “Tell-Tale Heart”, the Saints’ heart cannot be ignored. It simply will not be ignored. Last week, I went 10-6 I told you so: Raiders over Dolphins! What do I know: Titans over Jets? WEEK 2 Thursday, September 17th – Thursday Night Football Lions(1-0) at Bills(1-0) Buffalo follows-up their huge win in Houston last week, with another high-octane game to open up their new stadium. Buffalo wins 38-34. Pick: Bills *** Sunday, September 20th – Early Games Panthers(0-1) at Falcons(0-1) Carolina had a great offensive output last week, only to see their defense get demolished by a much more dynamic offense. Carolina won’t have to worry about that happening against Atlanta’s offense this week. Carolina wins 30-14. Pick: Panthers *** Vikings(1-0) at Bears(1-0) Chicago looked to have the NFL’s best offense in Week 1, but things will get closer this week against Minnesota’s tricky defense. This will be a close one. Chicago wins 23-21. Pick: Bears *** Bengals(1-0) at Texans(0-1) – Game of the Week Joe Burrow and the Cincy offense facing Will Anderson and the Houston defense will be one of the best matchups you will see all season. Cincy pulls it out with a game-winning field goal in the closing moments, handing Houston a second-straight heartbreaking loss. Cincinnati wins 32-29. Pick: Bengals *** Steelers(1-0) at Patriots(0-1) New England came out of Week 1 with a disappointing loss, but they will rebound against Pittsburgh, who took advantage of a gimme win against Atlanta last week. New England wins 21-14. Pick: Patriots *** Packers(0-1) at Jets(1-0) Few would have expected the Jets to come into this game with a better record than Green Bay, but things will even out when this game is done. Green Bay wins 34-12. Pick: Packers *** Browns(0-1) at Buccaneers(0-1) Tampa’s defense gladly welcomes the severe downgrade from Cincinnati’s offense to Cleveland’s, and will take advantage of that to pick up the win. Tampa Bay wins 23-21. Pick: Buccaneers *** Eagles(1-0) at Titans(0-1) After Tennessee’s disappointing Week 1 loss, they will follow it up with another loss against Philly. Philadelphia win 29-16. Pick: Eagles *** Saints(0-1) at Ravens(1-0) Baltimore finds themselves coming off a dominant performance in Indianapolis, a game that was never in doubt following Indy’s opening touchdown. Now they host a Saints team that came within a two-point conversion attempt in overtime from being 1-0 themselves. The Saints now face a Ravens team who have taken some significant injuries to their wide receiver room. The timing on that front couldn’t have been better, but the impact may not be as significant, as Baltimore runs their offense primarily through the premier rushing abilities of Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry. To be honest, the Saints were never favorites in this game at any point in the offseason, and that hasn’t changed now, but last week’s late game performance is giving some hope where none may have existed before. While the Ravens aren’t some unstoppable juggernaut, the Saints have historically struggled against them, going 2-6 all-time. The Saints defense will have to withstand the punishing and explosive Ravens ground attack, and that will unfortunately prove to be too much to overcome in this one. Baltimore wins 36-27. Pick: Ravens *** Sunday, September 20th – Late Games Jaguars(1-0) at Broncos(0-1) Following a disappointing performance in Kansas City, Denver bounces back with a late game-winner by Wil Lutz, against a very good Jacksonville team. Denver wins 29-26. Pick: Broncos *** Raiders(1-0) at Chargers(0-1) The Chargers are coming off the weakest performance of Week 1 and they know they can’t afford another loss here to Vegas. Los Angeles wins 26-12. Pick: Chargers *** Seahawks(1-0) at Cardinals(1-0) Drew Lock continues to play in place of an injured Sam Darnold, and will pick up another win, against an Arizona team that surprised a week ago. Seattle wins 34-21. Pick: Seahawks *** Commanders(0-1) at Cowboys(0-1) After falling on their faces last Sunday Night, Dallas rebounds with an offensive outburst at home against their division rivals. Dallas wins 37-24. Pick: Cowboys *** Dolphins(0-1) at 49ers(1-0) It’s going to be a long season in Miami, and that continues against a San Francisco team that looks like a contender once again. San Francisco wins 31-17. Pick: 49ers *** Sunday Night Football Colts(0-1) at Chiefs(1-0) Kansas City looked quite good in Week 1, while Indianapolis looked quite the opposite, and those trajectories will continue here. Kansas City wins 31-20. Pick: Chiefs *** Monday, September 21st – Monday Night Football Giants(1-0) at Rams(0-1) The Giants started the Harbaugh-era with a divisional home win last week, while the Rams traveled all the way to Australia just to get punched in the gut. Both teams will swing back to who they are this week. Los Angeles wins 31-17. Pick: Rams *** That’s how I see it, tell us how you see Week 2 playing out. Leave your comments and insight below. full_text: BATON ROUGE, LA - SEPTEMBER 05: LSU Tigers Trey'dez Green #7 plays against the Clemson Tigers during the first half of a game on September 5, 2026, at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the NFL 1 week into the season, the current draft order could be a bit… insane. For example, after their win against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Arizona Cardinals, a team many believe is going to be one of the worst in the NFL, are projected to select 32nd overall after Week 1. Of course, that will likely change, but for the New Orleans Saints, even after their loss, they are currently projected to have their pick at 19th. Alabama EDGE Yhonzae Pierre Last week’s edition was focused on two defensive linemen, and I’m sticking to that for this first player. Yhonzae Pierre out of Alabama is a fun pass rusher that the Saints might fall in love with early in this process. He plays with nice strenght; he has backup plans if he doesn’t win against that offensive lineman right away, has a high motor, is good at setting the edge against the run, and should fit right in at OLB. Pierre is still developing in run defense and could get pushed around a bit, but he still has plenty of time to improve that. For the Saints, Week 1 was not the best showing from the outside pass rush. Chase Young was the only consistent EDGE for New Orleans, and that just isn’t sustainable. Hopefully Cam Jordan’s return will help, but Granderson starting opposite Young may need to change. LSU TE Trey’Dez Green I know, I know, I know. Please don’t hate this potential pick before I explain why. I totally get the confusion if the Saints select yet another TE with Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant, and Oscar Delp under contract. But Trey’Dez Green is different compared to those three players. He’s an incredible blocker, the definition of a contested-catch threat, and extremely difficult to tackle once he has the ball. Looking at the player alone, without considering the Saints roster, he is a no-brainer selection. Now, let’s look at said roster. If the Saints ever made this pick, a couple of things would need to happen. First, the investments on defense must be exponential before the draft to even consider going with another offensive weapon. Then, if they make the pick, the Saints would need to move on from either Johnson or Fant. But I don’t think that’s out of the realm of possibility, and Green would be an incredible weapon for Tyler Shough.

title: If Saints win/lose vs. Ravens
summary: The New Orleans Saints are hitting the road again as they prepare to visit the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. After last week’s close call, maybe we should be adding the third possibility of a tie! But regardless, here’s a quick look at what either outcome might mean for the black and gold in Week 2. […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints are hitting the road again as they prepare to visit the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. After last week’s close call, maybe we should be adding the third possibility of a tie! But regardless, here’s a quick look at what either outcome might mean for the black and gold in Week 2. If the Saints win: Even more so than against Detroit, a win here would be a massive statement by Kellen Moore’s squad. As 7.5-point underdogs, New Orleans has one of the biggest handicaps across the league this week. That line has moved down from 8.5, perhaps a sign that bettors like the Saints here after their heroic comeback effort fell just short last week. The second half against Detroit showed everything people have been hoping for from the black and gold, with a defense able to get off the field on third down and an offense that can threaten both on the ground and through the air. The Saints will need an effective 60 minutes on both sides of the football against a Ravens team that scored at will against the Colts in Week 1. Should they beat Baltimore, it would be both emphatic and more than deserved to come back to New Orleans with a .500 record after a bit of controversy got in the way of a win in Detroit. If the Saints lose: This pair of road games to open the season were always going to be difficult for the black and gold. To end up 0-2 would be disappointing, but wouldn’t necessarily define the way the season might pan out. Moore will hope, regardless of the outcome, that the Saints look more in Baltimore like they did in the second half of the season opener than the first. Building on their momentum is crucial ahead of the winnable stretch of games to come. Do you think the Saints can pull the upset off in Baltimore? Let us know in the comments!

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 2 preview
summary: The New Orleans Saints had a very up-and-down first game of the season, but I think what surprised me most was the lack of impact from the rookies. Maybe I was a bit too confident in the Saints’ use of these players, but it was an overall quiet day from the first-year players, aside from […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 13: Bryce Lance #18 of the New Orleans Saints warms up prior to the game at Ford Field on September 13, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints had a very up-and-down first game of the season, but I think what surprised me most was the lack of impact from the rookies. Maybe I was a bit too confident in the Saints’ use of these players, but it was an overall quiet day from the first-year players, aside from maybe two who stood out. Week 2 may be different, and if the Saints want to win, it should be. DT Christen Miller On the Saints roster, Christen Miller had to overcome both Davon Godchaux and Nathen Shepherd in front of him, but he still got on the field against the Lions. Godchaux didn’t have a great game, and Shepherd made some plays here and there, but I saw no reason Miller wouldn’t be on the field. He did have a hold in the game, which was the main knock, but overall, he looked strong and performed well enough to consider playing him more. Against the Baltimore Ravens, Miller’s strenght and run defense are a necessity. RB Derrick Henry is inevitable. Stopping him is one of the most difficult things to do in the NFL, and it doesn’t help that Lamar Jackson is back there with the threat of running himself. Miller must see the field more. TE Oscar Delp Delp didn’t play in Week 1 because of his hamstring injury, and it looked like the Saints missed him. Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant both made plays in the air, but Delp’s blocking would have helped a lot. There were a couple of plays where Johnson’s blocking could have been better (although it wasn’t bad blocking), and moments where Treyton Welch did struggle holding blocks. Of course, we haven’t had consistency from Delp in the air, but I do think his presence would have changed the game a bit. Now for the Ravens matchup, I’m not sure Delp plays. Hamstrings are tricky, and the group of three that played against the Lions were not bad, just could have been better. OG Jeremiah Wright Wright also didn’t play in Week 1, but it was because Cesar Ruiz started in front of him. This will be a bit more about Ruiz and why a change could be made. Nothing on Sunday showed us that the improvements Mickey Loomis noted at the end of last season happened. Ruiz struggled in run blocking, was pushed back multiple times in pass protection, and was just flat-out beat throughout the game. To give Ruiz a compliment, he was a bit more consistent as a pass protector, just not where the Saints want him to be. I doubt a change will be made anytime soon; I just wanted to note that with Wright having a great end to the preseason, the Saints may want to see what they have in the rookie. WRs Bryce Lance Although Lance wasn’t listed as WR3 entering this game, he played like it, and the Saints put him in that role early in the matchup. They must have seen something to know Lance would be the better fit against this Lions defense, and it worked. Lance got open in the short game, had some nice run-after-the-catch moments, blocked well, and made one of the day’s biggest plays, converting a massive fourth-and-long. It’s going to be a more difficult matchup against the Ravens, but Lance may be the perfect WR3 option to make the tough catches when needed, similar to Devaughn Vele WR Barion Brown Barion Brown’s inclusion in the offense was probably the surprise of the day. The rookie, after a really impressive preseason, did not play much. He had one handoff that went for a short gain, but that was about it. I do wonder if the Lions just really played him well and Lance was just the better fit for this matchup. The questionable moments happened on the kick returns, which were not great. The Ravens’ secondary is very good, and with head coach Jesse Minter being defensively focused, I think this could be another quiet game from Brown. OT Mason Murphy Murphy was a healthy scratch against the Lions, and that should be the case again in Week 2. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson DB Lorenzo Styles Jr.
