title: Steelers film room: Pittsburgh trends on offense, defense against the Falcons
summary: Before we flip the page to the Steelers’ next opponents — our preview of the New England Patriots matchup is out Friday — we here at Read & React wanted to take one last look at the film from Week 1, and take stock of any interesting trends or tidbits we felt worth sharing. We […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts against the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before we flip the page to the Steelers’ next opponents — our preview of the New England Patriots matchup is out Friday — we here at Read & React wanted to take one last look at the film from Week 1, and take stock of any interesting trends or tidbits we felt worth sharing. We haven’t decided if we’ll do a film room each week in-season, or toggle between that and doing what we have in the past in discussing the trending Steelers narratives in the media at large. At least for this week, we’ve opted for the former, as we couldn’t bring ourselves to add another article with hand-wringing about the Joey Porter Jr. contract situation, attempts to interpret the various Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthey soundbites throughout the week, nor give any in-depth takes on former coach Mike Tomlin as an in-studio analyst — though I think he had more ups than downs, and I hope NBC doesn’t try to over-sanitize his personality; we don’t need more Jason Garrett types! So with that in mind, let’s dive into the tape with what Ryland and Ryan found noteworthy about Week 1’s performance. Defense RB: So much was made about how creative and at times complicated Patrick Graham’s Steelers defense would be in 2026, but to start off the season, Pittsburgh’s new coordinator kept things fairly simple. There were some twists rushing the passer, a healthy dose of coverage rotations, and some of Graham’s signature creepers at the line of scrimmage. But overall, Pittsburgh’s game plan was fairly straightforward by NFL standards. Pittsburgh blitzed at a league-low 7.7%, primarily relying on a four-man rush. According to Next Gen Stats, the Steelers played zone coverage exclusively when the Falcons dropped back to pass — though it should be noted, as Graham did in a later press conference, that some of those reps used match concepts, which have similarities to man coverage. And while some off-ball linebacker snaps for Nick Herbig were a new wrinkle in the Steelers’ three-outside linebacker package, there wasn’t much in the realm of exotic formations or schematics. Why were things so simple? My guess would be that the Steelers rightfully recognized their defense is clearly more talented than the Cooper Rush-led Falcons offense, and saw no need to complicate things. Despite Pittsburgh rarely blitzing, the Steelers managed a 15.4% sack rate, the league’s second-best mark in Week 1. Elite running back Bijan Robinson was a problem, as expected, with 90 receiving yards and plenty of missed tackles in the process. Despite this, he was held to a manageable four yards per carry in the run game. And Atlanta’s next-leading receiver, the talented Drake London, was held to 29 yards as Rush completed just 12/22 passes for 143 yards. Altogether, a lack of uber-confusing concepts likely helped the defensive players simply line up and make plays. Keeping things simple can be a detriment when a team lacks enough talent, but we’ve also seen plenty of elite defenses, like last year’s Texans or the Legion of Boom-era Seahawks, suffocate opposing offenses when the right collection of players can master a straightforward scheme. For the Steelers on Sunday, that resulted in arguably the best game of inside linebacker Payton Wilson’s career. For much of the summer, I projected my hope that a Year 3 breakout from the talented Wilson would be possible under Graham’s guidance. That campaign got off to a good start in Week 1. I’m not sure if I’ve ever seen Wilson look so fast and confident on the football field. He logged 13 total tackles, including two for loss, and looked both quick and decisive in coverage. And while he’s still not a thumper defending the run, the game looks like it has slowed down for him, with Wilson seeing success knifing through blocks near the line of scrimmage to make plays. Payton Wilson was cooking against the Falcons pic.twitter.com/qFQ3Lchz43 — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 15, 2026 Wilson’s play, as well as high-end performances from T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and Alex Highsmith, were probably the biggest individual storylines for the Steelers defense. However, I was also impressed by the contributions of some newcomers on the defense. Both safety Jaquan Brisker and cornerback Jamel Dean were solid in coverage (Brisker recorded a nice interception on an overthrow in zone; Dean got run by when flat-footed on one play but otherwise looked fine), but both made their biggest impacts as tacklers. Dean looked like a heat-seeking missile at times and managed to force a fumble on Robinson. Steelers DBs came to play against the Falcons (Jamel Dean 1/2) pic.twitter.com/uTmyEtgeC6 — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 15, 2026 Brisker was fearless when filling holes in the run game. Even if he didn’t always make a clean tackle, he clearly affected a number of plays. Jaquan Brisker (2/2) pic.twitter.com/8jbndnJESC — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 15, 2026 One of the hits on Robinson was a true bone-crusher, too. Jaquan Brisker looks phenomenal today for Pittsburgh… can’t believe Chicago let him go pic.twitter.com/4WFOBCvHuT — RGF (@rgfray1) September 13, 2026 Besides taking advantage of misfires and poor reads from Rush, Graham’s zone-heavy scheme (with a heavy dose of cover 4) allowed the team’s aggressive defensive backs to keep the game in front of them and crash down when needed. Defensive coverage rates in Week 1 Via @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/YAAYNFielQ — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) September 15, 2026 A more underrated contributor was new defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day, who logged just 18 snaps in a rotational role but still managed to stand out on several reps. His power is a real asset, and having a player of his caliber outside the main starting lineup speaks to the team’s overall depth at the position. Sebastian Joseph-Day (No. 69) with some good reps rotating in on the Steelers D-line pic.twitter.com/n32VRB6k8q — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 15, 2026 We’ll end with the Steelers’ biggest name on defense, T.J. Watt, who looked like his prime self once again against Atlanta with two sacks, a pick-six and another tackle for loss. Attentive watchers would’ve noticed Watt saw a number of rushes from the right side of the defense — he’s been almost exclusively a left-side rusher for much of his career — showing some of the “Watt moving around the formation” hype could finally be coming true under the defense’s new coordinator. Did Watt look especially different coming from the right side? Did defenses look unusually perplexed? Not exactly, but his first rep from the blind side resulted in a sack, which means the idea resulted in some success. It’s also a good sign for the Steelers continuing to matchup hunt and mix and match the team’s arsenal of pass rushers down the road. TJ Watt rushing from the right side pic.twitter.com/YzLhqBufIk — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 16, 2026 What’s exciting about Graham as the defensive coordinator is that it’s difficult to know what he’ll bring to the table next week. He’s made a career of being adaptable to the players he has and the opponents he faces, something he made clear to the media in Tuesday’s press conference. “My philosophy is what’s best for that week, usually … what we think is best to beat the opponent and make sure our guys are able to play fast,” Graham said when asked about the team’s zone-heaviness in Week 1. Graham had a similar response when asked about the lack of blitzing. “I mean, I’m going to tell you, we’re going to try to do what’s best for the game that week,” he said. One game we might have ‘blitz zero’ 20 times in a game. The next week might not blitz one time. We might ‘drop eight’ 20 times.…

title: Mike Macdonald admits ‘I was not a great leader my first year’ with Seahawks
summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald has become a popular interview since winning the Super Bowl. Macdonald was most recently on the ManningCast alt-broadcast of the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, and there’s a fascinating new article out on The Athletic about how he defines “chasing edges.” Over the summer, Macdonald had his most […]
full_text: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald has become a popular interview since winning the Super Bowl. Macdonald was most recently on the ManningCast alt-broadcast of the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, and there’s a fascinating new article out on The Athletic about how he defines “chasing edges.” Over the summer, Macdonald had his most personally revealing interview to date on In Depth with Graham Bensinger . Coach Macdonald went into great detail about his mental state after leaving the Baltimore Ravens to become the Seahawks head coach in 2024. He opened up in a way we’ve never really seen before, particularly as it pertained to his mental health. “It was paralyzing,” Macdonald said. “I’m a procrastinator, which I think has helped me do good work because you feel like you’re kind of elevated when you need to go. But the trade-off of that is, like, it was hard to move. It was even hard to get out of bed. I put a ton of pressure on myself. I have massive expectations for what we’re trying to create. “It’s not good enough to not be the best. But that takes time to get there, and it’s a process, and if you’re not willing to take it incrementally and take some punches along the way because you made decisions quickly — I just wanted to be right all the time and I didn’t know what right was, and I put a lot of pressure on myself to be right. “That was the weight that I was carrying. There’s a burden that I felt like I was holding because we weren’t where we wanted to be, and I wasn’t clear on what to do. That can be a lonely, tough feeling.” Between a move across the country from Baltimore to Seattle, the sudden passing of his beloved 4-year-old dog, and the aforementioned pressure he put on himself, Macdonald talked about how there were days where he wouldn’t leave his bed, much less the house. “It was an extremely difficult time. I’ve never felt like that in my life. I was sick. I’d go home, I’d get in bed and I wouldn’t get out. I’d get in bed as soon as I got home, I wouldn’t get out of bed until I went to work. I’d be late going into work. In the weekend – I wouldn’t get out of bed all weekend. I’d just sit in bed. It was crazy. But, is it depression? I don’t know, maybe. I find it hard to self-diagnose depression. There’s, like, serious cases of depression, like clinically diagnosed… Like it’s kind of irresponsible to say.” During this period, Macdonald said he only spoke to his wife, Stephanie, and his two sisters, about his struggles. But Macdonald pinpointed some lifestyle changes that benefited him. “It was like a through not around thing, ” Macdonald said. “I have to prioritize the routine and the health part of it… If I could get some physical, personal wins, then I could just start stacking those things. But, I’d take two hour-long walks. I’d call some of the players. But I need to get out. So I’d work out, walk, try to try to eat better. I was drinking a lot. Yeah, that was probably the toughest, most difficult stretch of my life, honestly – that first few months.” Toward the second half of the 2024 season, Macdonald said things started to turnaround for him, but he also confessed his belief that he wasn’t as good a leader as he could have been in the Seahawks locker room. “It was in that year, but I actually remember at one point going up to John Schneider and being like, ‘Feel like myself again.’ … I think it might have been in the season, the second half of the season. “I joke with the coaches now, I was not a great leader my first year. It sucks to say that, but I just fell short in so many different ways – in awareness and in trust and a communication style. Just wasn’t the best version of myself. Yeah, it’s not easy to say that, but it’s the truth.” You can watch more from the Macdonald interview in the playlist below. There’s a lot more to unpack and it’s the best insight you’ll get into Macdonald as a person, not just Seattle’s outstanding head coach.

In an appearance on Good Morning Football on Thursday, NFL Network and ESPN’s Ian Rapoport said on Darnold, “We’ll see about next week [versus the Washington Commanders], seems to be a bit of a longshot, but he at least has a bit of a chance. I would say Week 4 probably the most likely target for Darnold.” From @GMFB : Injury updates on #Bengals QB Joe Burrow, #Seahawks QB Sam Darnold, #Vikings QB Kyler Murray, and #49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling. pic.twitter.com/7kciukA8Ec — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 17, 2026 Rapoport’s update on the Seattle Seahawks’ quarterback is the latest, but most definitive, update on Darnold’s status since he left the regular-season opener. Within the past few days, there have been vague updates suggesting Week 3 was possible , then the team’s refusal to put a firm timeline on his return , and then a suggestion he was more day-to-day as opposed to week-to-week. Now, on the back of Rapoport’s latest update, it appears the Seahawks and Darnold are aiming for Week 4. That timeline would see him sit out a two-game road trip, including this week’s trip to the desert to take on the Cardinals and then a trip to Washington to face Dan Quinn’s Commanders, before returning under center when the team returns home to host the Chargers. In Darnold’s place, backup Drew Lock will look to hold the position down after he went 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown in relief in Seattle’s Week 1 win over the New England Patriots.

title: Former Seahawks running back Thomas Rawls breaks down Jadarian Price’s debut
summary: With Jadarian Price and Arizona Cardinals rookie Jeremiyah Love — former Notre Dame backfield mates, now both first-round NFL running backs — set to face off in Week 2, there was no better time to bring back one of the show’s favorite recurring guests. On the latest episode of the Sea Hawkers Podcast, former Seahawks running […]
full_text: With Jadarian Price and Arizona Cardinals rookie Jeremiyah Love — former Notre Dame backfield mates, now both first-round NFL running backs — set to face off in Week 2, there was no better time to bring back one of the show’s favorite recurring guests. On the latest episode of the Sea Hawkers Podcast , former Seahawks running back Thomas Rawls joined the show to break down Price’s Week 1 tape and preview what’s coming against Love and the Cardinals. Here are a few of the biggest takeaways. Price’s debut was about fundamentals, not flash Ten carries for 52 yards doesn’t jump off the box score, but Rawls didn’t grade the stat line. He pointed to Price’s vision and consistency as the traits that stood out on tape. He noted a few points of Price’s technique: squared shoulders, trusting what he sees, and getting north-south without hesitation (6:18) . The low touch count looks like a plan, not a limitation Seattle ran only 48 offensive plays in Week 1, and that helped to cap the amount of work Price could realistically get regardless of how the coaching staff feels about him. Rawls framed it as an intentional, patient build-up in a rookie’s usage and talked about his trust in the Seahawks coaching and medical staff to make sound decisions about playing time. He expects the touches to climb as he works into a rhythm (22:54) . Something to watch moving forward: How big does Price’s role actually get? The return of Zach Charbonnet in the next few weeks could cut into any projection around Price’s role. That said, Rawls offered up a projection. He thinks we’ll see Price around 800 to 1,000 yards at the end of the regular season and is much more interested in seeing him used inside the red zone. Rawls said, “I really want to see if he can get to double digit touchdowns.” (42:55). Rawls also covers a lot of other ground in the episode, including his own breakout 2015 game in relief of an injured Marshawn Lynch (28:05) , a look ahead to the matchup between Price and his former Notre Dame teammate Jeremiyah Love (13:42) and where Seattle-area fans can catch him in person — he’ll be at Muckleshoot Casino in Auburn for the Cardinals road game on September 20 (47:35) . title: Seahawks vs Cardinals: Week 2 score prediction
summary: Week 2 is upon us! After a Week 1 victory over the New England Patriots, the Seattle Seahawks now travel to Glendale for the first divisional rivalry game versus the Arizona Cardinals. In this battle of the birds, who will come out the victor? Will the Seahawks set a franchise record and get their 12th […]
full_text: Week 2 is upon us! After a Week 1 victory over the New England Patriots, the Seattle Seahawks now travel to Glendale for the first divisional rivalry game versus the Arizona Cardinals. In this battle of the birds, who will come out the victor? Will the Seahawks set a franchise record and get their 12th straight win? Or will the Cardinals end their losing streak against the Seahawks? Let’s try to predict this game! Seattle Seahawks The Seahawks in their home opener scored 13 points while holding the Patriots to 10 points in the Super Bowl rematch. It seems as though, defensively, the Seahawks have not missed a beat. They struggled a bit offensively, but between Sam Darnold going down five snaps in, and having a first time play-caller calling their first regular season game, that is to be expected. In 2025, they scored an average of 29 points per game, while allowing and average 17 points per game. Averaging the points for comes out to 21 points, while averaging the points allowed comes to 14 points. Per FTN’s DVOA , the Seahawks are the ninth ranked team in total DVOA. They were the 20th ranked offense per DVOA, the fifth ranked defense, and the fourth ranked special teams. It’s worth noting that DVOA takes several weeks into the season before it becomes a more stable metric. There’s also no accounting for Seattle having Drew Lock come into the game due to Sam Darnold’s injury. Per Sumer Sports , the Seahawks were the 14th ranked offense in total EPA and EPA per play. On defense, they were the 11th ranked defense in total EPA and the 12th ranked defense in EPA per play. Arizona Cardinals The Cardinals put up 26 in their upset road win over the Los Angeles Chargers. They held Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense to just 14 points. Arizona looked good in its first game of the season, and it seems first-year head coach Mike LaFleur has the team buttoned up. Last season, the Cardinals averaged 22 points a game while allowing opponents to score 29 points. Their overall average points for is 24, while their averaged points allowed is 22. Per DVOA , the Cardinals were ranked the 13th best team in the NFL after Week One. They had the sixth ranked offense per DVOA, 20th ranked defense, and 18th ranked special teams. Per Sumer Sports , the Cardinals have the 10th ranked team per total EPA on offense as well as EPA per play on offense. They were also the fifth ranked team per total EPA on defense and fifth in EPA per play on defense. Calculating the Score Now for some fun math: Seahawks 21 + Cards opponents 22 = 43 / 2 = 21.5 Points for Seahawks, but since you cannot have half a point, lets round up to 22. Cards 24 + Sea opponents 14 = 38 / 2 = 19 Points for Seahawks Seahawks score 7 more points on average than opponents. 19 – 4 = 15. Initial score prediction: 22 – 15, Seahawks win However, to make this score work, the Seahawks would need to go for a 2-point conversion, and that doesn’t make a ton of sense, so let’s make some adjustments. Three touchdowns for the Seahawks make sense. I think Jaxon Smith-Njigba and AJ Barner are likely to get one apiece, and I think Jadarian Price will get his first touchdown in this game. Add those points together with some Jason Myers extra points, and we get 21. Final Score Prediction: 21 – 15, Seahawks Victory Deep Dive I went into more detail on the matchup over on The Hawks Eye Podcast. The players who rested on Wednesday, Christian McCaffrey, Dre Greenlaw, and Trent Williams, were all upgraded to full participants during Thursday’s session. Edge rusher Khalid Kareem was also upgraded to a full participant after sitting out Wednesday with a shoulder injury. Kicker Eddy Pineiro did not practice for the second day in a row with an illness. The 49ers will likely give Pineiro as long as he needs to shake whatever is bothering him. If we see any news about the 49ers working out kickers over the next couple of days, that will not be a good sign for Pineiro’s availability for Sunday. The big news is rookie running back Kaelon Black, who was added to the injury report with a groin injury. Black had a limited designation. He joins George Kittle (Achilles), Keion White (back), Kyle Juszczyk (finger), and Nick Bosa (knee) on the limited list. It’s probably a good sign that we haven’t heard any reports yet about Black’s injury being anything serious. During a KNBR interview , Kyle Shanahan said, “I think we’re just being smart with him. He was a little tight today, so we didn’t push him too hard.”

title: How did the 49ers rookies fare in Week 1?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers got some unfortunate injury news regarding second-round pick De’Zhaun Stribling this week, as the rookie wideout will be out for close to 10 weeks after undergoing ankle surgery. Stribling had been poised for a key role in San Francisco’s offense, and that was reflected in his early playing time, as he […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers got some unfortunate injury news regarding second-round pick De’Zhaun Stribling this week, as the rookie wideout will be out for close to 10 weeks after undergoing ankle surgery. Stribling had been poised for a key role in San Francisco’s offense, and that was reflected in his early playing time, as he led the 49ers in snaps at wide receiver prior to his injury. He had been playing over Deebo Samuel in two-receiver sets, and was set for a big role following Ricky Pearsall’s injury in training camp. The 49ers drafted eight rookies back in the 2026 NFL Draft, with six of them seeing action in Week 1. While Stribling’s week was cut short, how did the rest of the group do? Romello Height played 30 snaps with San Francisco short-handed up front. He rushed the passer on 18 of them and ended without a pressure. Gracen Halton stepped into a big role as well, playing 31 snaps at defensive tackle, ranking second at the position only to Osa Odighizuwa. Kaelon Black got a big role, going for 65 yards on 14 carries, while seeing 28 snaps to Christian McCaffrey’s 36. While McCaffrey nearly doubled him in routes run, Black still ran 12 routes, while also being tasked with pass protection. Fifth-round pick Jaden Dugger saw a huge role in Week 1, playing 34 snaps as the 49ers No. 3 linebacker behind Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw. He was moved around a ton, playing 21 snaps in the box and 11 snaps on the line, according to PFF. Carver Willis only had a special teams role, while Ephesians Prysock and Enrique Cruz both did not play. What did Kyle Shanahan think about his rookies in Week 1? “I thought they all played well,” Shanahan said. “Especially losing Alfred [Collins] early in the week, losing Sam [Okuayinonu] early in the week, Gracen just coming back from a high ankle, so that was his first week of practice. James [Thompson] just coming back from a hamstring. He didn’t practice until that Friday, so he got a walk-through in before. “So, I was really impressed with the young guys on defense just being ready for the game. And same guys on offense. Just with Kaelon Black, I thought he did well. And Stribling, even though he didn’t get to play much, he was so prepared for the game. That was real impressive from all the rookies.” Dugger’s role was an interesting one, as the 49ers have praised his versatility and looked to get him a lot of snaps in the preseason. Shanahan was quite pleased with his performance. “Dugger I thought played real well,” Shanahan added. “We got him a lot of playing time during the training camp. A lot of playing time in all three of our preseason games. I thought this was his best game so far, so I was really impressed.” Meanwhile, Carver Willis didn’t play after the 49ers had yet to announce a left guard heading into last week. Shanahan said that Connor Colby’s body of work during the week made him the starter with no rotation at guard for Week 1.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: John Lynch: Christian McCaffrey will still have games as workhorse back
summary: One of the biggest takeaways from the San Francisco 49ers 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams last weekend was the split at running back. Rookie Kaelon Black ended up with four more carries than Christian McCaffrey, as he went for 65 yards on 14 carries, while McCaffrey had 10 rushes for 68 yards. Black, […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the biggest takeaways from the San Francisco 49ers 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams last weekend was the split at running back. Rookie Kaelon Black ended up with four more carries than Christian McCaffrey, as he went for 65 yards on 14 carries, while McCaffrey had 10 rushes for 68 yards. Black, who was a surprise pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, has impressed the coaching staff quite a bit this offseason, but it was still unclear how much of a split we’d see at running back, given how much McCaffrey has dominated the position’s snaps in recent years. Well, San Francisco went to Black early and often, keeping McCaffrey fresh while riding the hot hand as the run game flourished against Los Angeles. Was that the expectation, and will that continue to be the case? “I think, yes, we wanted to [rotate running backs], but you have to have the faith and the comfort, and it has to be earned,” general manager John Lynch said on KNBR on Thursday morning. “So, Kaelon, I think, through the way he performed in training camp, him being on his assignments, his ability to pass [protect earned him the right].” The big debate in recent years has been the value in taking McCaffrey off the field. While he’s racked up an exorbitant amount of touches, his value as a three-down back has made it hard for the 49ers to use a rotation. The 49ers still plan to have McCaffrey take on a workhorse load of touches in certain games. It just might not be as often with more viable backup options. “When you have options to split the carries, it’s hard to take Christian off the field,” Lynch added. “Christian doesn’t like coming off the field, but I think there’s a vision for how we want to do this, and you want to keep people healthy in a game, you want to keep people fresh for a season. “And so, I promise you, there’s going to be games where Christian’s right back to having the amount of touches he had last year. But it’s just the flow of the game, the way it went. Kaelon had a hot hand there. Christian ran it when he had his opportunities extremely well. The name of the game is to win, and running the football was a big part of that win, and we did it very well.” Head coach Kyle Shanahan chimed in as well, noting that Black’s body of work in the offseason has given the team the confidence to sub him in often. “More that he earned in training camp to be our number two back, so he was who we were going to go with and just how prepared he seemed throughout the week,” Shanahan said of Black. “I mean, there wasn’t a time that, all right, Christian got this rep, it’s a play for Christian, and his backup won’t know what to do. He showed during the week how attentive he was, how much he knew, how much he was studying whether he got to rep or not. “And when you do that, even though certain things you definitely want to keep Christian in on, that just makes it a lot easier for Bobby (Turner) to sub him. He doesn’t always know what play I’m going to call and stuff, and when you’re confident that the backup knows what he’s doing and can do it, it makes it easier on the position coaches.” The 49ers will likely rely on their run game a ton again in Week 2 when they face the Miami Dolphins at home. San Francisco enters the weekend as a near two-touchdown favorite, which means we could see a lot of Black once again.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Kyle Shanahan reveals rare trait that has helped 49ers rookie hit the ground running
summary: While De’Zhaun Stribling endured an unfortunate start to his NFL career as injury struck on his debut, Week 1 of the new campaign saw several promising signs from other members of the 49ers’ rookie class. Romello Height, Gracen Halton and Jaden Dugger all saw significant snaps and contributed to what was ultimately a strong defensive […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams with Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers on the field after the game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. The 49ers defeated the Rams 27-7. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images While De’Zhaun Stribling endured an unfortunate start to his NFL career as injury struck on his debut , Week 1 of the new campaign saw several promising signs from other members of the 49ers’ rookie class. Romello Height, Gracen Halton and Jaden Dugger all saw significant snaps and contributed to what was ultimately a strong defensive performance from San Francisco in the 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams. However, no rookie stood out more than third-round running back Kaelon Black, who surprisingly received more carries than longtime workhorse Christian McCaffrey and shone while doing so. Indeed, Black had 14 carries to McCaffrey’s 10 and put up 65 yards at an average of 4.6 yards per carry. Black’s success helped keep McCaffrey — who racked up 6.8 yards per rush — fresh as the 49ers produced an impressive and extremely efficient performance on the ground. While it is only one game, Black’s debut served as compelling evidence he can be consistently successful as a complementary back who can take the burden off McCaffrey. The 49ers have seen several young backs fail to live up to their draft status during Kyle Shanhan’s tenure but, asked about Black, San Francisco’s head coach pointed to an intangible as key to the former Oklahoma Sooner separating himself from those predecessors who were unable to impress. Speaking in Wednesday’s press conference, Shanahan was effusive in his praise of Black. Asked if the running back rotation worked out as he wanted, Shanahan said: “Yeah, it did work out. I was a little surprised at the end just that Kaelon got more [carries] than Christian. “That was just kind of how the game went. Has a lot to do with probably me starting out the game. I think I had like three runs in the first 17 plays, but love taking some off Christian and love the fact that Kaelon was prepared for everything, the run game and the pass game, and allowed us to be able to do that.” Going into more detail about what stood out about Black in comparison to rookie draft picks from previous years, Shanahan hailed his attention to detail, adding: “He earned in training camp to be our number two back, so he was who we were going to go with and just how prepared he seemed throughout the week. I mean, there wasn’t a time that, all right, Christian got this rep, it’s a play for Christian, and his backup won’t know what to do. He showed during the week how attentive he was, how much he knew, how much he was studying whether he got to rep or not. And when you do that, even though certain things you definitely want to keep Christian in on, that just makes it a lot easier for [running backs coach Robert Turner Jr.] Bobby to sub him. He doesn’t always know what play I’m going to call and stuff and when you’re confident that the backup knows what he’s doing and can do it, it makes it easier on the position coaches.” Pressed on whether that kind of attentiveness and focus is rare for a rookie back, Shanahan replied: “I’d like to say it’s what I expect, but it’s not always what you get. But, that’s how he was advertised coming out of college. “I do think he’s rare in terms of his maturity and just how much of a pro he’s seemed like since day one.” It was a very revealing answer from Shanahan, one that suggests they significantly misjudged the readiness of previous draft picks at the position. Of course, rare maturity is no guarantee of sustained production, but the early signs throughout camp, preseason and now through Week 1 have been very promising. The 49er backfield will be set up well for the long term if Black maintains his early momentum.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley shares his lasting impression when he left the 49ers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Shanahan will face an old friend in Week 2. Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley coached on the same staff as Kyle Shanahan with the Cleveland Browns for a season in 2014. Hafley worked with the 49ers from 2016 and stayed on through a regime change when Shanahan was […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins looks on against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Shanahan will face an old friend in Week 2. Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley coached on the same staff as Kyle Shanahan with the Cleveland Browns for a season in 2014. Hafley worked with the 49ers from 2016 and stayed on through a regime change when Shanahan was hired, serving as the Niners’ defensive backs coach through 2018. It’s been quite the journey for Hafley since he left the Bay Area. He’s had stops at Ohio State, Boston College, and the Packers before being hired as the Dolphins’ head coach this past offseason. Hafley couldn’t speak highly enough about what he learned from Shanahan, John Lynch, and the 49ers: The biggest lasting impression for me, as a younger coach when I left the Niners: John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan, coming in together, being aligned. It kind of, sent a message to me. If I ever get a chance to do this, I want it to be like that. I want it to be somebody that I’m aligned with. When I came in and John Lynch, obviously one of the best football players, Hall of Fame player, but you wanna talk about a good guy, he’s one of the best human beings of all-time. Combine that with Kyle, I think it’s such a great fit. Remember, we were 0-9. Kyle’s first season I’m there, we started off 0-9. We won a bunch of games. The next year, I think we won four or five games. The next year, they went to the Super Bowl. So he had a process. Kyle’s a huge influence on me. I truly believe he’s one of the reasons I’m here right now. Great coach, great friend. But I’ve learned so much from him. And seeing him stick to the process and hold people to a standard during two really hard years, and building it the right way, and not flinching. And him and John just being like this. I think that has stuck with me. And look at us know. I’m not saying we’re going to start that way, but Sully [Dolphins general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan] and I together, trying to build this thing the right way, Kyle kind of gave me the blueprint for that. This season probably feels a lot like 2017 for Hafley. The Dolphins were projected to be among the worst teams in the NFL. They’re going to play a lot of inexperienced players. Miami had 436 snaps played by rookies in Week 1, the most of any team, per the AP’s Josh Dubow. Three of the Dolphins’ top four wide receivers are rookies. Their left guard, Kadyn Proctor, is a rookie. Hafley starts three rookies on his defense. There will be growing pains, but the Dolphins are building a foundation. They will not be an easy out for San Francisco this week.

title: 49ers’ RB Christian McCaffrey can surpass a Jerry Rice milestone Sunday
summary: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is well on his way to being fitted for a gold jacket. He can inch one step closer as early as this Sunday by surpassing a pair of all-time greats in the record books. McCaffrey has 98 scrimmage touchdowns (62 rushing, 36 receiving) in 113 career games. This […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 09: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs against Quentin Lake #37 of the Los Angeles Rams in the second quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is well on his way to being fitted for a gold jacket. He can inch one step closer as early as this Sunday by surpassing a pair of all-time greats in the record books. McCaffrey has 98 scrimmage touchdowns (62 rushing, 36 receiving) in 113 career games. This Sunday, against the Miami Dolphins, McCaffrey can surpass none other than Jerry Rice (115 games) as the fourth-fastest player to reach 100 scrimmage touchdowns in the Super Bowl era. The only players to reach this mark in fewer games are a pair of Hall of Famers, LaDainian Tomlinson (89 games) and Emmitt Smith (93 games), as well as Shaun Alexander (96 games). That’s not the only record McCaffrey can break in Week 2. Additionally, McCaffrey can surpass Marshal Faulk (36 touchdown receptions) for the most touchdown receptions by a running back in the Super Bowl era. McCaffrey failed to reach the end zone in Week 1, but the matchup is appetizing for him against the Dolphins come Sunday. Second-year back Ashton Jeanty had two touchdown receptions through the air last week against Miami. Jeanty combined for 147 yards from scrimmage on 29 touches. If Week 1 is any indication, McCaffrey won’t have that kind of volume, but he shouldn’t need it to score twice.

title: Titans need way more from John Franklin-Myers in Week 2
summary: Several new Tennessee Titans players failed to meet expectations in Sunday’s Week 1 loss to the New York Jets. One of the glaring ones was defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers. The Titans need Franklin-Myers to be way better versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. The Titans signed Franklin-Myers to a three-year, $63 million contract in […]
full_text: Aug 4, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers (91) goes through drills during training camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Several new Tennessee Titans players failed to meet expectations in Sunday’s Week 1 loss to the New York Jets . One of the glaring ones was defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers. The Titans need Franklin-Myers to be way better versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2 . The Titans signed Franklin-Myers to a three-year, $63 million contract in free agency. That’s a hefty deal to play next to Jeffery Simmons. Franklin-Myers was brought in for his experience in Robert Saleh’s system, having played under him with the Jets. Remember that Franklin-Myers missed a huge portion of training camp with stiffness and soreness. The former Stephen F. Austin standout did not play a single snap in the preseason. Franklin-Myers got the veteran rest treatment, but it clearly had a negative impact on his Week 1 performance. Franklin-Myers recorded just three tackles and one quarterback pressure against the Jets. Pro Football Focus slapped him with an overall defensive grade of 52.7. His PFF pass-rushing grade was a 52.8, and run-stopping score wasn’t much better (55.4). Franklin-Myers was totally ineffective. The Eagles are dealing with an injury on the offensive line. They’ll be without starting left guard Landon Dickerson, who is a Pro Bowl-caliber interior blocker. The expectation is that sophomore backup Drew Kendall will replace him. Both Simmons and Franklin-Myers need to take advantage of that matchup. The Titans paid Franklin-Myers very handsomely to be a dominant force on the defensive line. His impact was totally muted by an underrated Jets offensive line in Week 1. Nonetheless, Coach Saleh’s defensive line was very disappointing. Franklin-Myers needs to help lead the charge towards improvement. The Titans have had way too many big-money flops lately. They certainly can’t afford another. It’s obviously far too early to panic. Franklin-Myers is known as a consistent defensive lineman. Hopefully Franklin-Myers will perform like his usual self soon.

The key takeaways from that 24-22 Week 1 loss to Philadelphia , as expressed by head coach Dan Quinn and many others: Get the defensive explosive plays allowed OFF the game tape. Find an earlier (and consistent) offensive rhythm Those lessons must be applied in general, but there are game specific issues to attend to in Dallas. How should the Commanders solve them? We’ll let you assess that in this week’s Reverse Q+A (working title), where we’ll drop five questions to be answered in the comments. The best responses will be moved into the article itself late by Friday morning. Question 1: Quarterback Jayden Daniels took some time to get revved up but finished strong down the stretch vs. Philly, as he’s known to do. Could this be a launching point against Dallas’ defense? Does Daniels need to dominate to leave Dallas with a win? Question 2: There are some obvious matchups Washington should be wary of on Sunday (Lamb/Pickens vs. WAS secondary). What’s a matchup in the Commanders’ favor they can exploit? Question 3: What should be done with Mike Sainristil? He has received appropriate criticism for his role in a costly explosive and a touchdown vs. Philly. He went so far as to say he had a “lack of effort” on those plays. The Commanders seem outwardly committed to him as a significant contributor. Do you work with him believing he’ll be better vs. Dallas for the humbling Philly experience, or do you go with another player(s)? In his roles outside and in the slot? Question 4: Rookie WR Antonio Williams had an excellent debut , with four receptions for 64 yards and a key touchdown on 10 routes run. What are your expectations for him in Week 2 against Dallas’ defense? Question 5: This one is a probably a bit unfair considering only one game has been played – with both guys playing well – but we’ll ask it anyway…is there any part of you wishing Washington would’ve drafted Caleb Downs over Sonny Styles?

Young defensive lineman Ricky Barber was released in a corresponding move. We have made the following roster moves: – Released DT Ricky Barber – Signed CB Isaac Yiadom from the practice squad pic.twitter.com/7ixuwCfVcv — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 17, 2026 The Commanders signed Yiadom to the practice squad on Sept. 1, after being released by the New Orleans Saints. He was a third-round draft pick out of Boston College back in 2018 and is entering his ninth NFL season. He has 34 starts in 118 NFL games and 230 tackles, three forced fumbles and three interceptions to his credit . Yiadom adds experienced depth to the cornerbacks corps and special teams. It’s uncertain why he wasn’t considered a practice squad elevation if needed, unless it was a move to keep another team from poaching him off Washington’s practice squad. It’s also possible that Barber ends up taking the open practice squad spot if he clears waivers, though time will tell on that front. Barber had a strong training camp and preseason, though he was inactive for the Week 1 loss to Philadelphia.

Here are five key factors for the Commanders on Sunday: The offensive line needs to improve The O-line stood out as a concern during camp because of many of the issues that showed up against the Eagles. For starters, the Commanders couldn’t get the run game going as they recorded just 4.1 yards per carry. Quinn said he thought they “left some meat on the bone” in the run game, and noted that made it easier for Philadelphia to sit back in two-high safety coverages. Although Daniels’s tendency to hold on to the ball didn’t make life easier in pass protection, the offensive line also just got beat on a lot of the Eagles’ pressures. Philadelphia pressured Daniels on 50 percent of his dropbacks. That’s obviously not good enough. Center Nick Allegretti had a challenging game. His biggest miscue was a whiffed block that doomed the Commanders’ two-point conversion attempt that would have tied the game late. His snaps were fine, but his blocking wasn’t up to par. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Pro Football Plus: Nick Allegretti talked about communication, sticking on the 2nd level blocks, lot of good from last week, but also improving on things that need to be better. pic.twitter.com/PHSx5xgBCx — Donna Hopkins (@DonnaHopkins_) September 17, 2026 Riggo’s Rag Lucas Patrick signing confirms Commanders fans were right to fear the worst [T]he Commanders are reportedly signing versatile interior offensive lineman Lucas Patrick to their 53-man roster . This is the clearest sign yet of dissatisfaction with how things unfolded at Lincoln Financial Field . Patrick has experience at all three interior offensive line positions. He suited up six times for the Cincinnati Bengals last season and started one game. While his production wouldn’t be classed as elite by any stretch, the Commanders are clearly desperate enough to give him a shot. If nothing else, Patrick becomes a better depth option. The Commanders don’t have much of that, so they had to do something. Allegretti was awful in Philadelphia, looking shaky, unsure of his responsibilities, and blowing assignments in crucial moments. With only sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin behind him, his job is now legitimately in jeopardy. Patrick can pile on the pressure. But the big question centers on whether his knee can hold up. The New York Giants cut Patrick before the season, but the reports were positive. His knee issue did flare up again , so it’ll be interesting to see how much he can do right away in Washington. He struggled early as a rookie before improving in the second half of his debut season, and that progress continued against the Eagles, with Conerly earning a 78.4 PFF pass-blocking grade. Right guard Sam Cosmi impressed again, allowing a pressure rate of just 2.4%. title: NFL Week 2 picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
summary: Minnesota vs. Chicago? Trevor Lawrence vs. Bo Nix? There are more games left in Week 2, and we have picks, predictions, key stats, watchability ratings and more.
full_text:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season is here! There are a lot of tough division matchups happening: the Vikings visiting the Bears, the Panthers and Falcons facing off, the Raiders against the Chargers and the Seahawks versus the Cardinals. You can also expect an exciting quarterback duel between Jacksonville's  Trevor Lawrence and Denver's  Bo Nix . 

 We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, NFL analyst Ben Solak gives one reason to tune in to each game (and rates the watchability of the matchup), fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder give us final score picks for every game.

 Let's get into the full Week 2 slate, which culminates with a "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Giants and Rams on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

 
 Jump to a matchup: 
 MIN-CHI | CIN-HOU | NO-BAL 
 PIT-NE | GB-NYJ | PHI-TEN 
 CAR-ATL | CLE-TB | JAX-DEN 
 LV-LAC | WSH-DAL | SEA-ARI 
 MIA-SF | IND-KC | NYG-LAR 

 
 

 What ESPN Analytics says ... 
 

 

 
 

 Vikings (1-0) at Bears (1-0) 
 1 p.m. ET | Fox | CHI -4.5 (47.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Vikings: DC Brian Flores posted an 83% blitz rate in the first half against the Packers and -- even after throttling down in the second half -- finished with a 71.7% rate that nearly tripled the NFL average in Week 1. Flores has always favored the blitz, but would he dare repeat that aggression level against the Bears? Flores considers the opening weeks of a season to be about improvement and experimentation. "What are the best groups of players who are out on the field? Who plays well with who?" he said. "That's what we're working through as a staff right now." -- Kevin Seifert 

 What we're hearing on the Bears: Chicago is preparing for the "King of the Cover-0 blitz," the nickname QB Caleb Williams gave Flores as a rookie. In 2025, Williams was blitzed 37.2% in his first meeting against Minnesota and 66.7% the second time. Trying to anticipate which strategy Flores will deploy is an ineffective plan. "You try to have answers for everything," coach Ben Johnson said. "He's been in this division three years now, and yeah, I mean you'd like to think he's put everything he could possibly do on tape until you play him next and you realize he hasn't yet. ... There always is with him and that's what makes him such a good coordinator." -- Courtney Cronin 

 

 Stat to know: The Bears need 37 points to break the NFL record for most points in a team's opening two games, currently held by the 1968 Raiders (95). -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: Vikings QB Carson Wentz will throw multiple interceptions. I know he had some impressive moments and didn't throw any picks in Minnesota's Week 1 win. But this is still Wentz, and I assume he's still prone to a mistake or four. -- Walder 

 Viewers rating (out of 10): 9.0. There isn't a more fun schematic matchup in the entire league than Johnson versus Flores. This is Round 7 of their showdown. With a bad Bears defense on the other side of the ball, there should be explosive plays everywhere. -- Solak 

 Injuries: Vikings | Bears 

 Fantasy nugget: Bears WR Luther Burden III finished with just five targets and 9.5 fantasy points against Carolina last week. However, he led Chicago's receivers in routes run and now faces a Vikings secondary that allowed the Packers' Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to combine for 48.2 fantasy points last week. Burden is in a good spot to bounce back. See Week 2 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: All five of Wentz's starts went over the total last season for the Vikings. Chicago just scored 59 points but also allowed Carolina to produce 478 yards and 37 points. Minnesota's defense now faces an explosive Bears offense, while Wentz and WR  Justin Jefferson get a vulnerable Chicago defense. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Bears 31, Vikings 24 
 Moody's pick: Bears 35, Vikings 26 
 Walder's pick: Bears 34, Vikings 17 
 FPI prediction: CHI, 65.6% (by an average of 4.5 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: Mason put on IR after having surgery on thumb ... Bears anticipate 'great challenge' vs. Vikings defense  ... No block, no rock' is not just a mantra for Bears' offense 

 
 

 Bengals (1-0) at Texans (0-1) 
 1 p.m. ET | CBS | HOU -2.5 (46.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Bengals:  QB Joe Burrow will be managing back tightness this week. And he'll be doing so against one of the NFL's best defenses. OC Dan Pitcher compared the combination of edge rushers Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr . to Cincinnati's WR tandem of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Keeping Burrow upright and intact this week will be paramount for Cincinnati's chances against Houston and for the rest of the season. -- Ben Baby 

 What we're hearing on the Texans: Houston is staring at another potential 0-2 start. If the Texans lose this week, it'll be the third such time under coach DeMeco Ryans since he was hired in 2023. But Hunter said "last year is last year," in response to being asked about their confidence level to dig themselves out of a hole to start the season. Houston may have to play without Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins ( hamstring ), who was injured in practice Wednesday. -- DJ Bien-Aime 

 Stat to know: The Bengals posted a 54% pass rush win rate in Week 1, the team's highest since November 2024. They had the worst pass rush win rate in the NFL last season (28.8%). -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: Texans RB David Montgomery will average 5.0 yards per carry. Montgomery scored three touchdowns in his debut but only averaged 3.0 yards per carry. The Bengals' defense, for all its turnover success in Week 1, did allow .09 EPA per opponent carry in Week 1 -- the fifth-worst mark. -- Walder 

 Viewers rating (out of 10): 8.8. There are high stakes in this one for the traveling Texans, who are trying to avoid 0-2 (against two AFC contenders!). This is one I'm going to keep a close eye on especially because Burrow and Collins are entering the week banged up. -- Solak 

 

 Injuries: Bengals | Texans 

 Fantasy nugget: Montgomery finished Week 1 with 23 touches and 28.9 fantasy points, while handling every Houston rushing attempt inside the red zone. He now faces a Bengals defense that ranked 21st in run stop win rate (25.8%) last week and allowed the Bucs' Bucky Irving to score 20.3 fantasy points. See Week 2 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: The Texans are 1-8 ATS (against the spread) in September under Ryans for the past three seasons, and their September struggles could continue against an offense built to attack Houston's Week 1 weakness. The Bills averaged 10.4 yards per pass against the Texans, and they now get Burrow, Chase and Higgins. If Cincinnati protects Burrow, it has enough offense to contend. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Bengals 27, Texans 24 
 Moody's pick: Bengals 24, Texans 21 
 Walder's pick: Texans 23, Bengals 20

 What we're hearing on the Saints: The Saints will be without long-snapper Zach Wood for several weeks because of a calf strain , according to a source. This is a very underrated loss for New Orleans, which hasn't had to deal with this problem for the 10 seasons Wood has…

title: Cards' Marvin Harrison Jr. looking for big rebound game vs. Seahawks
summary: Harrison was held to just one catch in the win over the Chargers, but most single coverage may result in bigger numbers.
full_text:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Marvin Harrison Jr . had a feeling Sunday would play out the way it did.

 During Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh's time at Michigan, Harrison, then at Ohio State, rarely saw single coverage against the Wolverines. Harrison figured, if they still had the same kind of respect for him in the NFL, then the defensive play against him would be similar.

 He was right.

 Harrison saw single coverage on about seven of 32 snaps and finished with just one catch on three targets for 33 yards. But it was an impressive over-the-shoulder catch, and the Cardinals won 26-14.

 "Then we did throw the go-ball and completed that one," Harrison said. "So, it was just like you're not going to get many of the opportunities, but when you do, obviously we capitalized on the one we had, but it's a part of the game.

 "Everybody's going to have their weeks, have their days, and, at the end of the day, the team won and all you can do is your part."

 Quarterback Jacoby Brissett isn't worried.

 "I don't want to get into the whole overreaction of Week 1 because he had one catch or something like that," Brissett said. "It's a long season. He did a lot of things. He got a lot of attention in the game. I think that speaks more to him. People may say, 'Oh, he didn't have a lot of catches,' but it's a reason why he's double-covered, and he's got a safety over top of him and playing him so heavy at the line of scrimmage because they understand the one time that they don't, you see what happens.

 "I think obviously it's finding different ways to give him the ball, but if he's attracting that amount of attention, I think Marv understands, 'Hey, I've got to help my brothers out and my teammate out and get them open.' I thought he did a good job with that."

 Harrison understands who's next on the schedule.

 He hasn't beat the Seattle Seahawks in any of his four previous meetings against them and while Arizona's nine-game losing streak against Seattle, as an organization, hasn't been a major topic in meetings and around the locker room, it certainly has been a point of emphasis, Harrison said. And he's not the only one who's craving a win over the defending Super Bowl champions.

 Tight end Trey McBride is 0-8 against them and wide receiver Michael Wilson is 0-6.

 

 "It's, like, we need to win here soon," Harrison said. "Sooner or later, for sure."

 How Seattle will defend Harrison will largely be dictated on McBride, who scorched the Seahawks for nine catches for 137 yards and a touchdown in their second meeting last season. If Seattle commits enough resources to McBride, Harrison could find himself in more single coverage situations than he did in Los Angeles. Of 33 routes, according to ESPN Research, Harrison was single covered on roughly seven of them. Most of the time, the Chargers kept a safety high on his side or shaded a safety toward him.

 Seattle didn't give up more than 51 receiving yards to any single Patriots receiver in Week 1 but pressed more, by a percentage, than the Chargers pressed the Cardinals. That could bode well for Harrison, whom Brissett considers a threat anytime only one defender is on him.

 "It's part of it," Harrison. "It's going to be different each week."

title: Bryce Young's 4-1 record vs. Falcons a harbinger for Week 2?
summary: The Panthers QB's previous trips to Mercedes-Benz Stadium should keep Falcons fans and coaches up at night.
full_text:
During the third quarter of a back-and-forth divisional donnybrook to end the 2024 season, the Carolina Panthers trailed the Atlanta Falcons by one point, roughly four minutes into the second half.

 It was fourth-and-1 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

 Bryce Young lined up under center and took a snap before faking a handoff to running back Miles Sanders . With tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders darting to the right behind the line of scrimmage to pick up a defender for a lead block, Young sprinted behind him on a bootleg. The quarterback then set his feet midway through his jaunt and fired a dart over the middle to tight end Tommy Tremble in the end zone.

 Before the ball even reached the wide-open Tremble's hands, Young turned around and threw up a touchdown signal as a way of celebrating the 12-yard heave for a go-ahead score. The oft soft-spoken signal-caller showed off his understated bravado with the early commemoration of the touchdown connection.

 

 "It was the coolest thing ever," Tremble said about Young's signature throw of 2024. "That play is one of my favorites. Like, it's fun to see, and that's when I feel like Bryce Young really, like, activated and everyone else could see the kind of player he was."

 

 The Panthers won the 2024 season finale against the Falcons on the road, 44-38, in overtime, as Young produced a career-high five total touchdowns -- three with his arm and two with his legs -- nearly four months after he was benched in Week 3 of his second campaign. The shot of Young's pre-completion celebration spread throughout the 2025 offseason and served as a beacon of hope for fans of the much-maligned passer.

 "He was the best dude on the field," Panthers right guard Rob Hunt said. "That was cool. ... It was a good moment for him, for sure -- confidence builder. ...That was good going into the next season."

 And while Young did improve throughout his 2025 season, it was again his bout against the Falcons on the road last season that turned heads. In his Atlanta-based follow-up to the 2024 clash, Young threw for a franchise-record 448 yards -- surpassing Cam Newton's previous mark of 432 yards in 2011 -- and three touchdowns in a 30-27 overtime win against the Falcons.

 While the Panthers head back to Atlanta on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) with an identical 0-1 record to the Falcons, Young's previous two trips to Mercedes-Benz Stadium should keep Falcons fans and coaches up at night. And considering the Panthers' defense gave up 59 points and 552 yards to the Chicago Bears last week, Young -- who led six scoring drives in Week 1 -- might need to be the difference-maker again on Sunday.

 "Coach [ Dave Canales ] talks about it all the time: Our first goal is to win the [NFC] South," Young said Wednesday. "And obviously, those division wins mean so much, when you're trying to accomplish that goal. You have the same process and you understand that. You don't want to get too high or too low, but again, this is a business, we're all pros and we understand what's at stake every time that it's a division opponent."

 Let's look closer at how Young has gone above and beyond inside the dome that sits in the heart of Atlanta and get a feel for what the 25-year-old could do for an encore.

 

 Young's performances in Atlanta 
 Despite losing his NFL debut in Atlanta in the season opener against the Falcons in 2023, Young's numbers against his familiar foes run counter to his overall career stat line.

 Young had a 16.4 total quarterback rating in his debut loss against the Falcons, but he has since won four consecutive starts against Atlanta, raising his QBR against the rival NFC South franchise to 67.4, which is more than 20 points higher than his career number of 43.9.

 

 Young is 4-1 in his starts against the Falcons and 10-30 as a starter against everyone else. His 66.7% completion percentage against Atlanta is five percentage points higher than his career average (61.4%). In five games, Young has thrown for 1,133 passing yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. He is throwing 3.5 touchdowns for every interception against Atlanta; he averages 1.7 touchdowns per interception against the entire league.

 The QB has also scored a third of his career rushing touchdowns against the Falcons, as three of his nine QB-keeper TDs have come against Atlanta.

 "I feel like every single time he goes to Atlanta, he just makes the plays," Tremble said. "And him breaking Cam Newton's passing record that game [in 2025] -- it was sick to see. It was fun to be a part of that. So, I'm excited to see him, hopefully, even top that game from last time."

 And while his numbers are comparatively modest at home in Charlotte (288 total passing yards, 17 rushing total yards and a rushing touchdown in two games) against the Falcons, his last two road trips to Atlanta featured 699 total passing yards, 23 total rushing yards and eight total touchdowns to go with a pair of overtime victories in thrilling shootouts.

 It's also worth noting, Young's success at Mercedes-Benz Stadium predates his NFL career. He threw for 765 total yards and seven total touchdowns in two blowout wins in Atlanta during his tenure as the Alabama Crimson Tide's starting QB. During one of those outings, he also ran for 40 yards and a touchdown on three carries -- to go along with 421 passing yards and three passing touchdowns -- against Georgia in the 2021 SEC championship game.

 
 Young's outlook against Falcons in Week 2 
 Young's fourth Week 1 appearance went much better than his previous three opening-week outings for Carolina. He finished the 59-37 loss to the Bears with 361 passing yards, four total touchdowns (including a rushing score) and an interception. He had a 66.4 QBR, nearly identical to his overall success against Atlanta.

 "He's off to a hot start right now, we've just got to keep it rolling," Tremble said.

 According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Young threw for a career-high 221 yards on deep throws against Chicago, completing 64.3% of his downfield heaves. He was particularly effective against zone coverage, throwing for 289 yards compared to 72 yards against man coverage.

 Against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, the Falcons ran zone coverage on nearly 40% of their defensive snaps. Atlanta favored man coverage at nearly 60% against Pittsburgh.

 

 Young will need to be much more efficient against man coverage than he was against the Bears, who primarily used zone coverage against Carolina in Week 1.

 Still, Young faced coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's scheme twice last season, and while the quarterback had a modest stat line in their initial meeting in Charlotte (121 passing yards, eight rushing yards and a rushing touchdown with 66.7% completion percentage), he exploded to boast career-high passing numbers in the second go-around in Atlanta in 2025.

 Nothing should be particularly foreign to Young about Ulbrich's attack, even with coach Kevin Stefanski now overseeing the team.

 "Very matchy group, guys that -- especially on the perimeter -- they play really well," Young said about the man coverage-heavy scheme. "Understand concepts, do a great job of pattern matching, all that stuff, so we know it's going to take everything. We have to be executing at a high level to have success."

 

 Biggest X factor for Young in Atlanta? 
 The Panthers' offensive line needs to keep Young upright Sunday. Against Chicago, Young was pressured on 11 of his 41 dropbacks, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also took two sacks.

 Carolina will go up against new faces on the Falcons front, too. With defensive ends James Pearce Jr . (suspension) and Jalon Walker (injured reserve) unavailable, Atlanta will count on veterans Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam to bring the pressure, along with newly acquired defensive tackles Maason Smith and Gervon Dexter Sr . title: NFL Week 2 betting guide: Top plays for Sunday afternoon's games
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 2 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

 Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league.

 From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 1.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's Game of the Week  | Solak's plays  | Walder's props 

 

 

 Bowen's Game of the Week 

 Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans (-2.5, 46.5) 
1 p.m. ET on CBS, Reliant Stadium, Houston

 

 This line has fluctuated but at -2.5, I am all-in. Would I feel the same at -3? I wouldn't love it, but I'd be willing to bet Houston at home in a bounce-back game after the Week 1 loss to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills . Let's get into what to look for on both sides of the ball, and we'll finish with some props bets to play.

 

 When Houston has the ball: Houston spent the offseason working on its run game, trading for David Montgomery and adding to the offensive front. And we saw a dedicated effort to run the football in Week 1, as Montgomery had 20 carries, with Woody Marks chipping in with nine. Now, was it super efficient? No. Montgomery averaged just 3.0 YPC, and the Texans registered a run block win rate of 74% (17th in the league). But it's clear that Houston wants the run game to be a foundational element of its offense. This can boost the passing opportunities for quarterback C.J. Stroud , who will see a Bengals defense featuring a rebuilt front anchored by defensive tackle  Dexter Lawrence II and an underrated secondary that can mix both zone and man looks. I would look for play-action concepts (which mirror the run game) to attack the Bengals' two-deep zone shells (in-breakers to Nico Collins , if he plays ) while also scheming up some shot plays. I truly think Houston looks to control the tempo on offense in this one, but let's keep an eye on third downs because the Texans need to beat man coverage from the Bengals there.

 When Cincinnati has the ball: I want to see this matchup against the Texans' defense. Though the Bengals looked flat in a Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ( Joe Burrow finished with 254 yards passing, and Ja'Marr Chase had two receptions for 12 yards), they create conflict because of scheme and talent. The Texans have been a zone-heavy defense under DeMeco Ryans, but they will mix in man coverage (based on game situations), which creates must-see TV when corners Derek Stingley Jr . and Kamari Lassiter match against Chase and Tee Higgins . Tight end Mike Gesicki (78 yards receiving in Week 1) could find room to operate against Houston's split-safety and single-high zone schemes to attack the voids there. But, my main question is will the Bengals' offensive line keep the pocket firm for Burrow and generate movement up front in the run game? The Bengals held a pass block win rate of 53.8% in Week 1 against the Bucs (13th in the league), while Chase Brown averaged only 3.5 YPC. It's a different matchup this week against Houston edge rushers Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter . Burrow will need to hit some explosive play throws to win this one.

 Leans: Texans -2.5 (-118), Texans moneyline (-142), Over 46.5 (-105)

 Now, let's get to some prop bets ...

 Ja'Marr Chase receptions OVER 6.5 (-109) 

 I expect a dedicated effort to get Chase the ball after he caught only two of four targets in the Week 1 win over the Bucs -- screens, unders and quicks that cater to Chase's explosive catch-and-run ability. Look for Chase to be involved early in this game plan.

 Mike Gesicki anytime TD (+280) 

 Gesicki caught a Week 1 touchdown on a schemed throw to beat man coverage. Plus, the Bengals can set up Gesicki on zone beaters in the high red zone (seams, corners) to counter the Houston defensive tendencies.

 

 
 Solak's plays 
 

 Green Bay Packers -3.5 (-112) at New York Jets 

 I'm grabbing a quick buy-low spot on the Packers, who were much better Sunday than the box score would indicate. The Minnesota Vikings scored 14 late points on defensive takeaways deep in Green Bay territory in their 39-22 victory. But the Packers had a better success rate (38.8%) than the Vikings (34.5%) and struggled only in situational spots. They were 3-for-12 on third down. On four red zone trips, they scored only one touchdown and one field goal. Those are the little execution problems that hurt a box score.

 

 Going from facing a Brian Flores-coached Vikings defense to the Jets should make things far easier. Matt LaFleur has experience facing Aaron Glenn from when Glenn was the defensive coordinator of the Detroit Lions and generally has found success (46% offensive success rate, 0.04 EPA per play, 2.2 points per drive).

 I thought about taking the Packers' team total, currently priced at 23.5 and juiced -135 to the over. I think the Jets' offense will be a functional group this season, but they need to run the ball and play clock control to win games against superior opponents -- and that might limit the Packers' total drives. As such, I'll go instead for the full-game spread at -3.5. I would play this no further than -120.

 Tennessee Titans team total UNDER 15.5 (-105) 

 The Titans' offensive operation was the worst I saw in Week 1: play designs that were dead in the water, offensive linemen uncertain of their assignments, easy drops and bad routes from receivers and poor accuracy and timing from Cam Ward at quarterback. It's tough to find anything to hang their hat on from a 23-10 loss to the Jets.

 

 It's worth remarking that Brian Daboll's offenses have been poor in Week 1 -- six, six and and zero points in the three seasons previous -- and then stronger in Week 2. But against this Philadelphia Eagles  defense, it's tough to have much faith. Philadelphia's defensive front looked as deep and disruptive as ever against an average Washington Commanders front, and the Titans are comfortably one of the eight worst lines in football. Though defensive back Cooper DeJean was banged up in the Week 1 game and sat out practice Wednesday, the Eagles' outside corner duo of Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen still poses a huge problem for the Titans' ability to create explosive plays through the air.

 The talent difference here feels simply insurmountable. The Titans will need defensive takeaways or big special teams outputs to get into scoring range. I don't see them getting enough. I would play this up to -115.

 New England Patriots -5.5 (-105) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers 

 The past four defenses the Patriots have faced are as follows: Seattle Seahawks (Week 1), Seahawks (Super Bowl), Denver Broncos (AFC Championship Game), Houston Texans (AFC divisional round). Even their wild-card opponent had a near-elite defense ( Los Angeles Chargers ). We are finally at a point at which we can buy low on the Patriots against an imperfect defense.

 The  Pittsburgh Steelers ' defense was hardly tested in Week 1 against the Cooper Rush -led Atlanta Falcons . Drake Maye and the Patriots' offense -- especially with TreVeyon Henderson returning from a right ankle injury -- represent a far stiffer test. Even though wide receiver  A.J. Brown is on injured reserve because of an ankle injury, the Patriots have had a long week since last Wednesday to prepare for his absence. title: Ravens looking for Bateman to step up if Flowers can't play
summary: The Ravens are looking for Bateman to step up after injuries hit the Ravens' wide receivers early in Sunday's win.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman can break one of the least productive stretches of his career by capitalizing on a big opportunity Sunday. 
 
 If Zay Flowers is unable to play due to a hamstring injury, Bateman becomes the wide receiver with the most familiarity with quarterback Lamar Jackson when Baltimore hosts the New Orleans Saints (1 p.m. ET, CBS). Bateman is looking to break out of a rut in which he has gone seven games without recording over 50 yards receiving. 
 
 "Our relationship is a great relationship, man," Jackson said. "My guy is actually going to get a lot more targets, I believe, with guys going down just because our offense is so explosive." 
 
 Bateman's chance to become a bigger part of the offense comes at an uncertain time. He is still waiting on the NFL to finalize its investigation on his June arrest on family violence charges . 
 
 Bateman declined to comment on the matter, saying it's a legal situation. He is subject to discipline under the NFL's personal conduct policy, and the baseline suspension for violations involving family violence is six games. 
 
 
 
 "Whatever the consequences are, I'll deal with it," Bateman said earlier this month. "But we're still waiting on the league and front office to let us know what's up." 
 
 The Ravens are looking for Bateman to step up after injuries hit the Ravens' wide receivers early in Sunday's 41-23 season-opening win at the Colts, when Flowers and rookie third-round pick  Ja'Kobi Lane  were hurt in the first half and didn't return. Lane was placed on injured reserve after having wrist surgery, and Flowers is day to day after not practicing Wednesday and Thursday. 
 
 Flowers is among the players Baltimore can least afford to lose. Since the start of the 2025 season, Flowers has accounted for over 60% of the Baltimore wide receivers' receptions and receiving yards. 
 
 Over the last 18 games, Flowers has 91 catches for 1,361 yards. During that same stretch, the other Ravens wide receivers have combined for 55 receptions for 814 yards. 
 
 "We all have Zay's back," Bateman said. 
 
 A first-round pick in 2021, Bateman had a breakthrough season in 2024, when he recorded 756 yards receiving and nine touchdowns. He then followed it up with his worst season, totaling a career-low 224 yards receiving. 
 
 On Sunday, Bateman didn't have a catch for the fourth time in his last 10 games. 
 
 "I cannot be worrying about my stats," Bateman said. "I need to be worried about how we can win a Super Bowl. And at the end of the day, no matter if I have zero yards or 100 yards, we finished with a 'W' at the end of the day, I slept good at night because we won rather than lost a game and I had 150 yards." 
 
 Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle explained that he was trying to get the ball to Bateman on the first play of the game. On Jackson's bootleg to his left, it was anticipated that Jackson would hit Bateman, who was running an underneath route. But Flowers got open deep for a 49-yard completion. 
 
 "He has certainly earned trust with myself [and] the rest of the staff," Doyle said of Bateman. "He has been great, and we have enjoyed being around him. It has been fun to watch the seriousness of his preparation and what he brings to that room from a leadership standpoint." 
 
 Ravens coach Jesse Minter praised Bateman for his blocking, which keyed Derrick Henry 's 32-yard touchdown run. Minter doesn't believe anyone should read too much into Bateman not having a catch Sunday. 
 
 "A lot of [the] time, maybe the play didn't go to him or whatever," Minter said. "But he is blocking downfield, and he is being unselfish. I think the offense will show over time that it could be anybody's big day on any day. So, I am excited about how he played, and I think there are big days ahead for 'Bate.'"
